## Asset references in JSON (wired before runtime)

| Where | Key | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `SpriteRenderer`, `Image`, `ParticleSystem2D` | `textureAsset` | texture GUID string (+ optional `spriteName`) |
| `AudioSource` | `clipAsset` | audio GUID string |
| `TextRenderer` | `fontAsset` | font GUID — **must be a string** |
| UI widget sprite states | `normalSprite`, `hoveredSprite`, … | texture GUID string |
| Prefab instance | `PrefabGUID` | prefab GUID string |
| Script field `Texture` / `Audio` / `Scene` | `ScriptFields` `value` | GUID string |
| Script field `Entity` (prefab) | `ScriptFields` `value` | `"prefab:<GUID>"` |
| Script field `DataAsset` subclass | `ScriptFields` `value` | GUID string |

Legacy path keys (`"texture": "Default/Pixel.png"`, `"clip"`) still load but resolve relative to the working directory — don't use them.

### C# field types that can be wired from JSON
`Texture`, `Audio`, `Scene`, `Material`, `Mesh`, `AnimationClip`, `AnimatorController`, `Graph`, `Entity` (scene entity or prefab), any `Component`/`EntityScript` subclass and built-in component wrapper, any `DataAsset` subclass, and `List<T>`/`T[]` of these. **Not** wireable: `Font` (put it on the `TextRenderer`), and the types `FontRef`/`SceneRef`/`PrefabRef` don't exist (`TextureRef`/`AudioRef` are internal) despite what older docs say.

```csharp
public class BrickHealth : EntityScript
{
    public int Hits = 1;
    public Audio? BreakSound;     // wired: "type": "audio",  "value": "<GUID>"
    public Entity? DebrisPrefab;  // wired: "type": "entity", "value": "prefab:<GUID>"
}
```

## Data Assets (`.dataasset`)

Tables of game content (enemies, items, waves, levels) and shared tuning live in Data Assets, not in C#. Class, file format, list encodings, generator helpers and patterns: **`data-driven.md`**. The short version: `public class EnemyData : DataAsset { … }`, one `Assets/Data/Enemies/Slime.dataasset` per entry (`{"version":1,"type":"EnemyData","fields":{"MaxHealth":"12"}}`, every value a string), referenced from scripts as `"type": "dataasset:EnemyData", "value": "<GUID>"`.

## Shipping notes
- Builds ship only what the game can reach: build scenes and everything they reference (by GUID, path or scene name, followed recursively), paths in `project.json`, folders/files named by string literals in C#, `AssetManager.FindAll<T>("Prefix")` targets, and all of `Assets/StreamingAssets/`. Files found through a **computed** path (`"Level" + i + ".json"`) are not detected, so put them in `Assets/StreamingAssets/`. Scenes/prefabs are converted to binary in the output (`Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Building-and-Shipping.md`).
- Keep `.meta` files in version control (the Launcher's `.gitignore` already does).

# Data-driven games with Data Assets

A Data Asset is Funke's ScriptableObject: a C# class deriving from `DataAsset` is the template, and each `.dataasset` file is one filled-in entry with its own GUID. Scripts hold references to entries in serialized fields. The Inspector edits them, and the engine keeps one shared live instance per file.

Agent-made games kept skipping this and wrote stat tables, `switch` ladders and `static readonly` arrays into C# instead. Such a game works, but every balance change becomes a code change, the content is invisible in the Editor, and adding an enemy means touching four scripts. Treat Data Assets as the default container for game content.

Ground truth: `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Scene/DataAsset.cs`, `Interop/ScriptInstanceManager.cs` (`MapFieldType`, `FormatFieldValue`, `EncodeListString`, `GetObjectListFields`), `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/DataAssetManager.cpp`, docs `Github-Docs/Documentation/Assets/Data-Assets.md`.

## When something is a Data Asset

| Situation | Container |
|---|---|
| Several entries of the same kind: enemy types, towers, weapons, items, waves, levels, upgrades, shop offers, dialogue lines, achievements | **Data Asset type**, one file per entry |
| Values a designer will tune: speeds, costs, health, spawn rates, difficulty curves | fields on a Data Asset (shared) or on the script (one entity only) |
| One set of values used by several prefabs or scenes: player stats, economy rules, theme colours | **one** Data Asset that they all reference |
| A reusable *entity* with components and children | **prefab**, which usually references its Data Asset |
| Per-instance values on one entity: this door's target, this platform's path | plain script fields in the scene |
| Runtime state: current health, score, cooldowns | fields on the script instance, **never** in a Data Asset |

## Declaring a type

```csharp
// Assets/Scripts/Data/EnemyData.cs
using Funke;

[CreateDataAsset("Game/Enemy")]                 // Asset Browser: Create > Data Asset > Game/Enemy
public class EnemyData : DataAsset
{
    public string Id = "";                      // stable id for saves and logs (renaming the file keeps the GUID, not the meaning)
    public string DisplayName = "Enemy";
    [ClampValue(1, 10000)] public int MaxHealth = 10;
    public float Speed = 1.5f;
    public int Armor;
    public int Reward = 5;
    public Entity? Prefab;                      // the prefab to spawn ("prefab:<guid>")
    public Texture? Icon;                       // for wave previews / bestiary
    public Audio? DeathSound;
    public EnemyKind Kind;                      // enum -> stored as its integer
    public Graph SpeedOverLife = new();         // curve, Graph.Evaluate(t01)

    public override void OnValidate() { if (Speed < 0) Speed = 0; }
}
```

Supported field types: `bool`, integer types, `float`, `double`, `string`, enums (`[Flags]` too), `Vector2/3/4`, `Color`, `Graph`, asset types (`Texture`, `Audio`, `Material`, `Mesh`, `Scene`, `AnimationClip`, `AnimatorController`), `Entity` (prefab), other `DataAsset` types, `List<T>`/`T[]` of those, a nested plain class/struct (flattened to `"Stats.Hp"`, up to 4 levels), and `List<PlainClass>` inline object lists (below). **Not serialized, without any warning:** `Font`, `Dictionary`, `HashSet`, other generic types, and lists inside list elements.

The class must be non-abstract with a parameterless constructor. Keep it in the global namespace, or use the full name as `type` in the file. Inspector attributes work (`[Header]`, `[ToolTip]`, `[ClampValue]`, `[Space]`).

## The file

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "type": "EnemyData",
  "fields": {
    "Id": "slime", "DisplayName": "Slime", "MaxHealth": "12", "Speed": "1.25", "Reward": "5",
    "Prefab": "prefab:7300000000000000101", "Icon": "7300000000000000201", "Kind": "0"
  }
}
```

- Path: `Assets/Data/<Type plural>/<Entry>.dataasset` (e.g. `Assets/Data/Enemies/Slime.dataasset`) plus its `.meta`.
- **Every value is a JSON string.** A raw number or bool silently becomes `""`, and the field keeps its default. `funke_game_tool.py validate` flags it.
- Encodings: numbers in invariant culture (`1.25`, never `1,25`), `"true"`/`"false"`, `"x,y"` vectors, `"r,g,b,a"` colours (0..1), enums as integers, asset and Data Asset references as decimal GUID strings, prefabs as `"prefab:<guid>"`, `Graph` as `"px,py,inX,inY,outX,outY;…"`, nested fields as `"Stats.Hp"`.
- Lists: each element prefixed with a newline (`"\nslime\nbat"`; GUID lists the same way). Inline object lists nest that encoding. Don't write them by hand. Use the generator helpers:

```python
import importlib.util, sys
sys.path.insert(0, r"<skill>/scripts"); import funke_game_tool as fg

slime = fg.write_dataasset(P / "Assets/Data/Enemies/Slime.dataasset", "EnemyData",
                           {"Id": "slime", "MaxHealth": 12, "Speed": 1.25, "Prefab": f"prefab:{SLIME_PREFAB}"})
fg.write_dataasset(P / "Assets/Data/Waves/Wave01.dataasset", "WaveData",
                   {"Groups": fg.encode_objects([[str(slime), 6, 0.8, 0.0],        # SpawnGroup: Enemy, Count,
                                                 [str(bat),   4, 0.5, 3.0]]),      #   Interval, Delay (declaration order)
                    "Reward": 25})
```
`write_dataasset` writes the `.meta` first, encodes every value as a string, and by default **never overwrites an existing file** (`overwrite=False`): once someone has tuned the entry in the Inspector, the file is the source of truth.

## Referencing from scripts and scenes

```csharp
public sealed class EnemyHealth : EntityScript
{
    public EnemyData? Data;                     // wired in the prefab's ScriptFields
    public int Current { get; private set; }
    public override void OnAwake() => Current = Data?.MaxHealth ?? 1;   // copy into runtime state
}
```
```json
"ScriptFields": { "EnemyHealth": [
  { "name": "Data", "type": "dataasset:EnemyData", "value": "7300000000000000301" } ] }
```
Lists of Data Assets: `{"name": "Levels", "type": "list", "value": "\n<guid1>\n<guid2>"}`.

Loading in code is fine for catalogs that are meant to be complete: `AssetManager.FindAll<EnemyData>("Data/Enemies")` (every entry under a folder, subclasses included) or `AssetManager.LoadByGUID<T>(guid)`. Prefer a serialized field whenever one script needs specific entries.

## Patterns

### Types of things (enemies, towers, items)
One `XData` type plus one prefab per **look/behaviour family**. The prefab's scripts take `Data` as a field, wired in the prefab or overridden per placed instance with `"Overrides": {"EnemyHealth.Data": "<guid>"}`. A `Class.Field` override only applies when the prefab entity already has a `ScriptFields` row for that field, so give the prefab a default. If several types share a prefab, the spawner instantiates `data.Prefab` and hands the data over: `if (data.Prefab is { } p) Instantiate(p, pos).GetComponent<EnemyHealth>()?.Init(data);`. Stats never live in the prefab's scripts as literals.

### Waves and spawn tables
```csharp
public class SpawnGroup { public EnemyData? Enemy; public int Count = 5; public float Interval = 1f; public float Delay; }

[CreateDataAsset("Game/Wave")]
public class WaveData : DataAsset { public List<SpawnGroup> Groups = new(); public int Reward = 20; }
```
`List<PlainClass>` elements may hold scalars, enums and asset/Data Asset references, but no nested lists. A `WaveSpawner` script walks `Level.Waves` with a coroutine. Balancing waves then means editing files, with no code change.

### Levels and progression
```csharp
[CreateDataAsset("Game/Level")]
public class LevelData : DataAsset
{
    public string Id = "";  public string DisplayName = "";  public Scene? Scene;
    public List<WaveData> Waves = new();  public int StartMoney = 100;
    public int TwoStarScore, ThreeStarScore;  public Texture? Preview;
}

[CreateDataAsset("Game/Level Catalog")]
public class LevelCatalog : DataAsset { public List<LevelData> Levels = new(); }   // explicit order = unlock order
```
The level select reads `LevelCatalog.Levels` and instantiates a card prefab per entry. Progress is saved by `Id` (`PlayerPrefs.SetInt($"best.{level.Id}", stars)` or one `SaveData` object), never by list index, so reordering levels doesn't scramble saves. One catalog asset beats `FindAll` here because the order is explicit and visible in the Inspector.

### Shared rules and theme
`EconomySettings` (start money, sell ratio, interest), `PlayerSettings` (speed, jump, coyote time) and `Theme` (palette colours from `Design/palette.json`, written by the art generator) each exist **once** and are referenced by every script that needs them. A balance pass then touches one file.

### Curves
Difficulty over time, damage falloff and jump arcs go in a `Graph` field (`Curve.Evaluate(t01)`) that is editable in the Inspector, not in a hand-written formula with magic numbers.

## Rules

- **Read-only at runtime.** All holders share one live instance per file, so writing `Data.Speed *= 2` speeds up every enemy of that type, also in later Play sessions until a reload. Copy into runtime state (`m_Speed = Data.Speed * buff`).
- **Content ids are strings** (`Id` field) when they reach saves, logs or analytics.
- **Generated vs tuned:** a generator may create the initial entries (`write_dataasset(..., overwrite=False)`), but it doesn't overwrite them afterwards. If a generator must own a data set (e.g. a procedurally generated level list), say so in `Design/GameBrief.md` and in the generator's docstring.
- **Validate:** `funke validate` checks every `.dataasset`'s `type` and fields, and `funke_game_tool.py validate` adds the string-value check plus the C# lint (content tables in code warn as rule 2).
- Edits to `.dataasset` files reload live in the Editor, even during Play. That makes them the fastest balancing loop there is.

# Pre-production: game brief, palette, design language

Every new game starts here, before the first scene, script or texture. The output is two short documents and a palette file in the project. Every later step reads them: the scene layout, the Data Asset tables, the art generators (`funke-game-art`) and the UI.

**Why this step exists.** Without an agreed look, agents produce a grab-bag: three pixel densities in one screen, the default font, colours picked per file, a menu that looks like a debug panel. The user then rejects whole asset families late. Mindcraft's art was regenerated three times for exactly that reason. A few questions up front cost minutes; a redo costs days.

## When

| Situation | Do |
|---|---|
| New game | Full flow below. |
| Existing game that has `Design/GameBrief.md` + `Design/DesignLanguage.md` (or its own equivalents: `DesignLanguage.md`, `Planning/Style-Guide.md`, `Planning/Design.md`, a README) | Read them before you start, and follow them. Don't ask again. |
| Existing game without design docs, and the task adds visible content (new screen, new enemy family, new level theme) | Offer to write the docs from what the project already shows. Then extend them for the new content. |
| A small change that adds no new visuals (a bug fix, a tweak, one more enemy of an existing kind) | Skip. |

## 1. Ask

Ask in the user's language. Use an available user-input tool according to its current schema and mode restrictions; otherwise ask a short numbered list in chat. Put your recommendation first. Ask only for unresolved choices that materially affect the result, and preserve decisions and autonomy already given in the request.

**Skip what the request already answers.** "Make a pixel-art roguelike for phones in portrait, dark fantasy" already settles platform, orientation, style and mood, so don't ask those again.

### Round 0: how much does the user want to decide?

Ask this first and on its own, because the answer decides whether there are more rounds:

> How should we set up the game?
> 1. **Define it together (recommended).** Two short rounds: the game, then the look.
> 2. **I give the idea, you do the look.** Only the game round; you design palette and design language.
> 3. **You decide everything (100 %).** No more questions; you fill the brief and design language yourself.

If the user already said something like "just do it", "entscheide selbst" or "mach einfach", that means option 3 and you don't ask.

### Round 1: the game

1. **Genre and core idea**: offer 3 concrete pitches derived from the request (one sentence each), plus "Other".
2. **Platform**: PC (mouse + keyboard) · phone portrait · phone landscape · PC + phone.
3. **Scope**: playable prototype of the core mechanic · one polished level/vertical slice · small full game (menu, 3–5 levels, progression) · bigger (tell me).
4. **Dimension and camera**: 2D side view · 2D top-down · 3D third person · 3D top-down/isometric. Leave this question out when the genre already implies it.

### Round 2: the look

1. **Art style**: pixel art (state the density, e.g. 16 px characters on 16 px tiles) · flat vector (clean shapes, soft gradients) · low-poly 3D (flat shaded, solid colours) · hand-painted/illustrated.
2. **Palette and mood**: offer 3 named palettes that fit the pitch, each with 5–6 hex values in the option text (e.g. "Warm dusk: #2B1B2F #6B2E4F #E26D5C #F5B971 #FFF3D6"), plus "I'll give hex codes".
3. **UI language**: rounded and soft (pills, thick outline, bottom lip) · sharp and minimal (thin lines, flat) · material frames that come from the game world (wood + stone, metal + rivets) · pixel frames (9-slice, 1 px outline). Name the font feeling with each option, e.g. "rounded sans", "pixel font for titles".
4. **Feel / juice level**: calm and clean · punchy (screen shake, hit-stop, particles, pop-in) · cosy (gentle easing, soft sounds).

Optional third round only when it matters for the game: audio mood, reference games ("like Celeste's dash, Hades' UI"), languages to ship, accessibility (colour-blind safe signals, big touch targets).

### Option 3: the agent decides (100 %)

Make every decision above yourself and be bold rather than generic. Pick a specific palette with a mood name, one art style and a specific UI language that suits the pitch. "Blue buttons on a grey panel" is not a design language. Write the documents exactly as below and show the summary and the style sample (step 3) in your next progress message. Then keep working, without waiting for approval. The user can still interrupt.

## 2. Write the documents

Create them in `<Project>/Design/`. That folder sits next to `Assets/`, so it is never shipped.

### `Design/GameBrief.md`

```markdown
# <Game> — Game Brief

**Pitch:** <one or two sentences: what the player does and why it is fun>
**Platform:** <PC / phone portrait / …> · **Dimension:** <2D side / top-down / 3D …> · **Scope:** <prototype / slice / full game: N levels>

## Core loop
1. <action> → 2. <challenge> → 3. <reward / progress> → back to 1

## Controls
| Action | PC | Touch |
|---|---|---|

## Win, lose, restart
- Win: … · Lose: … · Restart: … · Feedback: <score, lives, stars, HUD>

## Progression
<levels / waves / unlocks / economy; what the result screen and level cards show>

## Content (→ Data Assets)
| Kind | Entries | Data Asset type |
|---|---|---|
| Enemies | Slime, Bat, … | `EnemyData` |
| Levels | 1–5 | `LevelData` |

## Feel targets
<speed, weight, juice level, camera behaviour>

## Out of scope
<what we deliberately don't build now>

## Open questions
```

The **Content** table is where data-driven design starts: everything with more than one entry of the same kind (enemies, items, waves, levels, upgrades, dialogue) becomes a Data Asset type. See `data-driven.md`.

### `Design/DesignLanguage.md`

```markdown
# <Game> — Design Language

## Art direction
3–5 numbered principles, each one sentence plus the reason. Example: "One pixel density: 16 texels per tile,
characters 16×24, UI art pixel = 3 screen px at 1080p. Nothing finer or coarser."

## Palette
Tokens, not loose values. Source of truth: `Design/palette.json`.
| Token | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| ink | #1B1A2E | outlines, text shadows |
| surface | … | panel body |
| primary | … | main action, the player's signature colour |
| positive / danger / gold | … | win, damage, rewards |
(+ world ramps: 4–5 steps dark → light per material, e.g. grass, stone, wood)
Signature colours: every mechanic the player must learn (hazard, pickup, checkpoint) gets one colour that it keeps
everywhere: model, particles, UI icon.

## Typography
| Role | Font | Sizes (UI reference units) |
|---|---|---|
| Titles | … | 64 / 40 |
| Body, buttons | … | 32 / 26 |

## Scale and pixel rules
Pixel density, art px → UI px, PPU, target display scale and filter (see funke-game-art), camera size; minimum touch target.

## Shapes and UI
Corner radius or cut corners, outline width, bevel/lip, shadow, panel vs well vs button, 9-slice borders,
states (hover ×1.1, pressed ×0.8 + lip removed, disabled ×0.5).

## Light and shading
Light direction (e.g. top-left), highlight/shadow hue shift (warm highlights, cool shadows), outline colour rules.

## Motion and juice
Easing (ease-out for UI, overshoot for pop-in), durations (UI 0.15–0.25 s), screen shake, hit flash, particles.

## Do / Don't
Short list of the things that break the look.

## Generators
| Asset family | Generator | Output |
|---|---|---|
```

### `Design/palette.json`

The machine-readable copy of the palette. It is the one source that every art generator reads (`funke-game-art` → `scripts/pixelkit.py` loads it), so a colour changes in one place:

```json
{
  "name": "Warm dusk",
  "tokens": { "ink": "#2B1B2F", "surface": "#3D2A45", "primary": "#E26D5C", "positive": "#7BC47F",
              "danger": "#D9455F", "gold": "#F5B971", "text": "#FFF3D6", "textMuted": "#C9B8B0" },
  "ramps": { "grass": ["#1F3B2D", "#2F5D3A", "#4C8C4A", "#7DBB5C", "#B7E07A"],
             "stone": ["#2A2633", "#46404F", "#6A6273", "#958B9A", "#C9C0C8"] }
}
```

When runtime code needs the colours too (tinting UI states, damage flashes, team colours), a generator writes them into a Data Asset (`Assets/Data/Theme.dataasset` of a `Theme : DataAsset` class with `Color` fields), and scripts take it as a field. Don't hand-copy hex values into C#.

## 3. Show a style sample, then build

Before you produce whole asset families, render **one** sample image to `Design/style-sample.png`. It should hold the palette swatches with token names, one panel with a title and a button in its normal and pressed states, one character or tile at the real pixel density, and a line of body text in the chosen font. `funke-game-art` → `scripts/pixelkit.py sample` builds it from `palette.json`. Show it with `view_image` and your summary of both documents.

- **Modes 1 and 2:** ask "Does the look fit?" and wait. A change here costs one regenerate; after rollout it costs the whole asset family.
- **Mode 3:** show the sample and continue.

Then go back to `SKILL.md` → Workflow step 1 (plan) and keep both documents up to date as the game grows. If a decision changes, change the document first.

# Scene & Prefab JSON — authoring reference

Ground truth: `Funke-Engine/src/Serialization/SceneSerializer.cpp` (writer), `SceneSerializerDeserialize.cpp` (reader), `SceneSerializerShared.hpp`, `Funke-Engine/src/Scene/BuiltInComponentRegistration*.cpp`. If this file and the code disagree, the code wins — and fix this file.

## Format detection & the Editor

- The loader sniffs magic bytes: files starting with `FNKSCNB\x1A` are binary, **everything else is parsed as JSON**, regardless of project settings. A hand-written JSON scene loads in a Binary project.
- But the **Editor re-saves** scenes/prefabs in the project's `assetSerializationFormat`. New projects are `Json`; a `project.json` without the key (older projects) means `Binary` — run `funke convert --format json` so your files stay JSON.
- A save regenerates the file from live state: unknown keys are dropped, and `ScriptFields` for classes/fields the compiled assembly doesn't know are dropped. → Compile scripts before the user opens/saves the scene.
- The JSON parser is **strict**: no comments, no trailing commas, nothing after the root. UTF-8 (BOM tolerated). Duplicate keys: last wins (warning).
- If the Editor has the scene open while you edit the file, the Editor's in-memory copy wins on its next save. Edit with the Editor closed, or tell the user to reload.

## Scene file

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "name": "Level1",
  "systems": [ "WaveSpawner", { "className": "Other", "enabled": false, "fields": { "Speed": "2.5" } } ],
  "entities": [ ... ]
}
```

| Key | Rule |
|---|---|
| `entities` | **required**, array |
| `version` | optional; integer 0..1. `2+` is rejected |
| `name` | optional; defaults to file stem. Keep equal to the file name |
| `sceneId` | optional; omit |
| `systems` | optional; `SceneSystem` class names (string) or `{className, enabled, fields}` — `fields` values **must be strings** or the whole scene fails to load |

**A broken file can still half-load.** A missing prefab becomes a "Missing Prefab (…)" placeholder and an invalid `Origin` a warning, so a scene that "loads" can still be wrong: always read the log or run `funke validate`. Structural errors still reject the file: any bad entity (duplicate `uuid`, entity not an object, bad `systems` entry) rejects the entire file.

Scenes are found **by file name** anywhere under `Assets/` (case-insensitive). Two files with the same basename = ambiguous = load error. Scene names may not contain `/ \ : < > " | ? *`, `..` or start with `.`.

## Entity

```json
{
  "name": "Player",
  "uuid": "4821903311200457213",
  "parentUuid": "1730062311204411821",
  "childIndex": 0,
  "Transform2D": { "posX": 0, "posY": -4, "rotation": 0, "scaleX": 2, "scaleY": 0.4 },
  "SpriteRenderer": { ... },
  "Scripts": [ { "className": "PaddleMovement", "type": "Managed" } ],
  "ScriptFields": { "PaddleMovement": [ { "name": "Speed", "type": "float", "value": "9" } ] }
}
```

| Key | Rule |
|---|---|
| `uuid` | **Always set.** Non-zero uint64 as a **decimal string**, unique within the file. It's the stable identity that `ScriptFields` entity refs, `parentUuid`, UI `targetGraphic`/`onClick` etc. point at. Without it a random id is generated every load and nothing can reference the entity. Generate with `funke_game_tool.py guid`. |
| `name` | String. Omit → no name. Give every entity a clear name. |
| `parentUuid` | Parent's uuid; the loader accepts decimal strings or numeric uint64 values. Prefer strings to preserve precision across tools. Unresolved or malformed parent → root. |
| `childIndex` | Order among siblings (scenes only). |
| `disabled` | `true` = inactive. There is no `active`/`enabled` key. |
| `static`, `deadly` | Optional boolean tags. |
| `ComponentOrder` | Optional `{ "order": ["Camera3D", "script:Player", ...] }`: the Inspector order the Editor writes when components are reordered by hand (serialized names, `script:<Class>` for scripts, `managed:<Class>` for C# components). Editor-only, safe to omit. |
| `Origin` | Omit or use `"Scene"` for normal entities; `"Prefab"` for prefab instances (below). Unsupported values log a warning and load as scene content. |
| Don't write | `SceneGUID`, `RuntimeID`, `SourceEntityId`, `sourceUuid` (identity plumbing the Editor writes) |

- **No `Transform2D` key → the entity has no transform.** World entities need at least `"Transform2D": {}`. UI entities use `RectTransform2D` instead — the two conflict.
- Entities can appear in any order (parents may come after children).
- There are no string tags or named layers. Physics uses collider `layer`/`collisionMask` bitmasks; rendering uses `sortLayer` (0–255) / `sortOrder` (int16).
- Transform values are **local to the parent**. `rotation` is **radians** in JSON (the C# `Transform2D.Rotation` property and the Inspector show degrees).

### Value conventions
- Keys are case-sensitive. Enums are integers. Booleans must be `true`/`false` (`1` is rejected → default).
- Vectors are usually flat keys (`posX`/`posY`); a few are `{x,y}` objects (noted below).
- Colors: flat `r,g,b,a` on Sprite/Text/Camera; `{r,g,b,a}` objects on UI widgets and PostProcessing.
- **Author 64-bit ids/GUIDs as strings** everywhere to preserve precision. `uuid` and `parentUuid` accept numeric uint64 values too; `fontAsset`, UI entity refs, UI sprite GUIDs and all `ScriptFields` values use strings.
- Missing keys keep the component default (listed below).

## Built-in components (JSON key → fields, default)

### World / rendering
- **`Transform2D`** — `posX` 0, `posY` 0, `rotation` 0 (rad), `scaleX` 1, `scaleY` 1.
- **`SpriteRenderer`** — `r,g,b,a` 1; `sortOrder` 0; `sortLayer` 0; `textureAsset` (GUID string); `spriteName` (slice name from the texture's .meta; omit = whole texture); `filterMode` 4 (Point=0, Bilinear=1, Trilinear=2, Anisotropic=3, Default=4 → use .meta / Point); `wrapU`/`wrapV` GL constants (Repeat=10497, Clamp=33071 default, Mirror=33648); `pixelsPerUnit` 0; `flipX`/`flipY` false. Size on screen: with `pixelsPerUnit` 0 the sprite fills the Transform scale (1 unit per scale 1); with `pixelsPerUnit` > 0 it keeps its native size (slice px / pixelsPerUnit × scale) and sits on the slice's `.meta` pivot, like a Unity sprite.
- **`TextRenderer`** — `text`; `fontAsset` (**string** GUID; omit = default font); `fontSize` 32; `r,g,b,a`; `alignment` Left=0/Center=1/Right=2; `valign` Top=0/Middle=1/Bottom=2; `letterSpacing`, `lineSpacing`; `wrapMode` None=0/Word=1/Character=2; `autoSize`; `marginL/T/R/B`; `sortOrder`, `sortLayer`; effects drawn under the glyphs in text pixels (Font Size units): `outlineWidth` 0 (off) + `outlineR/G/B/A` (0,0,0,1), `shadowX`/`shadowY` 0 (off; +Y up, `2, -2` = down-right) + `shadowR/G/B/A` (0,0,0,0.5) — no duplicated child label for outlines or shadows. Two modes, chosen by the transform on the entity:
  - **World text** — with `Transform2D`: lives in the world like a sprite (moves with the camera, follows parent transforms, `rotation`, and `scaleX` as uniform scale). Size: `fontSize` pixels / 100 = world units at scale 1 (`fontSize: 64` ≈ 0.64 units tall). The anchor is the transform position; `alignment` picks left/center/right around it. Drawn **after all sprites** (above them, inside post-processing); `sortOrder`/`sortLayer` only order texts among each other. Use for damage numbers, labels over objects, signs.
  - **UI text** — with `RectTransform2D`: screen-space, laid out in the UI rect (HUD, menus).
- **`Camera2D`** — `orthoSize` 5 (half the visible height in world units), `zoom` 1, `clearR/G/B` 0.1, `clearA` 1, `postProcessing` true.
- **`ParticleSystem2D`** — `playOnAwake` true, `lifetime` 1, `speed` 5, `scaleX/scaleY`, `gravityX/gravityY`, `useGravity`, `useRandomColors`, `moveDirectionX/Y`, `emitOverTime` 10, `rateOverDistance` 0, `emissionSpace` Local=0/World=1 (default 1), `shapeType` Circle=0 (`radius`, `isOnCircle`, `arc` 360) / Square=1 (`halfExtendsX/Y`) / Edge=2 (`edgeLength`), `maxParticles` 1000, `colorR/G/B/A`, `sortOrder`, `sortLayer`, `textureAsset`, `bursts` `[{count, interval}]`, `scaleOverLifetimeEnabled` + `scaleOverLifetimeKeys` `[{x,y,inX,inY,outX,outY}]`, `colorOverLifetimeEnabled` + `colorOverLifetimeColorKeys` `[{t,r,g,b}]` + `colorOverLifetimeAlphaKeys` `[{t,a}]`.
- **`PostProcessing2D`** — nested objects: `colorGrading {enabled, exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint, colorFilter{r,g,b,a}}`, `vignette {enabled, color, intensity, smoothness, roundness, centerX, centerY}`, `chromaticAberration {enabled, intensity}`, `grain {enabled, intensity, size, colored}`, `bloom {enabled, threshold, intensity, scatter, taps, tint}`, `lensDistortion {…}`, `pixelated {enabled, blockSize, paletteSteps, quantizeColor}`, `gaussianBlur {enabled, radius, taps}`.

Only **one renderer per entity**: `SpriteRenderer`, `Image`, `ParticleSystem2D`, `TextRenderer` are mutually exclusive. Need a sprite with a label? Use a child entity.

### 3D (project `modules` contains `"Funke.3D"`)
- **`Transform3D`** — `posX/posY/posZ` 0, `rotX/rotY/rotZ` 0 (Euler degrees: pitch, yaw, roll), `scaleX/scaleY/scaleZ` 1. Never together with `Transform2D` or `RectTransform`. Entities default to `Transform2D` only when the key is present; a 3D entity just lists `Transform3D`.
- **`Camera3D`** — `projection` Perspective=0/Orthographic=1, `fov` 60 (vertical degrees), `orthoSize` 5, `near` 0.1, `far` 1000, `background` Skybox=0/SolidColor=1, `clearColor {r,g,b,a}` (SolidColor only), `skyTop`/`skyHorizon`/`skyGround {r,g,b,a}`, `sunSize` 2 (degrees, 0 hides the sun), `skyAmbient` 0.5. Looks down local −Z; a scene with a Camera3D gets no default Camera2D. **Always write `"background": 0`** for a sky: a `clearColor` without `background` loads as SolidColor (legacy scenes). Also `skyboxMaterial` "<material GUID>" (a Skybox-shader material replaces the gradient), `ambientFromSkybox` false, `fog` false, `fogColor {r,g,b,a}`, `fogStart`, `fogEnd` (world units from the camera).
- **`MeshRenderer`** — `mesh` Cube=0/Sphere=1/Plane=2/Cylinder=3 (unit size; Plane lies in XZ facing +Y), `material` "<.material GUID as decimal string>" (omit for the white default), `color {r,g,b,a}` (tint), `lit` true (only without a material), `castShadows` true.
- **`SkinnedMeshRenderer`** — animated `.glb`/`.gltf` model: `model` "<mesh GUID>", `material`, `color`, `lit`, `castShadows`, `clip` "<clip name>" ("" = first clip), `speed` 1, `loop` true, `playOnAwake` true, `previewInEditMode` false, `cullingMode` AlwaysAnimate=0/CullPose=1/CullCompletely=2, `distanceRate` ProjectSetting=0/Off=1/Custom=2, `halfRateDistance` 20, `quarterRateDistance` 40 (the last four only when changed). Conflicts with `MeshRenderer` on the same entity; switch clips from C# with `GetComponent<SkinnedMeshRenderer>().Play("Run", 0.2f)`.
- **`DirectionalLight`** — `color {r,g,b,a}`, `intensity` 1, `ambient {r,g,b,a}`, `castShadows` true. Shines along local −Z; the first enabled one is the main light (ambient, sun disc, the only shadow caster). Point it down with e.g. `rotX` −50.
- **`PointLight`** — `color {r,g,b,a}`, `intensity` 4, `range` 10 (falls to zero at range).
- **`SpotLight`** — `color {r,g,b,a}`, `intensity` 6, `range` 15, `innerAngle` 20, `outerAngle` 30 (half angles in degrees). Shines along local −Z (`rotX` −90 points it down).
- One light component per entity. A scene without any light gets a default light from above.
- **`ParticleSystem3D`** (needs `Transform3D`) — camera-facing billboards. `playOnAwake` true, `lifetime` 2, `lifetimeVariation` 0, `speed` 2, `speedVariation` 0, `size` 0.25 (world units), `sizeVariation` 0, `randomRotation` false, `angularVelocity` 0 (°/s), `useGravity` false + `gravityX/Y/Z` (0,−9.81,0, world space), `drag` 0, `useRandomColors` false, `emitOverTime` 10 (float, per second), `simulationSpace` Local=0/World=1 (default 1), `shape` Sphere=0/Hemisphere=1/**Cone=2** (default)/Box=3, `radius` 0.25, `coneAngle` 25 (half angle), `boxSizeX/Y/Z` 1, `emitFromSurface` false, `texture` "<texture GUID string>" (omit = soft round dots), `color {r,g,b,a}`, `blendMode` Alpha=0/Additive=1, `maxParticles` 1000, `bursts` `[{count, interval}]`, plus the same `scaleOverLifetime*` / `colorOverLifetime*` keys as `ParticleSystem2D`. Cone/Hemisphere open along local **+Y** (no rotation needed for an upward fountain). Additive for fire/sparks/magic, Alpha for smoke/dust; fade out with `colorOverLifetimeAlphaKeys` `[{t:0,a:1},{t:1,a:0}]`. Conflicts with `ParticleSystem2D`.
- **`.material` files** (asset kind Material, needs a `.meta` like any asset): `{"type":"Material","version":1,"lit":true,"baseColor":{r,g,b,a},"baseColorTexture":"<texture GUID or 0>","metallic":0,"roughness":0.5,"emissiveColor":{r,g,b,a},"emissiveIntensity":1,"tiling":{"x":1,"y":1},"offset":{"x":0,"y":0}}`; missing keys take these defaults. Further keys: `surface` Opaque=0/Transparent=1 (alpha blended, drawn after opaque meshes), `fog` true (false for sky domes), `shader` "<.wgsl GUID>" for a custom shader, `properties` {name: value} for its uniforms (`Github-Docs/Documentation/Engine-Core/Custom-Shaders.md`).

### Physics 3D (Jolt; needs `Transform3D`)
- **`Rigidbody3D`** — `type` **Static=0, Kinematic=1, Dynamic=2** (default 2), `mass` 1, `linearDrag` .05, `angularDrag` .05, `gravityScale` 1, `continuous` false (swept collision for fast bodies), `interpolate` true (smooth rendering between fixed steps; project `physicsTickRate` defaults to 50 Hz), `freezePosX/Y/Z`, `freezeRotX/Y/Z` false.
- Shared collider keys: `center {x,y,z}` (local offset), `isTrigger` false, `friction` .5, `bounciness` 0. Sizes are local; the entity's scale applies on top.
- **`BoxCollider3D`** — `size {x,y,z}` 1. **`SphereCollider3D`** — `radius` .5 (largest scale axis). **`CapsuleCollider3D`** — `radius` .5, `height` 2 (end to end), `direction` X=0/Y=1/Z=2.
- **`MeshCollider3D`** — `useMeshRenderer` true (take the MeshRenderer's mesh), `mesh` 0–3 primitive otherwise, `customMesh` (mesh asset GUID string, 0 = primitive), `convex` false. Concave meshes only collide as static/kinematic; dynamic bodies fall back to the convex hull.
- No rigidbody on the entity or an ancestor → a static body. Colliders on children join the nearest `Rigidbody3D` ancestor. Recipes and pitfalls: `3d-games.md`.

### Physics (Box2D)
- **`Rigidbody2D`** — `bodyType` **Static=0, Kinematic=1, Dynamic=2** (default 2); `gravityScale` 1; `mass` (only applied with `"massOverridden": true`); `freezePositionX`, `freezePositionY`, `freezeRotation` false.
- **`BoxCollider2D`** — `localSizeX`, `localSizeY` (both, multiplied by Transform scale — use 1/1 to match the sprite); `centerX/Y` 0; `friction` 0.3; `bounciness` 0; `layer` **1** (bitmask; `0` = collides with nothing); `collisionMask` all bits; `registerContacts` false; `sensor` false (true = trigger).
- **`CircleCollider2D`** — `radius` 0.5, `centerX/Y`, plus the shared collider keys.
- **`PolygonCollider2D`** — `sizeX/Y` 1, `centerX/Y`, `points` `[{"x":..,"y":..}]` (path 0; ≤8 convex/unordered points = hull, longer or concave outlines in order are split into convex pieces, up to 16384), `paths` `[[x0,y0,x1,y1,..], ..]` (further outlines on the same body), `edge` true = every path is an open line instead (ground/slopes, ≥2 points, smooth, solid on top of a left-to-right line, no mass, no sensor), plus shared keys. Shared collider key `density` 1 (mass per area; a Rigidbody2D without pinned mass sums density × area).
- **`TerrainRenderer2D`** — ground along a polyline (hills, roads): `points` flat `[x0,y0,x1,y1,..]` left to right (entity frame), `fillTexture`/`edgeTexture` GUID strings (textures need `wrapU/V: Repeat` in their meta), `fillColor`/`edgeColor` `[r,g,b,a]`, `fillTileX/Y` 4, `fillMapping` 0 World (rows stay horizontal) / 1 Draped, `fillDepth` 10, `edgeThickness` 0.5, `edgeOffset` 0 (edge top above surface), `edgeTileLength` 4 (along the slope), `edgeTextureOffset` 0 (start of the edge pattern in repeats, to continue a neighbouring piece), `sortLayer`, `sortOrder` 0, `edgeSortOrder` 1. Draw only; add a `PolygonCollider2D` (with `edge: true` for a surface line) for collision.
- **`RevoluteJoint2D` / `PrismaticJoint2D` / `WeldJoint2D`** — joint from this entity's body (body A) to `connectedBody` (entity uuid **string**, `"0"`/absent = world). `anchorX/Y` (body A frame, meters, unscaled), `autoConfigureConnectedAnchor` true (else `connectedAnchorX/Y` in body B's frame), `collideConnected` false. Revolute: `enableLimit`, `lowerAngle`, `upperAngle` (radians), `enableMotor`, `motorSpeed` (rad/s), `maxMotorTorque`, `enableSpring`, `springHertz`, `springDampingRatio`. Prismatic: `axisX/Y` (body A frame) + `lowerTranslation`/`upperTranslation`, `maxMotorForce`, same motor/spring keys. Weld: `linearHertz`, `angularHertz` (0 = rigid), `linearDampingRatio`, `angularDampingRatio` 1. Built at play start from the authored pose (author bodies in their rest pose). One joint of each type per entity: put several welds on the parts, connected to the chassis.
- One collider shape per entity. Static walls: collider without Rigidbody (or `bodyType` 0). Moving-by-script objects you still want to collide: `bodyType` 1 (Kinematic).
- **`OnCollisionEnter2D/Stay/Exit` only fire if at least one of the two colliders has `"registerContacts": true`** (default `false` → Box2D reports no contact events, scripts silently never hear about collisions). Set it on the mover (ball, player, bullet). Collisions also need a Rigidbody2D on at least one side.
- `OnTriggerEnter2D/Exit` (a collider with `"sensor": true`) work without `registerContacts`. A sensor reports **every** overlapping collider, static walls included — keep trigger volumes clear of level geometry and filter in the script (`if (other.Other.GetComponent<BallLauncher>() == null) return;`). `other.Other` is the entity that entered.
- A bouncing ball: `Rigidbody2D {bodyType 2, gravityScale 0, freezeRotation true}` + `CircleCollider2D {friction 0, bounciness 1, registerContacts true}`, and give walls/bricks/paddle `friction 0`.

Lightweight AABB physics (`FastBody2D` `type` **Static=0, Dynamic=1, Kinematic=2** — different order!, `mass`, `useGravity`, `boundaryCheck`; `FastBoxCollider2D` `halfX/halfY`; `FastCircleCollider2D` `radius`) comes from the `Funke.Physics` package (`funke package add Funke.Physics`; without it these keys don't load) and conflicts with the Box2D components. Default to Box2D.

### Audio
- **`AudioSource`** — `clipAsset` (GUID string), `volume` 1, `pitch` 1, `loop` false, `playOnAwake` false. Background music: an entity with `AudioSource {loop: true, playOnAwake: true}`.

### Animation
- **`Animator`** — `controllerAsset` (`.animctrl` GUID string), `clipAsset` (`.anim` GUID string, played on its own when there is no controller), `speed` 1, `updateMode` Normal=0/UnscaledTime=1/Fixed=2, `applyInEditMode` false, `cullingMode` / `distanceRate` / `halfRateDistance` / `quarterRateDistance` as on `SkinnedMeshRenderer`. Works with 2D, 3D and UI entities; tracks reach children by name path.
- **`.anim` files** (asset kind AnimationClip): `{"type":"AnimationClip","version":1,"length":1,"loop":true,"sampleRate":60,"tracks":[{"path":"Arm","component":"Transform3D","property":"Rotation.z","keys":[{"t":0,"v":-30},{"t":0.5,"v":30,"interp":"bezier","in":0,"out":0}]},{"path":"","component":"SpriteRenderer","property":"Texture","discrete":[{"t":0,"v":"<sheetGuid>|slice|walk_0"},{"t":0.1,"v":"<sheetGuid>|slice|walk_1"}]}],"events":[{"t":0.5,"function":"OnFootstep","argument":"left"}]}`. `path` = child names joined by `/` from the Animator's entity (`""` = itself); `component` = serialized component name (as in this file) or a C# script class; `property` = Inspector property name with `.x/.y/.z/.w` or `.r/.g/.b/.a` for one channel (`Position.y`, `Color.a`, `Scale.x`; RectTransform2D: `AnchoredPosition`, `SizeDelta`, `Pivot`, `AnchorMin`, `AnchorMax`, `Rotation` degrees, `Scale`). `interp` linear (default)/step/bezier. Asset, string and enum properties use `discrete` keys (asset GUIDs as decimal strings; a sprite-sheet slice as `"<textureGuid>|slice|<sliceName>"` on the `Texture` property of SpriteRenderer/Image; there is no `SpriteName` property). For a plain looping flip-book, assign the clip to the Animator's `clipAsset` without a controller. Events call a public method (no parameter or one string/int/float/bool) on the Animator entity's scripts.
- **`.animctrl` files** (asset kind AnimatorController): `{"type":"AnimatorController","version":1,"parameters":[{"name":"IsRunning","type":"bool","default":false},{"name":"Jump","type":"trigger"}],"states":[{"name":"Idle","clip":"<anim guid>","speed":1,"position":[0,0]},{"name":"Run","clip":"<anim guid>","position":[260,0]}],"defaultState":"Idle","transitions":[{"from":"Idle","to":"Run","conditions":[{"parameter":"IsRunning","mode":"if"}],"hasExitTime":false,"duration":0.2},{"fromAny":true,"to":"Idle","conditions":[{"parameter":"Jump","mode":"if"}],"duration":0.1}]}`. Parameter `type` float/int/bool/trigger; condition `mode` greater/less/equals/notEquals (+ `threshold`)/if/ifNot; state `loop` clip (default)/loop/once; `exitTime` is in clip lengths. Transitions name their states; unknown names are dropped on load, so run `funke validate`.
- Script side: `GetComponent<Animator>()` then `SetBool/SetFloat/SetInteger/SetTrigger`, `Play(state)`, `CrossFade(state, seconds)`, `CurrentStateName` (see `funke-game-scripting`).

### UI
UI entities live under a common root and use **`RectTransform2D`** (no `Transform2D`). Reference resolution comes from `project.json` `uiReferenceWidth/Height` (1920×1080 default).

- **`RectTransform2D`** — `anchorMinX/Y`, `anchorMaxX/Y`, `pivotX/Y` (all 0.5), `posX/Y` 0, `sizeX/Y` 100, `rotation` (rad), `scaleX/Y` 1.

**Layout rules — this is NOT Unity's RectTransform** (`Funke-Engine/src/Systems/UILayoutSystem.cpp` `ResolveRect`):
- `sizeX`/`sizeY` is **always the absolute size** in reference pixels. A parent's size never propagates; there is no stretching. `anchorMin ≠ anchorMax` does **not** stretch — it only moves the reference point to the centre of the anchor rect.
- Position: pivot = centre of the anchor rect inside the parent + `posX/posY`. Then the rect extends `size × pivot` around that point.
- So a **full-screen UI root** is: anchors 0.5/0.5, pivot 0.5, pos 0, `sizeX`/`sizeY` = `uiReferenceWidth`/`uiReferenceHeight` (1920×1080). A root with `sizeX: 0` collapses to a point and all its anchored children pile up in the screen centre. `"fillWidth": true` / `"fillHeight": true` span one parent axis; `"fillParent": true` spans both (the safe area for a root). Use these for responsive roots, bars and overlays; `ignoreSafeArea` extends edge backgrounds to the screen.
- Corner placement: anchor + pivot on the same corner, e.g. top-left label = anchors `(0,1)`, pivot `(0,1)`, `posX: 40, posY: -30`. Y grows upwards (negative `posY` moves down from a top anchor).
- Only `rotation`/`scale` propagate to children.
- **Check HUD elements against the world before placing them.** With a full-screen 1920×1080 root and `Camera2D.orthoSize = h` (16:9): world `y` → UI pixels from the bottom = `(y + h) / (2h) × 1080`, world `x` → pixels from the left = `(x + h·16/9) / (2·h·16/9) × 1920`. Example: paddle at `y = -5`, `h = 6` → ~90 px from the bottom, so a bottom-anchored hint must sit at `posY ≥ ~200`, not 40.
- **`Image`** — `r,g,b,a`, `textureAsset`, `spriteName`, `filterMode` (default **1** Bilinear; **4** follows `.meta`; non-default values call `SetFilter` and can affect users sharing the resolved texture handle), `sortOrder`, `sortLayer`, `materialAsset`; 9-slice: `imageType` Simple=0/Sliced=1/Tiled=2, `border` `[left, bottom, right, top]` in texture px (all 0 → the texture `.meta`'s `border`), `borderScale` 1 (multiplied by the UI scale). Recipes: `funke-game-art` → `references/ui-art.md`.
- **`Interactable`** — `interactable` true, `focusable` false.
- **`Button`**, **`Slider`**, **`Toggle`**, **`InputField`**, **`Dropdown`**, **`Scrollbar`**, **`CircularSlider`** — **dependencies are NOT auto-added on load**: each needs `RectTransform2D` + `Interactable` (+ usually `Image`) on the same entity.
  - Shared: `transitionMode` ColorSwap=0/SpriteSwap=1/None=2; colors `normal`, `hovered`, `pressed`, `disabled`, `focused` as `{r,g,b,a}`; sprites `normalSprite`… as GUID strings (`"0"` none).
  - `Button`: `targetGraphic` (entity uuid string, `"0"` = none), `onClick` (event bindings, below).
  - `Slider`: `value` 0.5, `min` 0, `max` 1, `direction` LeftToRight=0/RightToLeft=1/BottomToTop=2/TopToBottom=3, `wholeNumbers`, `isReadOnly`, `backgroundEntity`, `fillEntity`, `handleEntity`, `labelEntity` (uuid strings), `onValueChanged`.
  - `Toggle`: `isOn`, `isReadOnly`, `checkmarkEntity`, `onValueChanged`.
  - `InputField`: `text`, `placeholder`, `textEntity`, `characterLimit`, `lineLimit`, `contentType` (Standard=0, AlphaNumeric=1, Alpha=2, Integer=3, Decimal=4), `isSecret`, `isReadOnly`, `multiline`, color objects `textColor`, `placeholderColor`, `caretColor`, `selectionColor`, `onValueChanged`, `onSubmitted`.
  - `Dropdown`: `options` `["Easy","Hard"]`, `selectedIndex`, `labelEntity`, `rowHeight` 28, option color objects, `onValueChanged`.
  - `Scrollbar`: `handleEntity`, `direction`, `value`, `size` 0.2, `numberOfSteps`.
- **`ScrollRect`** — `content`, `viewport` (uuid strings), `horizontal`, `vertical`, `movementType` Unrestricted=0/Elastic=1/Clamped=2, `elasticity`, `inertia`, `decelerationRate`, `scrollSensitivity`, scrollbar refs + visibility, `normalizedPosition {x,y}`.
- **`Mask`** — `showMaskGraphic`.
- **`HorizontalLayoutGroup` / `VerticalLayoutGroup`** — `paddingLeft/Right/Top/Bottom`, `spacing`, `childAlignment` (UpperLeft=0 … LowerRight=8), `reverseArrangement`, `controlChildWidth/Height`, `useChildScaleWidth/Height`, `childForceExpandWidth/Height`.
- **`GridLayoutGroup`** — padding keys, `cellSize {x,y}`, `spacing {x,y}`, `startCorner` 0–3, `startAxis` 0/1, `childAlignment`, `constraint` Flexible=0/FixedColumnCount=1/FixedRowCount=2, `constraintCount`.
- **`ContentSizeFitter`** — `horizontalFit`, `verticalFit`, `paddingLeft/Right/Top/Bottom`. **`WidthConstraint`** — `minWidth`, `maxWidth`.
- **`LocalizedText`** — `key` (a key of `Assets/Localization/<lang>.json`). Needs a `TextRenderer` on the same entity (not auto-added on load). During play the text becomes the translation and follows `Localization.SetLanguage`; the `TextRenderer.text` you write is only the edit-mode placeholder. `funke validate` flags keys missing from `en.json`.

**Event bindings** (`onClick`, `onValueChanged`, `onSubmitted`) — wire UI to script methods in JSON instead of subscribing in code where possible:
```json
"onClick": [ { "entity": "<uuid of entity with the script; \"0\" = this entity>", "class": "PauseMenu", "method": "Resume", "enabled": true, "argKind": 0, "argValue": "" } ]
```
`argKind`: Void=0, Bool=1, Int=2, Float=3, Double=4, String=5, Vec2=6, Color=7, EntityRef=8. The target method is a public method on that script.

"Scripts": [ { "className": "BrickHealth", "type": "Managed" } ],
"ScriptFields": {
  "BrickHealth": [
    { "name": "Hits",        "type": "int",    "value": "2" },
    { "name": "BreakSound",  "type": "audio",  "value": "<audio GUID>" },
    { "name": "DebrisPrefab","type": "entity", "value": "prefab:<prefab GUID>" }
  ]
}
```
- `className` = C# class name (global namespace) or full name `"MyGame.BrickHealth"`. An unresolvable class is **skipped without any log** — log a marker in `OnStart` to prove it runs.
- `ScriptFields` entries only apply to classes listed in `Scripts` (or `ManagedComponents` for managed data `Component` classes).
- `name` = exact C# public member name. Nested plain struct/class members: `"Stats.MaxHp"`.
- `value` is **always a string**. `type` is informational except for entity refs (needed for remapping inside prefabs) — always write it.

| C# field type | `type` | `value` |
|---|---|---|
| `float`, `double`, `int`, `long`, … | `float`, `int`, … | `"5"`, `"0.25"` (invariant culture) |
| `bool` | `bool` | `"true"` / `"false"` |
| `string` | `string` | raw text |
| `Color` | `color` | `"r,g,b,a"` |
| `Vector2/3/4`, `Vector2Int`… | `vector2`, … | `"x,y"`, `"x,y,z"` |
| enum / `[Flags]` enum | `enum` / `flagenum` | underlying integer `"2"` |
| `Entity` (scene entity) | `entity` | target `uuid`, `"0"` = none |
| `Entity` holding a prefab | `entity` | `"prefab:<prefab GUID>"` → use with `Instantiate(field)` |
| a `Component` / `EntityScript` subclass, or built-in wrapper (`Rigidbody2D`, `TextRenderer`…) | `component:<Name>` | `"<entityUuid>:<Name>"` — `<Name>` = the C# type name (`TextRenderer`, `Rigidbody2D`, `BrickHealth`) or, for built-ins, the display name the Editor writes (`"Text Renderer"`, `"Rigidbody 2D"`; map in `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Scene/Entity.cs`). Both resolve. |
| `Texture` | `texture` | texture GUID |
| `Audio` | `audio` | audio GUID |
| `Scene` | `scene` | scene GUID (from its .meta) |
| `DataAsset` subclass | `dataasset:<Type>` | `.dataasset` GUID |
| `List<T>` / `T[]` | `list` (+ `"itemType"`: the element's type, e.g. `int`, `entity`, `component:Image`) | each element prefixed by `\n`: `"\n1\n2\n3"`; empty `""` |

`Font` is **not** a supported field type — set `fontAsset` on the `TextRenderer` instead.

## Prefab file

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "type": "Prefab",
  "Entities": [
    { "uuid": "1001", "name": "Enemy",
      "Transform2D": { "scaleX": 0.8, "scaleY": 0.8 },
      "SpriteRenderer": { "r": 1, "g": 0.3, "b": 0.3, "a": 1, "textureAsset": "12278967664992971869" },
      "Rigidbody2D": { "bodyType": 1 },
      "CircleCollider2D": { "radius": 0.5, "layer": 1 },
      "Scripts": [ { "className": "EnemyChase", "type": "Managed" }, { "className": "EnemyHealth", "type": "Managed" } ],
      "ScriptFields": {
        "EnemyHealth": [ { "name": "HealthBar", "type": "entity", "value": "1002" } ] } },
    { "uuid": "1002", "parentUuid": "1001", "name": "HealthBar",
      "Transform2D": { "posY": 0.8, "scaleX": 1, "scaleY": 0.1 },
      "SpriteRenderer": { "r": 0.2, "g": 1, "b": 0.2, "a": 1, "textureAsset": "12290035569547768290", "sortOrder": 1 } }
  ]
}
```
- **First entity is the root.** All `uuid`s unique and non-zero within the file; every `parentUuid` must point inside the file (string or number OK here). Child order = array order.
- Template uuids are local to the prefab; small numbers (`"1001"`) are fine. Entity refs between entities of the same prefab **must** carry `"type": "entity"` so they get remapped per instance. Component refs (`"1002:Sprite Renderer"`, `"type": "component:SpriteRenderer"`) between them are remapped too.
- **Lists** of such refs are remapped per instance when the field says what its elements are: `{ "name": "Slots", "type": "list", "itemType": "entity", "value": "\n1002\n1003" }`, `{ "name": "Icons", "type": "list", "itemType": "component:Image", "value": "\n1002:Image\n1003:Image" }`. Without `itemType` only `"<id>:<Component>"` elements are recognized; bare ids then stay as written (a `List<int>` holding `1002` must not move). Inline-object lists remap the members whose `itemFields` entry has type `entity` / `component:…` (the editor writes `itemFields`). Covered by `SceneSerializerPrefabRefTests.cpp`.
- `type`/`version` are ignored on read; the prefab's GUID comes from `Enemy.prefab.meta` — create it with `funke_game_tool.py meta`.
- Variant: `{ "PrefabRef": "<base GUID or Assets-relative path>", "Overrides": {...}, "EntityOverrides": {...} }` with no `Entities`.

## Prefab instance in a scene

```json
{ "Origin": "Prefab", "PrefabGUID": "<Enemy.prefab GUID>", "uuid": "<new unique id>", "name": "Enemy A",
  "Overrides": { "Transform2D.posX": 3.0, "Transform2D.posY": 2.0, "EnemyChase.Speed": "2.5" },
  "EntityOverrides": { "1002": { "SpriteRenderer.g": 0.5 } } }
```
- Only the instance root is stored; children come from the prefab. Current loaders derive their persistent ids from the instance root id and the template child id, so references to instance children can survive reloads. Let the engine author these derived ids instead of copying template ids into scene references.
- `Overrides` = dot-path → value on the root. `Class.Field` hits a script field only if the prefab entity already has a `ScriptFields` array for that class → in the prefab, write every tunable field once (even with its default).
- `EntityOverrides` keyed by the child's **template** uuid.
- `parentUuid` works on instances too. An unresolved prefab asset becomes a `Missing Prefab` placeholder preserving the instance JSON (identity, parent and overrides); read the warning and repair the asset reference. Missing/zero prefab identity still fails the instance load.

## Checklist before you finish a file
- [ ] Valid strict JSON; `entities` array present.
- [ ] Every entity has a unique decimal-string `uuid`; all `parentUuid`s are strings and exist.
- [ ] World entities have `Transform2D` or `Transform3D`, UI entities `RectTransform2D`; never mix those transforms on one entity.
- [ ] Every GUID you reference exists in a `.meta` (or is a built-in from `assets-and-meta.md`).
- [ ] Colliders have non-zero `layer`; only one renderer and one collider per entity.
- [ ] UI widgets have `RectTransform2D` + `Interactable`; the UI root uses the project reference size or `fillParent` (anchors alone do not stretch).
- [ ] Every collider whose script uses `OnCollisionEnter2D` (or its partner) has `registerContacts: true`.
- [ ] Entities that start hidden (`"disabled": true`) carry no logic — the script that enables them sits on an active entity.
- [ ] `ScriptFields` classes are listed in `Scripts`; all values are strings; entity refs have `"type": "entity"`.
- [ ] `funke validate` is clean: it flags entity/component refs whose target entity or component is missing in the file, and component refs that don't match the field's type.
- [ ] `python funke_game_tool.py validate <project>` reports no errors.

# Testing a Funke game without clicking

An agent can't play the game. It can validate the files, run the game with scripted input, ask the game for its state through dev commands, and look at screenshots taken at exact game times. This file covers all of that, plus shipping a build.

Ground truth: `Funke-Engine/src/DevTools/RunAutomation.cpp` (automation flags, input scripts), `Funke-Engine/src/Core/Application.cpp`, `Funke-Runtime/src/RuntimeApplication.cpp`, `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Core/DevConsole.cs` + `Attributes/DevCommandAttribute.cs`, `Funke-CLI/src/`, `scripts/dev/Run.ps1`. User docs: `Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Testing.md`, `Command-Line.md` and `Editor-Bridge.md`.

## What proves what

| Check | Proves | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Static validation | files load, references resolve, no house-rule violations | `funke validate` + `funke_game_tool.py validate` |
| Compile | scripts build with the shipped defines | `funke run` (compiles first) or `dotnet build -c Release` |
| Smoke run | the game starts, scripts run, no exceptions | `funke_game_tool.py smoke`, `funke run --seconds 5` |
| Scripted run | a gameplay path works: menu → level → win/lose → result | input script + `[DevCommand]` state + game-time screenshots |
| Editor bridge | the same, but faster, while the editor is open | `funke editor play/tap/exec/screenshot` |
| Human playtest | it is fun and feels right | a short checklist for the user |

A smoke run only proves that the game *starts*. Say "playable" only after a scripted run has gone through the core loop, and say "fun" only after the user has played it.

## House rules for test runs on this machine

Several agent sessions build and test in parallel while the user works. So:

- **Never take focus.** Every app you launch gets `--background`: no activation, no exclusive fullscreen, no pause when unfocused. `Run.ps1` and `funke_game_tool.py smoke` add it; `funke run` does **not**, so add it there yourself or use the others. `-Foreground` / no `--background` only when computer-use must see the window.
- **Stay silent.** The engine mutes automated runs by itself: any of `--input-script`, `--screenshot-at`, `--quit-at`, `--exec`, `--fixed-step`, `--background` or `--prefs-profile=<name>` (`Run.ps1` and `smoke` always pass some) makes `Application.IsAutomatedRun` true, and the log says `Sound muted: automated run`. No game-side mute switch or env var is needed, and the game's own volume (`Audio.MasterVolume`, the `GameSettings` template) can't unmute it. `--sound` keeps a run audible, `--mute` silences any run. Use `Application.IsAutomatedRun` to skip intros, ads or tutorials in tests. (Engines before 2026-10-19 had neither; games built for them carry their own `*_MUTE` switch.)
- **Isolate saves.** Runtime test runs use `--prefs-profile=<name>`, which `Run.ps1` sets to `agent`. Then PlayerPrefs and SaveData go to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<Company>\<Name>\Profiles\<name>\`, and the user's real progress stays untouched. Use your own profile name when another session may fill `agent` (a full save list once hid a "New World" button), and delete that folder when you are done.
- **Own log under parallel load.** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\Logs\Funke-Runtime.log` interleaves every session's runtime. Copy `Funke-Runtime.exe` to a unique name in the same folder (e.g. `MyGame-Test.exe`) and you get `MyGame-Test.log`. Re-copy it after an engine rebuild, and delete the copy at the end.
- **Game time, not wall time.** Take screenshots with `--screenshot-at` (game time starts after the splash and startup load) instead of guessing wall-clock seconds.
- **Performance is not measured with screenshots or FPS** here, because other games are always running. See "Performance" below.

## The `funke` command-line tool

Headless unless noted. `funke help <command>`; every command takes `--project <dir>`, most take `--json`.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `funke create <Name> --path <dir>` | New project, same as the Launcher (starter scene, csproj, compile, `git init`, Launcher list). |
| `funke validate [--json] [--strict]` | Read-only: metas, GUID refs, uuids/`parentUuid`, script-field entity/component refs, build/startup scenes, localization keys, shaders, `.anim`/`.animctrl`, `.dataasset` type/fields, then loads every scene and prefab. Exit 1 on errors (`--strict`: warnings too). |
| `funke run [--scene N] [--seconds S] [--no-compile]` + `--prefs-profile`, `--input-script`, `--screenshot-at`, `--screenshot-dir`, `--fixed-step`, `--quit-at`, `--exec` (space form) | Compiles the scripts with the `FUNKE_BUILD` defines in funke.exe's configuration, then plays the project in the sibling `Funke-Runtime`. `--seconds` = real seconds (`--quit-after`). No timeout and no `--background`. Exit 1 when the runtime exits non-zero. |
| `funke build [--release\|--debug\|--development] [--platform P] [--profile N] [--output dir] [--json]` | The Build-panel pipeline without the Editor. `project.json` is not modified. Release builds use the Dist runtime. |
| `funke convert --format json\|binary [paths]` | Rewrites scenes/prefabs/Data Assets (no paths = everything + the project setting). |
| `funke assets refresh` / `funke assets guid <path>` | Write missing metas / print a GUID. |
| `funke prefab create\|apply\|revert\|unpack\|list` | The Editor's prefab buttons on a scene file. |
| `funke sprite slice <png> --grid WxH\|--count CxR\|--alpha` | Writes named slices into the `.meta`. |
| `funke package list\|add\|remove\|refresh` | Project packages (`add Funke.Tilemap2D`, `add nuget:Id@ver`). |
| `funke editor <cmd>` | Drives an **already open editor** (see below). Exit 3 busy/timeout, 4 no editor. |

## App flags

All flags take `--flag=value`; a space-separated value is silently ignored (only `--prefs-profile` accepts both). Run the exe with its own folder as working directory and `CI=1` (suppresses the ".NET missing" dialog).

| Flag | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--project=<root>` | Runtime | Run a project folder (no build needed). |
| `--scene=<Name>` | Runtime | Start in this scene; an unknown name exits with -1. |
| `--prefs-profile=<name>` | Runtime, built game | Isolated PlayerPrefs/SaveData (see above). The Editor ignores the flag; Play mode uses `project.json` `"prefsProfile"`. |
| `--background` | all apps | Never activate, never exclusive fullscreen, never pause unfocused. |
| `--screenshot-at=2s,5.5s,300f` | all | Game-time screenshots (`s`, `ms`, `f` = frame). Default folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\Screenshots`, or `--screenshot-dir=<dir>`. |
| `--input-script=<file.json>` | all | Scripted input (below). |
| `--fixed-step=60` | all | Fixed frame time (≥ 1 = fps, < 1 = seconds per frame): reproducible runs. |
| `--quit-at=<t>` | all | Quit at that game time (`[Automation] Quit at frame N`). |
| `--exec="cmd; cmd"` | all | Console / `[DevCommand]` lines on the first game frame. |
| `--quit-after=<s>` | all | Quit after N real seconds. |
| `--ci-smoke-test` | all | Quit 3 frames after loading. |
| `Funke-Editor.exe --project=<root> --build [--build-profile=N] [--build-output=dir]` | Editor | Old way to build; prefer `funke build`. |

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 init/frame failure, -1 exception at the app boundary. **C# exceptions never change the exit code.** Read the log.

## `scripts\dev\Run.ps1` (engine repo)

`Run.ps1 -App Runtime -Project <root> [-ScreenshotAt 2s,5s] [-InputScript run.json] [-FixedStep 60] [-QuitAt 9s] [-Exec "level.load 2"] [-ExtraArgs "--scene=Level2"] [-Config Release]`. It adds `--background` and `--prefs-profile=agent`. With `-ScreenshotAt`, `-InputScript` or `-QuitAt` the game quits itself (0.5 s after the last shot if nothing else quits it). Game shots land in `bin-int\_agent\run\shots-<time>-<pid>\`, the run's own log slice in `bin-int\_agent\run\Runtime.log`. It prints warnings, errors and crash dumps. It returns 1 for detected crashes/non-zero self-exits; error log lines alone can still accompany exit 0, so read them. The default config is **Release**: compile the scripts with `-c Release`, or the runtime silently loads an older DLL.

## Input scripts

```json
{ "fixedStep": 60, "steps": [
  { "at": "0.5s", "key": "D", "action": "down" },  { "at": 2.0, "key": "D", "action": "up" },
  { "frame": 130, "key": "Space" },
  { "at": "3s", "mouse": [0.5, 0.8], "button": "left" },
  { "at": "4s", "touch": [0.2, 0.8], "finger": 0, "action": "down" },
  { "at": "4.5s", "touch": [0.3, 0.8], "action": "move" }, { "at": "5s", "touch": [0.3, 0.8], "action": "up" },
  { "at": "6s", "command": "coins.add 50; state" },
  { "at": "8s", "screenshot": "level-end" }, { "at": "8s", "log": "checkpoint reached" },
  { "at": "9s", "quit": true } ] }
```

- Each step has a time (`"at"`: seconds or `"2.5s"`/`"500ms"`/`"120f"`; or `"frame"`) and one action: `key` (`action` press/down/up; names like `a`, `space`, `enter`, `esc`, `left`, `shift`, `f1`), `mouse` `[x, y]` 0..1 of the window with optional `button`, `touch` `[x, y]` with `finger` and `action` tap/down/move/up (finger 0 also drives the mouse, so UI buttons react), `command`, `screenshot` (name, no dots in it, `.png` is added), `log`, `quit`.
- A `press` lasts one frame. There is no `wait` step; timing comes only from `at`/`frame`.
- **Not scriptable:** mouse wheel, text entry into an `InputField`, gamepad. Expose what a test needs as a `[DevCommand]` (`map.zoom 2`, `name.set Bob`) and call it from a `command` step.
- One malformed step aborts the **whole** script, including its `quit` (error `[Automation] Input script …: step N`). Always pair a script run with a timeout.
- The same scripts run in an open editor: `funke editor input run.json`.

## Dev commands: the test API every game should have

A `[DevCommand]` is a static method that the console, `--exec`, input-script `command` steps and `funke editor exec` can all call, in the editor, the runtime and Release builds. It is the clean replacement for env-var probes and temporary teleport hacks: it lives in the game for good, it is visible with `help`, and it doesn't have to be deleted afterwards.

```csharp
using Funke;

public static class LevelCommands                    // Assets/Scripts/Core/DevCommands/LevelCommands.cs
{
    [DevCommand("level.load", Description = "Load level N")]
    static void Load(int n) => SceneManager.LoadScene($"Level{n}");

    [DevCommand("player.tp", Description = "Teleport the player")]
    static void Teleport(Vector2 pos) { if (PlayerMovement.Instance is { } p) p.TeleportTo(pos); }

    [DevCommand("game.win")]
    static void Win() => LevelGoal.Instance?.Complete();

    [DevCommand("state", Description = "One-line game state for tests")]
    static string State() => $"level={LevelFlow.Instance?.LevelName} score={ScoreCounter.Instance?.Score} lives={LivesCounter.Instance?.Lives}";
}
```

- Static, non-generic methods (private works). Arguments: `string` (the last one takes the rest of the line), `bool`, `int`, `long`, `float`, `double`, enums, `Vector2`/`Vector3` written as `1,2`. Defaults make parameters optional. A return value is printed.
- Every executed line logs `[DevConsole] > <cmd>` and its output, so `command: "state"` turns into a log assertion you can grep.
- Built-ins: `help`, `timescale [x]`, `scene [name]`, `screenshot [file]`, `quit`, `physics.debug` (collider overlay, also F8), `physics.contacts`, `prefs.path`, `prefs.clear`; runtime only `stats`, `logs`.
- In `Funke-Runtime` the backtick key (left of 1) or a three-finger tap opens the console window unless the build profile turns `devConsole` off (default: off in Release). The commands work either way.
- Group them per feature (`LevelCommands`, `EconomyCommands`) under `Assets/Scripts/Core/DevCommands/`.

## The editor bridge (fastest loop when an editor is open)

Only drive editors you started yourself (`Run.ps1 -KeepOpen`) or that the user asked you to use; `funke editor list` shows the running ones. Nothing moves or focuses windows, and screenshots render offscreen, even while the editor is minimized.

`funke editor play [--scene N] [--size 1080x2400] [--fixed-step 60]` · `tap 0.5 0.4` / `click` / `drag x1 y1 x2 y2` / `key Space [--hold s]` (0..1 of the game surface, `--px` for pixels) · `exec "<command>"` (edit and play mode) · `wait --seconds 2` · `screenshot shot.png` · `input run.json` · `logs --level warning --since …` · `recompile` (prints compiler errors) · `stop`. Edit scripts → `recompile` → `play` again, all without building or starting a runtime.

## Logs

- Line format: `[HH:MM:SS] [FUNKE|APP|EDITOR] [trace|info|warning|error|critical] [Tag] message`. C# `Log.*` lines are `[APP] [info] [Script] …`.
- **Must appear:** `Loaded project:`, `[SceneSerializer] Loaded scene: <name>`, `User assembly loaded:` (missing = no script runs, and nothing else complains), `[ScriptSystem] Applied N pending field value(s) for <Class>` (for entities with `ScriptFields`), and your own markers or `state` output.
- **Must not appear:** `Exception in On…()`, `[Coroutine]`, `Exception in … handler`, `Unhandled exception at app boundary`, `Unhandled frame exception`, `[CrashReporter] Wrote minidump`, `Failed to load user assembly`, `could not be resolved`, `no matching class`, `registered event(s) still active` (a leaked static-event handler), and any `[error]`/`[critical]` line.
- Repeated exceptions are throttled: the first 3 in full, then `… repeated N more time(s) in the last 5s`. The **first** occurrence is the one to read.
- Log one line per state change ("mode Cube -> Ship at x=265", "level completed in 41.2 s") and grep for it. That proves a playthrough even when no screenshot catches the moment. Format numbers with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`: the machine is German, so `8.5` prints as `8,5`.

## Screenshots

- Take them at game time (`-ScreenshotAt` / `--screenshot-at` / input-script `screenshot`) and open them with `view_image`. A shot proves layout, art and overlap, not motion and not performance.
- Shoot **every place you changed**: each new screen, panel state, level joint, bend, the HUD over the busiest part of the world. Overlapping geometry, text behind panels, mojibake and placeholder colours were all caught this way.
- Reach a state with dev commands in the input script (`level.load 3`, `player.tp 120,4`, `ui.open shop`) instead of editing scenes temporarily.
- Judge colours from in-game shots: lighting, ambient light and post-processing shift them away from the offline art.
- Phone layouts: `funke editor play --size 1080x2400`, or a portrait window size in the runtime.

## Prove the core loop

For every game, write one input script per path and keep them in the project (`Tests/Input/*.json`):

1. menu → Play → level select → level 1 loads (screenshot each screen);
2. play → `game.win` (or real input) → result screen → best result saved (`state` / `prefs.path`) → Back → the next level is unlocked;
3. play → die/lose → lose screen → Restart reloads the level.

Run them after every larger change. If gameplay uses fixed-step physics, a small offline simulation (Python is fine) can check that every level is beatable and can generate the input for an autoplay script.

## Performance (on a busy machine)

Other games and builds always run at the same time, so frame times swing by ±40 %. Don't prove performance with screenshots or FPS. Instead:

- Compare load-independent numbers: per-thread CPU cycles, `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread` per frame, GC counts, work counters (entities updated, meshes rebuilt), the biggest single-frame costs per cause.
- Do A/B runs alternating base/change for 2+ rounds and flip the order each pair, best-of-N for microbenchmarks.
- Uncap the frame rate first: `Application.VsyncEnabled = false; Application.TargetFrameRate = 0;` in a test-only dev command.
- Phone costs vary by device and runtime. Measure per-stage timings on the target device before optimizing; a desktop-to-phone multiplier is not a reliable budget.

## Shipping a build

```bash
funke build --project <root> --release            # Release = Dist runtime, no stats/log overlays, no console window
funke build --project <root> --platform Android --release --output Builds/Android
```
- `buildScenes` in project.json lists every shipped scene. The first enabled one is the startup scene.
- The build converts scenes/prefabs to binary in the output only (your sources stay JSON) and ships only the assets the game can reach (references from build scenes, literal paths in C#, `FindAll` prefixes, `Assets/StreamingAssets/`). Files loaded through computed paths go in `Assets/StreamingAssets/`.
- Build profiles (`BuildProfiles/<Name>.build`) carry `configuration`, `defines`, `showRuntimeStats`, `showRuntimeLogs`, `devConsole`, `isolatedPrefs`. Details: `funke-build-and-ship`.

## Creating a project by hand (only if `funke create` is unavailable)

Minimum for the loader: `project.json` + `Assets/`. For scripts you also need the csproj and `Packages/Funke-ScriptCore/Funke-ScriptCore.dll` (+ `.xml`) from `<Engine>/bin/<Cfg>-windows-x86_64/Funke-ScriptCore/`. Then run the Editor once with `--ci-smoke-test` to complete migrations.

```json
{
  "projectFormatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Breakout",
  "engineVersion": "<FunkeVersion from the engine's Version.props>",
  "startupScene": "MainMenu",
  "buildScenes": ["MainMenu", "Level1"],
  "globalSystems": [],
  "assetSerializationFormat": "Json"
}
```
`engineVersion` is required whenever `projectFormatVersion` is set. Other keys get defaults.

`<Name>.csproj` — copy exactly (from `FunkeProject::Create`):
```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Library</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Configurations>Debug;Release;Dist</Configurations>
    <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>
    <EnableDynamicLoading>true</EnableDynamicLoading>
    <CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies>true</CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies>
    <EnableDefaultCompileItems>false</EnableDefaultCompileItems>
    <EnableDefaultNoneItems>false</EnableDefaultNoneItems>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>false</AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'"><OutputPath>bin\Debug\</OutputPath></PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Release'"><OutputPath>bin\Release\</OutputPath><Optimize>true</Optimize></PropertyGroup>
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Dist'"><OutputPath>bin\Dist\</OutputPath><Optimize>true</Optimize></PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup><Compile Include="Assets\**\*.cs" /></ItemGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <Reference Include="Funke-ScriptCore">
      <HintPath>Packages\Funke-ScriptCore\Funke-ScriptCore.dll</HintPath>
      <Private>true</Private>
    </Reference>
  </ItemGroup>
  <Import Project="Packages/FunkePackages.props" Condition="Exists('Packages/FunkePackages.props')" />
  <Import Project="Packages/FunkeDefines.props" Condition="Exists('Packages/FunkeDefines.props')" />
</Project>
```
`global.json`: `{"sdk": {"version": "10.0.100", "rollForward": "latestFeature", "allowPrerelease": false}}`.

Compiling by hand: `dotnet build <Name>.csproj -c Release` puts the DLL in `bin/Release/`. Without `-p:DefineConstants` the editor define set (`FUNKE_EDITOR`) is compiled in. That's fine for a quick check, but `funke run` compiles with the shipped `FUNKE_BUILD` defines. If its own configuration's DLL is missing, the runtime loads **any** `bin/*/<Name>.dll` it finds, so a stale Debug DLL can run silently.
