# Funke logs for agents

Funke writes plain-text logs:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Windows log per executable | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\Logs\<exe>.log` (`Funke-Editor.log`, `Funke-Launcher.log`, `Funke-Runtime.log`, or the shipped game's exe name). Active file plus up to three rotated backups (`<exe>.1.log` through `<exe>.3.log`), 10 MiB each. Appends across runs. |
| Windows crash dumps | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\CrashDumps\<exe>_<FNK_BUILD_ID>_<timestamp>.dmp` (written by `Funke-Engine/src/Core/CrashReporter.cpp`) |
| Other native platforms | File logs use `Path::GetSpecialFolderPath(SpecialFolder::LocalAppData)/Funke/Logs`, backed by the platform's user-data root. Linux/macOS crash reports are `<exe>-<timestamp>.crash.txt` under its `Funke/CrashDumps` folder. |
| Android / Web | Android also writes logcat tag `Funke` (`adb logcat -s Funke`). Web uses the browser console; it deliberately creates no log file. |

Line format: `[HH:MM:SS] [<logger>] [<level>] [<Tag>] message` — logger is `FUNKE` (engine), `APP` (client) or `EDITOR`; level is `trace|debug|info|warning|error|critical`. Warn and above flush immediately; info may lag until shutdown.

## Recipes

- Problems only: Grep `\] \[(warning|error|critical)\] ` in the log file.
- One subsystem: Grep `\[Tag\]`, e.g. `\[AssetRegistry\]`, `\[SceneSerializer\]`, `\[ScriptSystem\]`.
- Only the latest session: start from the last `Funke Engine <version>` / `Initializing...` line.
- Reproduce and capture cleanly: `scripts\dev\Run.ps1` — it records only the run's lines into `bin-int\_agent\run\<App>.log` and lists new crash dumps.
- Several editors open: `scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 logs --level warning -Project <dir>` selects one editor's process-local log buffer; the shared file can mix sessions from multiple processes.

Read logs proactively when the user reports a runtime bug or after you changed code and need proof a path executed. Not needed for pure code questions.

# Funke Profiler

Two layers fed by the same macros (`Funke-Engine/src/Profiling/Profiler.hpp`):

1. **Tracy** (`External/tracy` submodule, built as a shared `Tracy` DLL, `TRACY_ON_DEMAND`): every scope/value/frame mark, whether or not a module exists. Connect a Tracy viewer over TCP to see it; its version must match the submodule's (`External/tracy/public/common/TracyVersion.hpp`, 0.13.x at the time of writing — the "v0.11.1" in `premake/dependencies/tracy.lua` is stale), otherwise the viewer refuses the connection.
2. **In-engine ring buffers** (`ProfilerModule`): per-name sample history that the editor/runtime **Profiler panel** draws. A push only lands if the name is a registered module and every gate passes (see below).

## Compile gate

- `FUNKE_PROFILER_ENABLED` (+ `TRACY_ENABLE`, `TRACY_IMPORTS`, `TRACY_ON_DEMAND`) comes from `Dependency.Profiler` in `Dependencies.lua`, applied by `UseFunkeProfilerDependencies()` in `premake5.lua` to **Debug and Release only**. **Dist never has the profiler.**
- `premake5 ... --no-profiler` strips it from every config (`FunkeProfiler.Enabled = false`): `src/Profiling/**` is removed from `Funke-Engine`, Tracy isn't built or copied, and `Tracy.dll` is deleted from outputs.
- When stripped, the macros are `((void)0)` and `Profiler` becomes inline no-op stubs, so **macro call sites and plain `Profiler::` calls need no `#ifdef`**. Anything that names `GpuTimer`, `ProfilerScopedSample` or Tracy symbols directly must be inside `#ifdef FUNKE_PROFILER_ENABLED` (see `Renderer2D.hpp` / `Renderer2D.cpp`).
- Native package layers get the same defines via `premake/package-loader.lua`, so packages can use the macros too.

## Macros

```cpp
#include "Profiling/Profiler.hpp"

void PhysicsSystem2D::FixedUpdate(float dt) {
	FUNKE_PROFILE_SCOPE("Physics");                 // Tracy zone + ms sample on scope exit
	...
}

FUNKE_PROFILE_VALUE("Batches", float(drawCalls));  // TracyPlot + numeric push (counts, MB)
FUNKE_PROFILE_FRAME("Frame");                       // Tracy frame mark — already done once per frame in Application::Run
FUNKE_PROFILE_THREAD_NAME("FileWatcher");           // names the current thread in Tracy (call at thread start)
```

- `FUNKE_PROFILE_SCOPE(name)` uses `ZoneTransientN` + a `__LINE__`-suffixed RAII `ProfilerScopedSample`, so two scopes on different lines of one function are fine; two on the **same line** collide. `name` must be a `const char*` that outlives the scope (string literal).
- Don't add another `FUNKE_PROFILE_FRAME`; `Application.cpp` emits it once per frame and `Profiler::OnFrameMark` is currently a no-op hook.
- Direct API when you already have the number: `Profiler::PushSample(name, ms)` (e.g. `Renderer2D::RenderSceneWithVP` pushes `"Rendering"`), `Profiler::PushValue(name, value)`.

## Modules

`Profiler::Initialize()` (called early in `Application` startup, before the job system and renderer) **clears the table** and registers the built-ins:

| Group | Module names |
|---|---|
| Internal | `Frame Time` (from `PushFrameDelta`; feeds the `Others` residual) |
| CPU Usage | `Rendering`, `Scripts`, `Physics`, `VSync`, `Others` |
| Rendering | `Batches`, `Triangles`, `Vertices`, `Rendered Sprites` |
| Memory | `Total Memory`, `Texture Memory`, `Entity Count` |
| Audio | `Playing Sources` |
| Animation | `Animator`, `SkinnedMeshAnimation` (ms), `Animator Poses`, `Skinned Poses` (how many animations wrote a pose this frame — culling / distance rate) |
| GPU | `GPU` (published by `GpuTimer`; not in the panel layout) |
| Frame breakdown | `UpdateScenes`, `OnPreRenderScenes`, `Renderer2D.Begin/End/Collect/Sort/Upload/Submit`, `GuiRenderer.Begin/End`, `GizmoRenderer.Begin/End`, `Layer.OnUpdate/OnPreRender/OnPostRender`, `SwapBuffers` |
| Gate diagnostics | `Editor.HierarchyRebuild`, `TransformHierarchy`, `UILayout`, `UIEvent.Update/RefResolve/HitTest/Visuals/Widgets`, `ParticleUpdate`, `UIFocus`, `ManagedSceneSystem` |

Adding a module:

- **Engine-owned, permanent:** add the name to the `names[]` list in `Profiler::Initialize()` (`Profiling/Profiler.cpp`), in the right group.
- **Ad hoc / package:** `Profiler::Register("MyMetric")` — idempotent, returns the existing module. Must run **after** `Profiler::Initialize()`; a `Register` done earlier is wiped. Returns `nullptr` in stripped builds.
- A scope or value whose name isn't registered still produces Tracy data but is dropped from the ring buffer — that is fine for Tracy-only zones (`"Hierarchy Panel"`, `"Editor PreRender"` in the editor are unregistered on purpose). Names are matched byte-for-byte.

## When samples land

`PushValue`/`PushSample` (mutex-protected, any thread) record only when **all** hold:

1. the module exists and `Enabled` (panel toggle; disabling also clears its buffer),
2. the panel is visible (`Profiler::SetPanelVisible`, driven by `ProfilerPanel::Render`) **or** background tracking is on (`SetBackgroundTracking`),
3. **the application is playing and not paused** (`Application::GetIsPlaying()` / `IsPaused()`) — in edit mode the panel stays empty by design; tests without an `Application` skip this gate,
4. the per-module rate gate passed: at most `SamplingHz` samples/s per module (`SetSamplingHz`, default 60; `<= 0` = unlimited).

`SetTrackingSpan(n)` (default 200) sets ring-buffer length. Tracy ignores all of these gates.

## GPU timing

`Profiling/GpuTimer.{hpp,cpp}`: WebGPU timestamp queries (`wgpu::FeatureName::TimestampQuery`), 3-slot ring, results pushed to the `"GPU"` module in ms. Owned by `Renderer2D` (`m_GpuTimer`) and attached to the sprite pass via `PassTimestampWrites`. Lifecycle is order-sensitive: `BeginFrameWrites()` before `BeginRenderPass`, `ResolveCurrentFrame(encoder)` after `pass.End()`, `PollAndPublish()` in `EndFrame`, `OnFrameStart()` only from `Renderer2D::OnAfterPresent()` (issuing `MapAsync` earlier races the frame's Submit and Dawn rejects it). Availability depends on `WebGPUBackend::HasTimestampQuery()` for the selected device; don't infer it from the backend name alone. Reuse it; don't hand-roll query sets. `GpuTimer::QueryGpuMemoryMb()` returns -1 (no portable WebGPU query).

## Profiler panel

- `Funke-Editor/src/Gui/ProfilerPanel.{hpp,cpp}`, owned by `ImGuiEditorLayer` (`m_ProfilerPanel`, toggled with **Ctrl+F6** in `ImGuiEditorLayerChrome.cpp`). The same `.cpp` is compiled into `Funke-Runtime` (see `Funke-Runtime/premake5.lua`) and shown by `RuntimeProfilerLayer` on Ctrl+F6 when the project sets `profiler.enableInRuntime`. Without `FUNKE_PROFILER_ENABLED` it renders a "Profiler is disabled in this build" stub.
- **The panel does not list modules automatically.** It draws the hard-coded `GetCategoryLayout()` table (`{ RegisteredName, DisplayLabel, Unit }` per row, grouped by header). To show a new module add a row there; unit `"ms"` for durations, `"MB"` for memory, `""` for counts (shown as integers). Rows whose module isn't registered are skipped silently.
- Settings persist in `<project>/project.json` under `"profiler"`: `enableInRuntime`, `trackInBackground`, `samplingHz`, `trackingSpan`, and `modules` (only modules the user disabled, as `name: false`). Written only when non-default (`FunkeProject.cpp`). New modules need no migration — absent means enabled.
- Panel UI conventions: `funke-add-editor-panel`.

## Pitfalls

- "Panel shows nothing" → not in Play mode, paused, panel collapsed, module disabled, or name not registered/not in the layout table.
- Registering in a static initializer or before `Application` init → wiped by `Profiler::Initialize()`.
- `Profiler::AllModules()` deep-copies every ring buffer; in per-frame code use the `AllModules(std::vector<ProfilerModule>&)` overload.
- Mixing `TRACY_ON_DEMAND` on/off between Tracy and its consumers corrupts zones (comment in `Dependencies.lua`) — don't touch those defines piecemeal.
- Long editor sessions without `TRACY_ON_DEMAND` grew to multiple GB; it must stay on.
- One-off timing that won't be committed: `Timer` / `ScopedTimer` (`funke-debug`).

# Funke Assets & Content

Content in Funke is **discovered, not imported**: drop a file into the project's `Assets/` folder and the engine assigns it a permanent **GUID**. Everything references content by GUID, never by path, so you can move/rename freely. This skill covers the asset model, how to reference and load content from C#, the per-type asset classes, and **Data Assets** (shared game data).

## The asset model

- **No import wizard.** Files in `Assets/` are scanned and classified by extension into an `AssetKind`:

  | Kind | Extensions | Use |
  |---|---|---|
  | Texture | `.png .jpg .jpeg .bmp .tga` | sprites/images |
  | Audio | `.wav .mp3 .ogg .flac` (Ogg Vorbis; Opus can't be decoded) | sfx/music |
  | Font | `.ttf .otf` | text |
  | Scene | `.scene` | a level/screen |
  | Prefab | `.prefab` | reusable entity |
  | Script | `.cs` (+ C/C++) | game logic |
  | Shader | `.wgsl .vert .frag …` | custom rendering |
  | Data Asset | `.dataasset` | shared game data |
  | Material | `.material` | shader + parameters |
  | Mesh | `.obj .gltf .glb` | 3D models |
  | AnimationClip | `.anim` | keyframe animation |
  | AnimatorController | `.animctrl` | animation state machine |
  | Other | anything else | tracked, unhandled |

- **GUID + `.meta`.** Each asset gets a 64-bit GUID stored in a `<file>.meta` JSON sidecar (GUID + import settings like texture filter/wrap and sprite slices). **Keep and commit `.meta` files; move them with their asset.** A regenerated `.meta` gets a *new* GUID and breaks existing references.
- **Built-in engine assets** (default font, default white/circle/etc. textures) have fixed stable GUIDs identical on every machine.
- **File-based runtime assets.** Textures/audio are loaded on demand and cached behind handles. The build stages project content, can prune unused assets, and converts staged scenes, prefabs and Data Assets to binary; platform packaging may then bundle those files (for example, inside an Android APK). The source assets remain editable. Build details: `funke-build-and-ship`.

## Referencing content from C#

Two idioms — prefer the first.

**1. Inspector slot (the normal way).** Declare a typed field; the Editor shows an asset picker; the engine stores the GUID with the scene. Drag the asset onto the slot.

```csharp
public class Pickup : EntityScript
{
    public Texture? Icon;      // texture picker
    public Audio?   PickupSfx; // audio picker

    public override void OnStart()
    {
        if (Icon != null) GetComponent<SpriteRenderer>()!.Texture = Icon;
    }
}
```
(Slot/attribute rules — `[ShowInEditor]`, read-only, etc. — are in `funke-inspector-ruleset`.)

**2. Load in code via `AssetManager` (static).**

```csharp
T? Load<T>(string path) where T : class;          // path resolved to a GUID internally
T? LoadByGUID<T>(ulong guid) where T : class;     // also a string-GUID overload
IReadOnlyList<T> FindAll<T>(string pathPrefix = "") where T : class;  // every asset of a kind, optionally under a folder
ulong GetGUID(string path);                        // path → GUID
```
```csharp
Texture? tex = AssetManager.Load<Texture>("Sprites/player.png");
var allItems = AssetManager.FindAll<ItemData>();              // great for building catalogs at startup
```

Under the hood everything is GUID-based; the path form just looks up the GUID. References saved in scenes/prefabs/components are always GUIDs. Paths are relative to `Assets/`. `T` can be `Texture`, `Audio`, `Font`, `Material`, `Mesh`, `AnimationClip`, `AnimatorController`, a `DataAsset` subclass, or `Entity` for a prefab; anything else returns `null` / empty.

## Asset classes (`Funke.*`)

### `Texture`
```csharp
ulong UUID;  bool IsValid;  bool IsRuntime;  string Name;  string Path;  int Width;  int Height;
static Texture? FromAssetUUID(ulong assetId);
// Built-in shapes (stable GUIDs): Texture.Square / Pixel / Circle / Capsule /
//   IsometricDiamond / HexagonFlatTop / HexagonPointedTop / NineSliced / Invisible
// Procedural runtime textures:
static Texture? Create(int w, int h, TextureFilter filter = TextureFilter.Point);
void SetPixel(Vector2Int cell, Color c);  Color GetPixel(Vector2Int cell);
void SetPixels(Color[] rowMajor);  Color[] GetPixels();  void Apply();   // upload CPU buffer → GPU
bool SaveToPng(string path);  void Dispose();                            // runtime textures aren't GC'd — Dispose them
```
`TextureFilter`: `Point | Bilinear | Trilinear | Anisotropic | Default`.

### `Audio`
```csharp
ulong UUID;  bool IsValid;  string Name;  string Path;
static Audio? FromAssetUUID(ulong assetId);
void PlayOneShot(float volume = 1.0f);     // fire-and-forget
```
For looping/positional/controllable playback use the **`AudioSource`** component (`Play/Pause/Stop/Resume`, `Volume`, `Pitch`, `Loop`) — see `funke-game-scripting`.

### `Font`
```csharp
ulong UUID;  bool IsValid;  string Name;  string Path;
static Font? FromAssetUUID(ulong assetId);
```
Assign to a `TextRenderer.Font`. Fonts are cached per pixel size.

`TextureRef` / `AudioRef` are thin GUID wrappers used in serialization; you normally just use the `Texture` / `Audio` field types directly.

## Data Assets — shared game data (ScriptableObject equivalent)

When many objects should read the **same** data edited in **one** place (item/enemy/stat definitions, loot tables, dialogue, difficulty presets), use a **Data Asset**. The class is the template; each `.dataasset` file is one filled-in instance with its own GUID. The engine keeps **one shared live instance per file**.

### Define the class

```csharp
using Funke;

[CreateDataAsset("Gameplay/Item Data")]   // adds a Create → Data Asset → Gameplay/Item Data menu entry
public class ItemData : DataAsset
{
    public string DisplayName = "New Item";
    public int    MaxStack    = 99;
    [ClampValue(0f, 1000f)] public float Weight = 1.0f;
    public Color   Tint = Color.White;
    public Texture? Icon;
    public RarityData? Rarity;            // a Data Asset can reference another Data Asset

    public override void OnValidate()     // runs after edit-in-editor or load-from-disk
    {
        if (MaxStack < 1) MaxStack = 1;
    }
}
```
- Base class: `public abstract class DataAsset` (in `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Scene/DataAsset.cs`); override `OnValidate()`.
- `[CreateDataAsset(menuPath)]` (`menuPath` is slash-separated; default `""`). Without it the class still works but won't appear in the create menu.
- **Field types** = the same set as script fields: primitives, `string`, enums, `Vector2/3/4`, `Color`, `Graph`, `Texture`/`Audio`/`Material`/`Mesh`/`Scene`, prefabs (`Entity`), **other `DataAsset` subclasses**, lists of those and `List<PlainClass>` inline objects. `Font`, `Dictionary` and other generic types are silently not serialized. Inspector attributes apply (`[ClampValue]`, `[Header]`, `[ToolTip]`, …).

### Create & reference

- **Editor:** Asset Browser → right-click → **Create → Data Asset → <your menu path>** → name it → edit fields in the Inspector.
- **From a script (slot):** `public ItemData? Item;` shows a Data Asset picker; reference saved by GUID.
- **From code:** `AssetManager.Load<ItemData>("Items/Sword.dataasset")` or `AssetManager.FindAll<ItemData>("Items/Weapons")`.

### On disk
A `.dataasset` stores the class `type` name, a format `version`, and the field values (JSON or binary per the project's `assetSerializationFormat`). Hot reload re-creates instances from disk and replays field values (creating all first, so cross-references resolve).

File format, list encodings, generator helpers and patterns (enemy types, waves, levels, catalogs): `funke-make-a-game` → `references/data-driven.md`.

**Data Asset vs alternatives:** shared data decoupled from entities → **Data Asset**; a reusable *entity* with components/children → **Prefab**; per-instance values on one entity → **plain script fields**.

## Hot reload & purging (editor)

- Editing a `.png`/`.ttf`/`.wav` on disk re-decodes and re-uploads it live; Asset Browser thumbnails refresh. The shipped runtime reads files once (no hot reload).
- Managers cache loaded assets behind generation-checked handles. Texture purging preserves built-ins, runtime textures, direct scene references, indirect material/3D-particle texture references, and registered reference providers. Runtime textures remain owned by their script `Texture` objects and must be disposed explicitly.

## Pitfalls

- **Never hard-code GUIDs or fragile paths** when an Inspector slot will do — slots keep references stable across moves/renames.
- **Lost `.meta` = broken references.** Treat `.meta` as part of the asset; commit it.
- **Runtime `Texture` objects must be `Dispose()`d** — they hold a GPU resource and are not garbage-collected.
- **New projects serialize as JSON**; older projects (or a `project.json` without `assetSerializationFormat`) are Binary and their `.dataasset`/`.scene` files aren't human-readable until converted (`funke convert --format json`, see `funke-project-structure`).
- **`SpriteRenderer.Color` is a `Vector4`**, but `Color` (struct, with presets like `Color.White`) is what most APIs and Data Asset fields use — convert deliberately.

## Related skills
`funke-game-scripting` (using assets at runtime), `funke-inspector-ruleset` (asset-slot attributes), `funke-project-structure` (on-disk layout & formats), `funke-build-and-ship` (staging, pruning and platform packaging).

# Funke Package System

Funke's extensibility model: anything the core doesn't ship lives in a **package**. Packages have a manifest (`funke-package.lua`), build into one or two DLLs (`Pkg.<Name>.Native` and/or `Pkg.<Name>`), and are loaded at runtime by `PackageHost`. The system is two-rooted (engine-shipped packages live at `<repo>/packages/`, project-local packages at `<project>/Packages/`), and a separate cloud registry serves a third install path for end users. `<repo>/packages/` is empty today: the official `Funke.*` packages (Tilemap2D, Serialization, AudioMixer, Cryptography, Physics, Ads, …) live in the `Ben-Scr/Funke-PackageRegistry` repo — read their sources there when this skill says "Tilemap2D-style".

This skill covers the whole pipeline. Source of truth for the loader is `premake/package-loader.lua` — when the rules below contradict that file, the file wins.

**Not covered here: platform packages.** Manifests with `kind = "platform"` or `"build-component"` (`platforms/Funke.Platform.*`, `platforms/Funke.ScriptRuntime.Mono`) add export targets, not game features: no `layers`, a `builder` script speaking the Funke Platform Builder protocol instead. premake ignores them; `Project/PlatformPackages.cpp` discovers them. See `funke-build-and-ship` → *Android, iOS, Web* and `Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Platform-Packages.md`.

## The three layers

A package declares one or more layers under `manifest.layers`. **Canonical names** (use these in new manifests):

| Layer | Builds | Links the engine? | Default refs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `native` | `Pkg.<Name>.Native` (C++ SharedLib) | Yes (via `EditorRuntimeCommon`) | Engine include set, `FNK_IMPORT_DLL`, `FUNKE_ENTITY_BITS=…` |
| `native_standalone` | Same `Pkg.<Name>.Native` SharedLib | **No** — pure C++, no engine symbols | None |
| `csharp` | `Pkg.<Name>` (C# net10.0 SharedLib) | n/a | Auto-links `Funke-ScriptCore` |

**Deprecated aliases** (still loaded but warned): `engine_core` → `native`, `standalone_cpp` → `native_standalone`. The loader normalises them before validation. Rename old manifests, don't add new ones with the old names.

**Hard rule:** `native` and `native_standalone` **cannot coexist** in the same package. They would merge into a single `Pkg.<Name>.Native` DLL, but `native` links the engine and `native_standalone` is the explicit "no engine link" path — combining them silently links the engine into "standalone" sources and defeats the whole point. The loader fails loud (`PackageError` in [package-loader.lua](../../../premake/package-loader.lua)). `NewPackage.py` rejects the combo upfront too.

## Manifest schema

`packages/<Name>/funke-package.lua` returns a table:

```lua
return {
    name        = "Funke.Hello",       -- required, PascalCase.PascalCase[…], must match folder name in practice
    version     = "0.1.0",             -- required, SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-pre]
    description = "Hello world.",      -- optional
    engine      = ">=2026.1.0",        -- optional engine version range (npm syntax)

    layers = {                         -- required, at least one layer
        native = {
            sources          = { "src/**.cpp", "src/**.hpp", "include/**.hpp" },   -- required list
            includes         = { "include" },                                       -- optional, public-ish
            private_includes = { "src" },                                           -- optional
        },
        csharp = {
            sources      = { "Source/**.cs" },
            pinvoke_dll  = "Pkg.Funke.Hello.Native",   -- only when bridging to native sibling
            allow_unsafe = true,                        -- enables `clr "Unsafe"` for fixed-pin pinvoke
            nuget        = { "System.Text.Json:8.0.0" }, -- optional PackageReferences (keep short)
        },
    },

    -- optional; "Name", "Name@range", { name = ..., version = range } or ["Name"] = range
    dependencies = { "Funke.Foo", "Funke.Bar@^1.2.0" },

    -- optional; engine modules the package builds on. Install enables them; a project with one off
    -- doesn't load the package, GameBuilder refuses the build, and the module can't be removed under it.
    -- Omit when only core APIs (UI, text, audio, input, assets) are used.
    modules = { "Funke.2D" },
}
```

Manifests are parsed by Lua (premake) **and** by a literal-only reader in C++ (`Packages/PackageManifest.cpp`, used by PackageHost and the editor): keep them plain data, with no function calls, string concatenation or variables, or the editor and runtime ignore the package.

**Validation rules enforced by the loader** (all fail-loud with `[Funke Packages]` prefix):

- `name` needs dot-separated alphanumeric segments, each starting uppercase, with at least one dot. `NewPackage.py` additionally requires at least two characters per segment (`^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+(\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+)+$`); the Lua loader accepts single-letter segments. Use names accepted by both, such as `Funke.Foo` or `MyGame.Loot.Combat`.
- Layer names must be `native` / `native_standalone` / `csharp` (or the deprecated aliases).
- Every layer must declare a non-empty `sources` list.
- `pinvoke_dll` on the csharp layer requires a sibling native layer and must equal `Pkg.<manifest.name>.Native` exactly.
- `nuget` entries must be `"PackageId:Version"` strings.
- `dependencies` entries need valid names and ranges, no self-reference, no duplicates. The loader topologically sorts; cyclic deps, missing deps and an installed version outside a declared range fail loud. A non-SemVer `version` only warns, but any dependent with a range on it then fails.
- `modules` must be a list of known module ids (`Funke.2D`, `Funke.3D`); module ids are not package names, so never put them in `dependencies`. `NewPackage.py --modules Funke.2D` scaffolds it.
- `engine` must parse as a range and accept the engine's `FNK_VERSION` (pre-release suffix ignored), read from `Funke-Engine/src/Core/BuildMetadata.generated.hpp`.
- The same rules (SemVer, ranges, pre-release opt-in) are implemented twice: Lua in `package-loader.lua` (self-test: `vendor\bin\premake5.exe --file=premake/tests/package-loader-tests.lua funke-test-packages`) and C++ in `Packages/SemanticVersion.cpp` / `PackageResolver.cpp` (doctest `PackageVersioningTests.cpp`). Change both together.
- Duplicate package names across `packages/` and `<project>/Packages/` fail loud.

## The two roots

| Root | Who ships it | Generated into |
|---|---|---|
| `<repo>/packages/<Name>/` | Engine-shipped | `Funke.sln` (engine `premake5 vs2022`): every package, no allow-list |
| `<project>/Packages/<Name>/` | Per-project (local, or installed from the registry by the editor) | The project's own package workspace `<project>/.funke/build/packages/`, generated by `premake/project-packages.lua` |

Generate a project's package workspace (NewPackage.py, RemovePackage.py and the editor run this for you; the editor's code path is `FunkeProject::RegeneratePackageWorkspaceForProject` + `BuildProjectPackages`):

```sh
./vendor/bin/premake5.exe --file=premake/project-packages.lua --funke-project="C:/path/to/MyProject" vs2022
```

The path must be absolute. The workspace registers the project's enabled packages from both roots. On the engine workspace (`premake5.lua`) `--funke-project` only selects `entityBits`; it no longer registers project packages.

## The project allow-list

In the project package workspace and at runtime (`PackageHost`), `<project>/project.json` is the source of truth for which packages register and load:

```jsonc
{
  "packages": [
    "Funke.Tilemap2D",
    "MyGame.Loot"
  ]
}
```

Behaviour (`ResolveProjectPackages` / `FilterManifestsByAllowList` in `package-loader.lua`):

- **Field present and non-empty** → only listed packages are registered. Transitive dependencies are auto-included so listing `B` (which deps on `A`) pulls `A` along.
- **Field present and empty `[]`** → no packages registered (fresh-project state).
- **Field absent / `project.json` missing** → fail closed (no packages registered). This is deliberate — without an explicit list we don't know what the project intends.
- **Engine workspace (`Funke.sln`)** → no filter: every package under `<repo>/packages/` is registered.

Skipped packages get a one-line `[Funke Packages] Skipped N package(s)…` log. Allow-list entries that don't resolve to a manifest get a `WARNING: project lists package 'X' but no manifest…`.

## Build outputs

For each registered package (`<cfg>` = e.g. `Release-windows-x86_64`; engine packages under the repo root, project packages under `<project>/.funke/build/packages/`):

- `native` and/or `native_standalone` → one `Pkg.<Name>.Native` project (C++ SharedLib, C++20, /Zc:preprocessor, MultiProcessorCompile).
  - Output: `bin/<cfg>/Pkg.<Name>.Native/Pkg.<Name>.Native.dll`, plus the `.funkeabi` sidecar written by a post-build step (see *Runtime loading*)
  - Intermediate: `bin-int/<cfg>/Pkg.<Name>.Native/`
  - Generated vcxproj: `premake/generated/Pkg.<Name>.Native/` (project packages: `generated/Pkg.<Name>.Native/`)
- `csharp` → one `Pkg.<Name>` project (C# SharedLib, net10.0, Nullable enabled, EnableDynamicLoading true, AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath=false).
  - Output: `bin/<cfg>/Pkg.<Name>/Pkg.<Name>.dll`
  - Implicit references: `Funke-ScriptCore` (always — don't add it as a dependency manually; the project workspace links the engine's built `Funke-ScriptCore.dll` per configuration).

Configurations: `Debug` / `Release` / `Dist`. The Dist config strips symbols and is what shipped runtimes use.

## Runtime loading

`Funke-Engine/src/Core/PackageHost.{hpp,cpp}` is the runtime side:

- `PackageHost::LoadAll()` collects `Pkg.<Name>.Native` libraries from the project workspace (`<project>/.funke/build/packages/bin/<editor cfg>-…/`), prebuilt `<project>/Packages/<Name>/Bin/<Platform>-<Arch>/`, the folder above the exe (`bin/<cfg>/Pkg.<Name>.Native/`) and `<exeDir>/Packages/`, then `LoadLibrary` / `dlopen`s only those in the project's resolved allow-list. No project or an empty list loads nothing; `FUNKE_LOAD_ALL_PACKAGES=1` overrides the list for engine development. Idempotent.
- `PackageHost::LoadInstalled()` is the editor's "I just installed a package — pick up the new DLLs without restarting" hook, with the same filter.
- **ABI check (Windows):** each native library needs the `<dll>.funkeabi` sidecar its premake post-build writes (`boundary=standalone_c`, or `engine_cpp` + the SHA-256 of the `Funke-Engine.dll` it was linked against). Missing sidecar or another engine hash → `Skipping native package '…': … Rebuild the package against this engine version.` This is the usual "package doesn't load" after an engine rebuild; the editor rebuilds stale project source packages on open (`PackageHost::FindStaleProjectNativePackages`, `EditorApplication.cpp`).
- Before loading, `ResolvePackages` (`Packages/PackageResolver.hpp`) resolves `project.json`'s list against the manifests in `<engine>/packages` and `<project>/Packages`: transitive dependencies are added, DLLs load dependencies-first, and a package with a missing/out-of-range dependency or an incompatible `engine` is skipped together with its dependents (logged as `[PackageHost]` errors). Listed packages without a manifest (shipped games stage only DLLs) load afterwards in project order.
- `packages-lock.json` (project root, `Packages/PackageLock.hpp`) is rewritten by the editor after every package change: exact versions plus source (registry URL + SHA-256, git, local, engine). The Package Manager's **Restore locked versions** re-downloads missing registry entries from it.
- Each loaded module is queried for `FunkePackage_OnLoad` (and optionally `FunkePackage_OnUnload`). Both are pure C entry points.
- `PackageHost::UnloadAll()` runs `FunkePackage_OnUnload` (if present) and frees modules in reverse order. Called at app shutdown.

### The native entry point

Provide this entry point when the package initializes engine state. Desktop DLL loading accepts a missing `FunkePackage_OnLoad` and logs that no initialization export exists; the Android/iOS/Web static-package builder requires it in the native sources:

```cpp
#include "Packages/PackageApi.hpp"
#include "Core/Log.hpp"

extern "C" FUNKE_PACKAGE_API int FunkePackage_OnLoad() {
    FNK_INFO_TAG("Pkg.Funke.Hello", "Loaded.");
    return 0;   // non-zero is logged but the module stays loaded
}

extern "C" FUNKE_PACKAGE_API void FunkePackage_OnUnload() {
    // optional
}
```

`PackageApi.hpp` declares both, so the signatures must match exactly (`void` OnUnload; `int` would be a C2371 redefinition).

`FUNKE_PACKAGE_API` is the package export marker — see `Funke-Engine/src/Packages/PackageApi.hpp`. It is always `__declspec(dllexport)` on Windows and default symbol visibility elsewhere; it has no import-mode switch. `PackageHost` resolves desktop exports dynamically. Don't substitute `FUNKE_API` for it.

For `native_standalone` packages, `FNK_*_TAG` logging is **unavailable** (no engine link). Use `std::printf` or a self-contained logger.

## The Package API

Inside `FunkePackage_OnLoad`, packages typically register components and systems via helpers in `Packages/PackageRegistration.hpp`:

```cpp
#include "MyComponent.hpp"
#include "Inspector/PropertyRegistration.hpp"
#include "Packages/PackageRegistration.hpp"

extern "C" FUNKE_PACKAGE_API int FunkePackage_OnLoad() {
    using namespace Funke;

    std::vector<PropertyDescriptor> props = {
        Properties::Make("Value",     "Value",      &MyComponent::Value),
        Properties::Make("TintColor", "Tint Color", &MyComponent::TintColor),
    };

    Package::RegisterSerializableComponent<MyComponent>(
        /* displayName    */ "My Component",
        /* subcategory    */ "Gameplay",
        /* serializedName */ "MyComponent",
        /* drawInspector  */ nullptr,   // null = unified auto-drawer
        /* serialize      */ nullptr,   // optional; see funke-serialize-field skill
        /* deserialize    */ nullptr,
        /* category       */ ComponentCategory::Component,
        /* properties     */ std::move(props),
        /* icon           */ "particles");  // optional editor icon stem from FunkeAssets/Textures/Editor/General

    // Optional mutual exclusion. Declare on either side — registry checks both.
    Package::DeclareComponentConflict<MyComponent, Funke::SpriteRendererComponent>();

    return 0;
}
```

For the full inspector ruleset (PropertyType, ReferencePicker, ShowInEditor, conflicts), defer to the `funke-inspector-ruleset` skill. The component pipeline (registry sites, lifecycle hooks, C# bindings) is in `funke-add-component`.

## Bridging C# to native (P/Invoke)

When a package declares both a native layer and a csharp layer **with `pinvoke_dll`**, the csharp side calls into the native sibling via P/Invoke.

The conventions:

1. **Library name** — set `pinvoke_dll = "Pkg.<Name>.Native"` in the manifest. In C# use the same string as the `DllImport` library name. Don't include a path or extension — `Funke.Interop.PackageNativeResolver` in Funke-ScriptCore resolves it by probing the engine's bin tree and the project's `Packages/` folder.
2. **Export prefix** — prefix every C export with `<Name with underscores>_` so symbols don't collide across packages. `Funke.Tilemap2D` → `Funke_Tilemap2D_GetTile`, `MyGame.Loot` → `MyGame_Loot_DropTable`.
3. **Calling convention** — always `CallingConvention.Cdecl` on the C# side; `extern "C"` on the C++ side. Match primitive types exactly.
4. **Unsafe blocks** — set `allow_unsafe = true` on the csharp layer to enable `clr "Unsafe"`. Required for `fixed` / `Span` / pointer-based bindings.

Example native binding:

```cpp
// src/MyPInvoke.cpp
#include "Packages/PackageApi.hpp"
#include <cstdint>

extern "C" FUNKE_PACKAGE_API
int32_t Funke_Hello_Ping() { return 1; }
```

Mirrored on the C# side:

```csharp
// Source/NativeBindings.cs
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
namespace Funke.Hello;

internal static class NativeBindings {
    private const string Lib = "Pkg.Funke.Hello.Native";

    [DllImport(Lib, EntryPoint = "Funke_Hello_Ping",
               CallingConvention = CallingConvention.Cdecl)]
    public static extern int Ping();
}
```

**The binding surface MUST match on both sides** — names, calling convention, signatures. There's no tooling that cross-checks it; a mismatch surfaces as a runtime `EntryPointNotFoundException` or stack corruption.

For component wrappers (managed `MyComponent : Component` with native state under the hood), follow the `Funke.Tilemap2D` pattern (source in `Funke-PackageRegistry`): per-field Get/Set bindings, pin spans with `fixed` for batch APIs, no parallel state on the managed side.

## Android, iOS, Web: native layers are linked statically

These players can't load package DLLs, so the platform builders compile `native` / `native_standalone` layers into the player (`libmain.so`, the iOS app, the wasm archive set):

- `scripts/platform/funke_platform_sdk/native_packages.py` (`prepare_native_packages`) reads the project's packages (dependencies first), expands the layer's sources/includes, scans `.cpp/.c` files for `FUNKE_PACKAGE_API` functions and writes `native-packages.json` + `FunkeStaticPackages.cpp` (defines `FunkeRegisterStaticPackages()`; on Android/iOS also a symbol table). Offline tests: `python -m unittest scripts.ci.test_native_packages`.
- `funke_add_native_packages(<target> JSON ...)` in `cmake/FunkeEngine.cmake` makes one STATIC `Pkg.<Name>.Native` per package (archive in `<build>/packages/`) with `-DFunkePackage_OnLoad=FunkePackage_OnLoad_<Name_Id>` (same for OnUnload) so entry points don't collide.
- The player mains call `FunkeRegisterStaticPackages()` → `Funke::StaticPackages` (`Packages/StaticPackages.hpp`); `PackageHost::LoadAll` runs their OnLoad before DLLs, `UnloadAll` their OnUnload. Mono's `PINVOKE_OVERRIDE` resolves `[DllImport("Pkg.<Name>.Native")]` via `StaticPackages::FindSymbol` (Android, iOS); the Web relink scans `Pkg.<Name>.Native.a` (`ScanForPInvokes`) and generates `pinvoke-table.h` itself.
- Rules for authors: every C#-called export carries `FUNKE_PACKAGE_API` in a `.cpp`; OnLoad must exist; don't rely on static initializers; keep helpers namespaced (one binary shared by all packages). Blittable P/Invoke signatures (pointers, ints) work everywhere.

## Package components in C# and engine hooks

- A managed wrapper `class Foo : Component` for a natively registered component needs `Entity.RegisterNativeComponent<Foo>("<display name>")`, called from a `[ModuleInitializer]` (`#pragma warning disable CA2255` around the attribute). ScriptCore runs a package module's initializer before a type lookup can miss (`Entity.EnsureModuleInitialized`). Property accessors use `RequireComponent<Foo>()` (returns the entity id).
- Native side: `Scripting/ScriptEntityReference.hpp` — `ResolveEntityReference(id, scene, handle)` and `GetEntityScriptId(scene, handle)`; C# turns ids back with `Entity.FromID(id)`.
- Runtime state next to the registry: `SceneExtensions::Register(SceneExtension{Name, OnSceneCreated, OnRuntimeStateInitialized, OnSceneDestroyed})` (`Scene/SceneExtensions.hpp`; hooks run for detached scenes too). A 2D physics backend: `PhysicsSystem2D::RegisterExtension(PhysicsExtension2D{...})` with `BodyComponent = entt::type_hash<Body>::value()`. Unregister both in OnUnload. Reference: `Funke.Physics` in the registry repo.

## Android contributions (Java, Maven AARs, manifest)

Besides native layers (above), Android SDKs (ads, billing, Play Games) come in through a top-level `android` table, read only by the Android builder (`platforms/Funke.Platform.Android/Builder/android_libraries.py`; premake and the C++ manifest reader ignore it, but it must stay plain data):

```lua
android = {
    java         = { "Android/Java/**.java" },                     -- Java 8 syntax, no lambdas (anonymous classes)
    maven        = { "com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads:25.5.0" },
    manifest     = "Android/AndroidManifest.xml",                 -- merged by android_manifest.py
    placeholders = { admobAppId = "ca-app-pub-3940256099942544~3347511713" },  -- ${admobAppId}; profile option overrides
},
```

- `maven` closures are resolved from POMs (Google Maven + Central, newest version wins, androidx constraints honoured) and **must be pinned**: `python platforms/Funke.Platform.Android/Builder/android_maven.py lock <packageDir>` writes `Android/maven.lock.json` (URL + SHA-256 per file). Without a lock matching the `maven` list the build re-resolves and warns.
- The builder links library resources as aapt2 overlays, regenerates each library package's `R` class from the app's `R.txt`, compiles package Java against all jars, dexes with d8 (multidex), copies `jni/arm64-v8a/*.so`, AAR assets and jar Java resources (`META-INF/services` merged).
- Java ↔ C#: Java exposes `public static String method(String)`; C# `AndroidBridge.Call(class, method, json)` (engine `Platform::CallJava` → `dev.funke.player.FunkeBridge.call`, class loaded via the activity's class loader). Java answers with `FunkeBridge.send(channel, json)` → `Platform::PushJavaMessage` → dispatched to `AndroidBridge.Subscribe` handlers each frame before coroutines. Off Android `Call` returns null; `AndroidBridge.Simulate` feeds handlers for editor stand-ins.
- Static state survives editor Play sessions; reset it in `Application.PlayModeExited`.
- Reference implementation: `Funke.Ads` in the `Funke-PackageRegistry` repo (C# facade + simulated/Android/unsupported backends, `FunkeAds.java`, manifest meta-data from `admobAppId`). Offline tests: `python -m unittest scripts.ci.test_android_builder`.

## Scaffolding new packages

Don't hand-write the boilerplate. Use the scaffolder:

```sh
# Engine-shipped native-only:
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py Funke.Foo

# Engine-shipped csharp-only (Serialization-style pure managed):
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py Funke.Foo --layers csharp

# Native + C# bridged (Tilemap2D-style):
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py Funke.Foo --layers native+csharp

# Same, plus an example component end-to-end (.hpp/.cpp/.cs/PInvoke):
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py Funke.Foo --layers native+csharp --component Health

# Project-local (also adds to project.json packages array):
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py MyGame.Loot --layers native+csharp \
    --project "C:/Users/me/Funke/Projects/MyGame"

# Skip premake regen (CI / batch):
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py Funke.Foo --no-premake

# With dependencies on other packages (optional @range per entry):
python scripts/packages/NewPackage.py Funke.Foo --depends-on Funke.Bar@^1.0.0,Funke.Baz
```

`--layers` shorthand: `native` → `native`, `standalone` → `native_standalone`, `csharp` → `csharp`. Separate with `,` or `+`.

`--component Health` is the recommended starter for gameplay packages — it scaffolds `HealthComponent.{hpp,cpp,cs}`, the matching `Properties::Make` registration, and the Get/Set P/Invoke surface. The name must NOT include a trailing `Component` (the scaffolder adds it).

After creation the scaffolder regenerates projects — `premake5 vs2022` for engine packages, `premake/project-packages.lua --funke-project=…` with `--project` — and, for a csharp layer, runs `dotnet restore` on the generated `Pkg.<Name>.csproj` (the mixed engine solution can't be restored by the .NET CLI). Pass `--no-premake` to skip that.

Sibling scripts: `scripts/packages/RemovePackage.py` (deletes the dir + allow-list entry + reruns premake) and `scripts/packages/BumpPackageVersion.py` (rewrites the `version` line).

## Cloud registry

End users install packages via the editor's Package Manager, which fetches a static `index.json` from the public registry:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ben-Scr/Funke-PackageRegistry/main/index.json
```

Hardcoded as `k_FunkeRegistryUrl` in `Funke-Editor/src/Gui/PackageManagerPanel.cpp`.

The registry is a separate GitHub repo whose `index.json` lists available packages with download URLs and SHA-256 hashes. The editor:

1. Fetches `index.json` via `Funke-PackageTool registry-fetch <url> <cache.json>` (atomic write: stage to `.tmp`, rename).
2. On install: `Funke-PackageTool registry-download <zipUrl> <expectedSha256> <project>/Packages/`. The tool streams the download with progress events, SHA-256 verifies, extracts (rejecting `..` path traversal and zip-bomb escapes), and moves the single top-level folder into `<project>/Packages/<PackageFolder>/`. The zip MUST contain exactly one top-level folder with `funke-package.lua` at its root.
3. Adds the package name to `<project>/project.json` packages array (via the editor's normal allow-list write path).
4. Regenerates and builds the project package workspace (`FunkeProject::AutomateForProject` → `project-packages.lua`, then `BuildProjectPackages`).
5. Calls `PackageHost::LoadInstalled()` to load the new DLLs without restarting the editor.

Install is atomic: download → verify → extract → move into place. Any failure cleans up the temp zip + extract dir AND rolls back a partially-installed package dir, so re-running install doesn't trip the "Package already installed" check.

To publish a package to the registry: zip the package directory (single top-level folder containing `funke-package.lua`), upload it somewhere fetchable, append an entry to `Funke-PackageRegistry/index.json` with the download URL + SHA-256, push. The CDN cache on `raw.githubusercontent.com` is the only deploy step.

## Funke-PackageTool CLI

`Funke-PackageTool/Program.cs` is a stateless .NET 10 CLI. Current editor callers use `Process::Run` with the executable resolved by `Utils/PackageToolPath.hpp`. Commands write JSON to stdout, errors to stderr.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `nuget-search <query> [--take N]` | Search nuget.org via the v3 search endpoint, return JSON array of results. |
| `nuget-versions <packageId>` | List versions of a NuGet package (newest first, max 30). |
| `github-index <url>` | Fetch arbitrary JSON from a URL (used for GitHub-hosted package indexes). |
| `github-download <url> <outputPath> [expectedSha256]` | Stream a file to disk in 64KB chunks, emit `{event:"progress"}` JSON lines every ~100ms; verify SHA-256 when supplied. |
| `unzip <archive> <outDir>` | Extract a zip. Refuses to overwrite existing files. |
| `zip <projectDir> <outZip>` | Pack a project for the asset library (excludes `bin/`, `obj/`, `.vs/`, `.vscode/`, `__pycache__/`, `.idea/`, `*.user`, `*.suo`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`). Refuses to overwrite output. |
| `registry-fetch <registryUrl> <outputJsonPath>` | Download the registry index.json with atomic write. |
| `registry-download <zipUrl> <expectedSha256> <destPackagesDir>` | Download + SHA-256 verify + extract + move-into-place, with full rollback on failure. |

When invoking the tool from C++, the path is resolved via `Utils/PackageToolPath.hpp`. Don't shell out to `dotnet` directly — go through `Process::Run` so output streaming and exit-code handling stays consistent.

## Non-obvious gotchas

These break things in ways that aren't obvious from the error messages. Internalise them.

1. **EnTT entity bits MUST match across DLLs.** The `native` layer auto-defines `FUNKE_ENTITY_BITS=<value>` and adds `FunkeEntityBitsConfigIncludeDir` to the include path so transitively-included EnTT headers see the same `entt_traits` specialization as the engine. Skipping this is an ODR violation that surfaces as memory corruption when entities cross the package boundary. The editor's Rebuild Engine flow rewrites `FunkeEntityBitsConfig.h` to override the `-D` value without a premake regen; the EnTT patch in `entity.hpp` picks it up via `__has_include`. If you're hand-writing a `Pkg.<Name>.Native` premake project (don't), you need both the define AND the include dir.

2. **Dawn libdirs are per-configuration.** `EditorRuntimeCommon` pulls in `EngineCoreRender` which links `webgpu_dawn.lib`. The lib lives under per-config `Debug/Release` folders, so the `native` layer must set `libdirs` per-config — Dist points at the Release dir. See [package-loader.lua](../../../premake/package-loader.lua). LNK2038 can indicate a configuration mismatch.

3. **`FNK_IMPORT_DLL` is required on the native side.** Engine is a SharedLib; without this define, `FUNKE_API` resolves to `dllexport` in the package and you get unresolved-external errors against engine symbols. The loader sets it automatically for `native` (not `native_standalone`).

4. **csharp layer auto-references Funke-ScriptCore.** Don't add it to `manifest.dependencies` — that's for OTHER packages. Funke-ScriptCore is implicit and unavoidable; pure-managed packages that don't touch scene state pay nothing for the unused reference.

5. **Allow-list is fail-closed.** Missing `project.json` or absent `packages` field means **no packages are registered**, not "all packages". This is deliberate: without an explicit list we don't know the project's intent. Fresh projects need to add their packages to the array before they appear in the solution.

6. **Always rerun premake after editing the allow-list or adding/removing packages** — `premake5 vs2022` for engine packages, `premake/project-packages.lua --funke-project=…` for a project's. The vcxproj files don't regenerate themselves. The scaffolder and the editor's install flow do this automatically; manual edits don't. Without regen, the IDE solution silently lags behind the manifest set.

7. **Don't combine `native` and `native_standalone`.** Already covered, but worth repeating because the error message comes from the loader, not the compiler — i.e. you see it at premake time, not after a long build.

8. **Package name PascalCase pattern is strict.** `My-Game.Loot` ✗, `mygame.loot` ✗, `MyGame.loot` ✗, `MyGame.Loot_v2` ✗. Loosening it breaks downstream identifiers — folder names, project names, DllImport library names. The regex is enforced by both the loader and `NewPackage.py`.

9. **The csharp layer's `nuget` list widens the runtime surface.** Each entry becomes a `<PackageReference>` in the generated csproj. Keep the list short — this is the only way new dependencies ship to all users of the package, and it cuts against the engine's "no mandatory dependencies" rule. Prefer pinning versions explicitly (`"System.Text.Json:8.0.0"` not `"System.Text.Json:*"`).

10. **Cloud install atomicity depends on the rollback.** The `RegistryDownload` flow in `Funke-PackageTool/Program.cs` tracks `installedDirToRollback` and deletes the half-installed package dir on any post-Move failure. Don't bypass it — directly extracting a registry zip without verification creates a state the editor can't recover from without manual filesystem surgery.

## Where things live (quick reference)

| Subsystem | File | What's in it |
|---|---|---|
| Loader / validator / Premake registration | `premake/package-loader.lua` | The single source of truth for the schema. Read first when in doubt. |
| Project package workspace | `premake/project-packages.lua` | `--funke-project=<abs>` → `<project>/.funke/build/packages/` (allow-listed packages only). |
| Runtime DLL discovery & lifecycle | `Funke-Engine/src/Core/PackageHost.{hpp,cpp}` | `LoadAll`, `LoadInstalled`, `UnloadAll`, OnLoad/OnUnload hooks. |
| Editor-side NuGet + Funke registry management | `Funke-Engine/src/Packages/PackageManager.{hpp,cpp}` | Async install / remove / restore for NuGet sources. |
| Component registration API | `Funke-Engine/src/Packages/PackageRegistration.hpp` | `Package::RegisterSerializableComponent`, `DeclareComponentConflict`. |
| Cross-DLL marker + macros | `Funke-Engine/src/Packages/PackageApi.hpp` | `FUNKE_PACKAGE_API`, `FunkePackage_OnLoad` signature. |
| Editor UI | `Funke-Editor/src/Gui/PackageManagerPanel.{hpp,cpp}` | NuGet tab, disk-install tab, cloud-install tab (registry). |
| Stateless tool CLI | `Funke-PackageTool/Program.cs` | `nuget-*`, `github-*`, `zip` / `unzip`, `registry-fetch` / `registry-download`. |
| Scaffolder | `scripts/packages/NewPackage.py` | Authoritative on layer combos + folder layout + scaffolded entry points. |
| Remover | `scripts/packages/RemovePackage.py` | Inverse of NewPackage; preserves allow-list integrity. |
| Version bumper | `scripts/packages/BumpPackageVersion.py` | Rewrites the manifest's `version` field. |
| Cloud registry (external) | `github.com/Ben-Scr/Funke-PackageRegistry` | `index.json` schema; static, no server. Also the sources of the official `Funke.*` packages. |

# Building & Shipping a Funke Game

A shipped desktop Funke game is the **`Funke-Runtime`** executable plus your project's **`Assets/`** as **loose files**. The build converts serialized scene/prefab/data assets to binary but does not bundle them into an asset archive. Platform builders may package this content into an APK, app bundle or Web payload. The Editor's **Build** panel produces the output; **build profiles** pick the platform + render backend; `project.json` carries the window/branding/runtime settings the game boots with.

## Build profiles (`.build`)

A profile is a tiny file under the project's `BuildProfiles/` folder, one per `.build`. Schema (`FunkeBuildProfile`):

```json
{
  "name": "Windows",
  "platform": "Windows",          // Windows | Linux | MacOS | Android | IOS | VisionOS | Web
  "renderBackend": "Direct3D12",  // must be allowed for the platform (else coerced on load)
  // optional test/QA switches; unset = follow project.json (FunkeBuildProfile::ApplyTo)
  "configuration": "Debug",       // Debug | Development | Release
  "defines": ["FUNKE_TEST"],      // added to customDefines for this build
  "showRuntimeStats": true, "showRuntimeLogs": false,
  "devConsole": true,             // ` console + F8 physics overlay
  "isolatedPrefs": true           // PlayerPrefs/SaveData under Profiles/<profile name>
}
```

- `FunkeBuildProfile::WriteDefaultProfiles` scaffolds **Windows + Linux + macOS** profiles on project creation (skips existing files; a project template's `BuildProfiles/` replaces them).
- **Allowed backends are per-platform** (`AllowedBackends`): Windows → D3D12/D3D11/Vulkan/OpenGL; Linux → Vulkan/OpenGL; macOS/iOS/visionOS → Metal; Android → Vulkan/OpenGLES; Web → OpenGLES. `FunkeBuildProfile::Load` coerces a backend outside the list to the first allowed entry and logs a `Build` warning — `Auto` is in no list, so a profile never keeps it. The Build Profiles panel only offers allowed backends and re-coerces when the platform changes. A build always ships the profile's backend.
- Platform enum values are **stable integers** — don't renumber (existing `.build` files depend on them).
- The active profile is `project.json` → `activeBuildProfile` (name) and the `buildProfile` (`Debug` | `Development` | `Release`) / `renderBackend` keys. `GameBuilder::Prepare` folds the active profile's switches into the build snapshot only; `Request::ConfigurationOverride` (CLI `--debug/--development/--release`) wins over the profile's `configuration`.
- Debug/QA tooling a profile can switch on (dev console, `[DevCommand]`, physics overlay, `--prefs-profile`, `--input-script`, `--screenshot-at`, `--fixed-step`) is described in `Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Testing.md`; engine code in `Funke-Engine/src/DevTools/`.

Manage profiles in the editor's **Build Profiles** panel (create / duplicate / delete / rename, pick platform + backend).

## What a build produces

From the **Build** panel: choose a profile, set the **scene list** (`buildScenes`, first enabled entry becomes the shipped startup scene), pick an output folder, **Build** (or **Build & Run**). The editor then:

1. **Compiles the C# script assembly** (`<Name>.dll`) with `FUNKE_BUILD` defines (below). Configuration follows the profile (`FunkeProject::GetBuildConfigurationFor`): **`Release` → `Dist`**; **`Debug` → `Debug`** (debug runtime + PDBs of runtime, engine, ScriptCore and the user assembly; needs engine sources or a `Runtime-Debug` folder, links the non-redistributable debug CRT); **`Development` → the editor's own configuration** (`FunkeProject::GetActiveBuildConfiguration()` = `FNK_BUILD_CONFIG_NAME`).
2. **Copies the `Funke-Runtime` executable** for the target platform (`Runtime-Dist` for Release, `Runtime-Debug` for Debug, `Runtime-Development` for Development, when no freshly built runtime is found).
3. **Copies the reachable part of `Assets/`** (and `FunkeAssets/`) as **loose files** beside the exe. `Editor/BuildAssetPruning.cpp` follows GUIDs, asset paths and scene names out of the enabled build scenes and `project.json`, plus path literals and `AssetManager.FindAll<T>` calls in `.cs` sources. Unreferenced assets, `.cs` files and scenes not in the build list are left out. `Assets/StreamingAssets/` always ships, so files only loaded through computed paths go there. If the scan fails, the build ships everything and logs a warning.
4. **Converts serialized assets to binary** in the staged copy, then **writes the boot config** the runtime reads (scene list, startup scene, window/splash/branding). The project's source assets keep their format.

The output is a runnable, distributable folder. Because assets are loose, the player's machine reads PNG/WAV/`.scene` files directly from disk on demand (`funke-assets-and-content`).

**Without clicking (CI, agents):** `Funke-Editor.exe --project=<root> --build [--build-profile=<Name>] [--build-output=<dir>]` runs the same pipeline once the project has loaded and quits with exit code `0`/`1` (`EditorApplication.cpp` → `ImGuiEditorLayer::RequestCommandLineBuild`). Default profile: the active one, else the first profile for the host desktop platform; default output `<root>/Builds/<Profile>`. No Explorer window opens and no modal dialog blocks. Keep the output path short — Dawn's license tree can exceed Windows' 260-char limit under long paths. Built games accept `--scene=<Name>`, `--quit-after=<seconds>` (wall clock), and the game-clock test options `--input-script=`, `--screenshot-at=`, `--screenshot-dir=`, `--fixed-step=`, `--quit-at=`, `--exec=` and `--prefs-profile=` (`DevTools/RunAutomation.hpp`).

### Android, iOS, Web: platform packages

Only the editor's own desktop platform builds natively (`BuildPlatformSupport::IsHostDesktop`). Every other platform comes from a **platform package** (`platforms/Funke.Platform.{Android,iOS,Web}`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\Platforms`, or `FUNKE_PLATFORM_PACKAGES`), discovered by `Project/PlatformPackages.{hpp,cpp}`; without one the platform is greyed out. For those builds the editor stages platform-neutral content into `<output>/.funke-content` (project.json, Assets with binary scenes, FunkeAssets, `bin/<cfg>/*.dll`, Funke-ScriptCore.dll, Licenses) and runs the package's Python builder (`Editor/PlatformBuilder.cpp`, protocol in `scripts/platform/funke_platform_sdk/protocol.py`), which compiles the engine for the target via `cmake/FunkeEngine.cmake` and writes the artifact (APK / Xcode project or .app / static site).

- Per-platform settings: `"platformOptions": { ... }` in the `.build` file → `options` in the build request (keystore, `orientation`, `developmentTeam`, `dotnetSdk`, `debugSymbols`, ...). `env:NAME` reads a value from the environment — use it for passwords. Each builder's `describe` lists its options; the Build Profiles panel shows them plus the builder's `check` results.
- A package-platform profile's `renderBackend` goes only into the staged project.json; it must not change the live project, whose backend the editor uses for itself.
- C# off-desktop runs on Mono (`platforms/Funke.ScriptRuntime.Mono`, a `build-component`). Android Release builds AOT-compile the game assemblies, Funke-ScriptCore and their direct framework references (Mono AOT + LLVM, `Builder/mono_aot.py`, cached in `PlatformCache/Android/aot`); options `aot` / `aotLlvm`; the player log says `Mono runtime started (android-arm64, AOT: N ...)`. Web + C# needs the .NET 11 SDK with `wasm-tools`: the engine is compiled to `FunkeWeb.a` with that SDK's Emscripten and `dotnet publish` relinks it with the runtime. `Builder/WasmCalliSignatures` turns every `delegate* unmanaged` / `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` signature into a placeholder `[DllImport]` so the SDK generates the wasm trampolines — a new function-pointer signature needs no manual step.
- The Android builder currently targets API 36 (`Builder/android_toolchain.py::TARGET_SDK`) and links for 16 KB pages (`ANDROID_SUPPORT_FLEXIBLE_PAGE_SIZES`). Check current store requirements when preparing a publication. Release also writes `<Game>.aab` for Play (`Builder/android_bundle.py`: aapt2 `--proto-format` → base module → bundletool → jarsigner with the profile keystore); option `appBundle` forces it on/off. A Play upload needs the user's own keystore (`keystore`, `keyAlias`, `keystorePassword: "env:..."`) and a growing `versionCode`; the debug key only warns.
- Packages contribute Android code through `android = { java, maven, manifest, placeholders }` in `funke-package.lua` (`Builder/android_libraries.py`, `android_maven.py` with `Android/maven.lock.json`, `android_manifest.py`); scripts call it via `AndroidBridge.Call` / `Subscribe`. Ads: the `Funke.Ads` registry package (AdMob + UMP consent, simulated in the editor), app ID = profile option `admobAppId`. Details in `funke-author-package`.
- First build per platform compiles SDL3/Dawn and caches them in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\PlatformCache`. Builder logs: `PlatformCache\<Platform>\work\<hash>\build.log`.
- Testing a Web build: serve the folder over HTTP (not `file://`). The editor's Web preview (`platforms/Funke.Platform.Web/Builder/preview.py`) serves on loopback with `Cache-Control: no-store`; use equivalent cache behavior when serving manually.

User docs: `Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Platform-Packages.md`.

At runtime, `Funke-Runtime` reads the project's `buildScenes` + `startupScene` and registers/loads scenes as in `funke-project-structure` → *How scenes register at runtime*. List every intended shipping scene explicitly. `SceneManager.LoadScene` can also register other shipped `.scene` files by name; pruning follows reachable GUID/path/name references in serialized assets and C# literals, so those references can retain additional scenes. Arbitrary computed names do not ensure inclusion.

## Shipped-game settings (in `project.json`)

These control how the built game looks and behaves (full list + defaults in `funke-project-structure`). The ones that matter most for shipping:

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `buildScenes` / `startupScene` | shipping roots and startup; the builder sets startup to the first enabled scene |
| `buildWidth` / `buildHeight` (+ min/max) | window size |
| `buildFullscreen` / `buildFullscreenMode` | `Exclusive` \| `BorderlessWindowed` \| `Maximized` |
| `buildResizable` / `buildRunInBackground` | window behavior |
| `executableName` / `buildVersion` / `buildCompany` | exe name + metadata |
| `appIcon` | window/exe icon (project-relative image) |
| `splashScreen { … }` | startup splash (image/text/colors/durations/fades) |
| `showRuntimeStats` | FPS/frame-time overlay in the shipped build (unset = on for Development, off for Release) |
| `showRuntimeLogs` | log console in the shipped build (unset = on for Development, off for Release) |
| `graphics { postProcessingEnabled, renderScale, … }` | quality defaults (block written only when non-default; a top-level `enablePostProcessing` is legacy, read only when `graphics.postProcessingEnabled` is absent) |
| `renderBackend` | the editor's own backend (`Auto` = engine picks); a build overwrites it in the shipped copy with the profile's backend |
| `assetSerializationFormat` | source-project save format: `Json` (new projects) \| `Binary` (also the missing-key default); shipped serialized assets are converted to binary |
| `profiler.enableInRuntime` | include the profiler panel in the shipped build |

For a public release set `buildProfile: "Release"` (or `funke build --release`); the overlays are then off unless `project.json` sets them explicitly.

## Three axes — don't mix the words

| Axis | Values | Lives in | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Engine configuration** | `Debug` / `Release` / `Dist` | MSBuild `-p:Configuration` | How the engine + script DLLs are compiled; `FNK_DEBUG` / `FNK_RELEASE` / `FNK_DIST` |
| **Build profile** (`FunkeProject::BuildProfile`, Build window "Configuration") | `Development` / `Release` / `Debug` | `project.json` `buildProfile` (written only when not Development), or a `.build`'s `configuration` | `FUNKE_BUILD_*` define, shipped binaries (Release → Dist, Debug → Debug), overlay + dev-console defaults |
| **Platform profile** (`FunkeBuildProfile`, `.build` file) | platform + render backend | `BuildProfiles/*.build`, active name in `activeBuildProfile` | Target platform / backend (section above) |

## Editor vs shipped — the build defines

The C# `-p:DefineConstants=` value is assembled by `FunkeProject::BuildManagedDefineConstants(primarySymbol)` (editor contexts) or `BuildManagedDefinesForSnapshot` (`Funke-Editor/src/Build/GameBuilder.cpp`, ship builds from the Build panel, `--build` and `funke build`) — `%3B`-joined, in this order:

| Compile context | Primary | Config | Profile | Platform | Custom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Editor hot-reload (`ScriptSystem`), package restore (`PackageManager`), Launcher new-project starter-script compile | `FUNKE_EDITOR` | `FNK_<editor cfg>` | **always** `FUNKE_BUILD_DEVELOPMENT` | the **active build profile's** platform (`FUNKE_ANDROID`, …; `FunkeProject::GetEditorScriptTarget`), else the editor's own | `customDefines` + the active profile's `defines` |
| Build panel ship build | `FUNKE_BUILD` | `FNK_DIST` (Release), `FNK_DEBUG` (Debug), or `FNK_<editor cfg>` (Development) | effective build snapshot's `FUNKE_BUILD_DEVELOPMENT` / `FUNKE_BUILD_RELEASE` / `FUNKE_BUILD_DEBUG` | selected build profile's target platform | `customDefines` + the profile's `defines` |
| Launcher "launch runtime" | `FUNKE_BUILD` | `FNK_<launcher cfg>` | project's profile define | host platform | `customDefines` |

Editor preview **never** sees `FUNKE_BUILD_RELEASE`, whatever the project profile — Release-only code is only exercised by a real build.

**Platform simulation:** the editor plays scripts as the active build profile's platform so `#if FUNKE_ANDROID` code can be debugged without a device. `ScriptSystem::PollScriptDefines` rebuilds within a second when the define string changes (profile switch, profile platform/defines, custom defines) and rewrites `FunkeDefines.props`; the defines of the loaded assembly are stamped in `bin/<cfg>/<Name>.dll.defines`. The toolbar shows a **Simulating <Platform>** badge. C# `Application.Platform` is the simulated platform in the editor (`Funke_Application_GetPlatform`), `Application.IsSimulatingPlatform` flags it, `Engine.Platform` stays the real OS. Native `FNK_PLATFORM_*` never change.

**Native C++ scripts** (generated `NativeScripts/CMakeLists.txt`) get a different set: `FNK_DEBUG;_DEBUG` / `FNK_RELEASE;NDEBUG` / `FNK_DIST;NDEBUG` per CMake config, `FUNKE_ALL_MODULES=1`, `FNK_PLATFORM_WINDOWS` / `FNK_PLATFORM_LINUX`, `FUNKE_BUILD_${FUNKE_BUILD_PROFILE}` (CMake default `DEVELOPMENT`; editor hot-reload passes `-DFUNKE_BUILD_PROFILE=DEVELOPMENT` explicitly), and `customDefines`. There is **no `FUNKE_EDITOR` / `FUNKE_BUILD` and no `FUNKE_WINDOWS`** for native code — branch with `Application::IsEditor()` instead. The Build panel neither rebuilds native scripts with the Release profile nor stages their DLL (`funke-engine-scripting`).

```csharp
#if FUNKE_EDITOR
    DrawDebugBounds();        // stripped from BOTH Development and Release ship builds
#endif
#if FUNKE_BUILD_RELEASE
    UseFastPath();            // ship-Release only; never compiled in editor preview
#else
    UseValidatedPath();
#endif
```

Generated files — **don't hand-edit**:
- `Packages/FunkeDefines.props` — rewritten by every `FunkeProject::Save()` (`WriteManagedDefinesProps`) with `$(DefineConstants);FUNKE_EDITOR;<active profile define>;<platform>;<custom>` for VS IntelliSense; older `.csproj`s get the `<Import Project="Packages/FunkeDefines.props" …>` line patched in. Real compiles pass `-p:DefineConstants=` and override it, so with profile=Release IntelliSense greys out `#if FUNKE_BUILD_DEVELOPMENT` code that the editor actually compiles.
- `NativeScripts/CMakeLists.txt` — written **only when missing**. Changing `customDefines` later does *not* reach an existing one; delete it (it's regenerated by `EnsureNativeScriptProjectFiles`) or edit its `target_compile_definitions` block. Keep the `FUNKE_BUILD_${FUNKE_BUILD_PROFILE}` indirection and always pass an explicit `-DFUNKE_BUILD_PROFILE=` when invoking cmake — CMake caches the variable across configures.

**Custom defines** are added in the Build panel's **Defines** row (trimmed, de-duplicated, saved immediately) and stored as `"customDefines": [...]` in `project.json` (written only when non-empty). Names only — no `NAME=value` form.

## Compile-time `#if` vs runtime check

- **`#if`** when the code must not exist in the other binary: calls editor-only APIs, strips debug/cheat code from ship size, changes the assembly's surface.
- **Runtime** when the same assembly should behave differently:
  - `Application.IsEditor` (C#, `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Core/Application.cs`) / `Application::IsEditor()` (C++, `Core/Application.hpp`). True only in the editor process: `EditorApplication`'s constructor and `CreateApplication` call `SetEditorHost(true)` (process-global static, so it works before the `Application` exists). Runtime and Launcher leave it false.
  - `Engine.BuildConfiguration` (C#, `Core/Engine.cs`) → `Editor` (0, editor play mode) / `Development` (1) / `Release` (2) / `Debug` (3, Debug game build), resolved at runtime from the shipped `project.json`'s profile (`Funke_Engine_GetBuildConfiguration` in `ScriptBindingsScene.cpp`). `Engine.ConfigurationName` gives the string.
- Designer-facing switches (stats overlay, logs) belong in `project.json` settings, not `#if`.

```csharp
public override void OnUpdate()
{
    if (Application.IsEditor) return;      // e.g. skip analytics while iterating
    Analytics.Tick();
}
```

## Profile flip resets overlays

Changing the **Configuration** combo in the Build panel (`ImGuiEditorLayerPanels.cpp`) resets `ShowRuntimeStats` and `ShowRuntimeLogs` to unset and saves the project, so they follow the new configuration (`FunkeProject::ResolveShowRuntimeStats/Logs`: off for Release, on otherwise) and a Release build doesn't ship the stats overlay by accident. Users can set them explicitly afterwards in Project Settings → Build (`RenderSettings_Build`). A new "should default differently in Release" toggle follows the same pattern: an `std::optional` on the project plus a `Resolve…()` default (like `DevConsole` / `ResolveDevConsole`), reset in that handler.

## Build configurations

The script `.csproj` defines `Debug` / `Release` / `Dist` (`funke-project-structure`). **`Dist`** is optimized, strips symbols, and is what a **Release-profile** build compiles; a Development-profile build uses the editor's own configuration (a Debug editor produces a Debug assembly). Don't ship a `Debug` assembly — set the profile to Release for public builds.

## Pitfalls

- **Scene not in the game?** Check the staged file and pruning report. Enabled `buildScenes` entries are build roots; reachable asset references and C# literals can retain additional scenes, while computed names cannot. List every intended shipping scene explicitly.
- **Assets are loose** — the output folder *is* the distributable; zip the whole folder, don't expect a single packed file. Keep `Assets/` (and its `.meta` files) next to the exe.
- **Backend coercion** — an invalid platform/backend pair (or `Auto`) in a `.build` is replaced by the first allowed backend when the profile loads, with only a log warning; verify the profile shows what you intended.
- **`Packages/` is git-ignored**, but the *build* still needs the compiled assembly + `Funke-ScriptCore`; build from the editor (which restores them) rather than from a bare clone.
- **Don't renumber `BuildPlatform`/serialized enums** — old `.build` and `project.json` files decode by value.
- **`showRuntimeStats` / `showRuntimeLogs` follow the profile when unset** — on for Development, off for Release. An explicit `true` in `project.json` still ships them in Release.
- **Don't conflate `FNK_DEBUG`/`FNK_RELEASE`/`FNK_DIST` with `FUNKE_BUILD_*`.** The first is the engine configuration, the second the game profile; C# sees both.
- **"Works in the editor, broken in the Release build"** — usually logic inside `#if FUNKE_EDITOR` that the game needed at runtime (move it out, or use `Application.IsEditor`), or a Release-only `#if FUNKE_BUILD_RELEASE` path that editor preview never compiled. Test by building and running the output.
- **Native scripts in a build** — not compiled or staged by the Build panel. Package native layers are (engine packages built via MSBuild, binaries staged under `Packages/`) — put shipping C++ in a package (`funke-author-package`).

## Files to know

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Funke-Engine/src/Project/FunkeProject.hpp` | `BuildProfile` enum, `ActiveBuildProfile`, `ActiveBuildProfileName`, `CustomDefines`, `ShowRuntimeStats/Logs` |
| `Funke-Engine/src/Project/FunkeProject.cpp` | `BuildManagedDefineConstants`, `GetActiveBuildProfileDefine`, `GetActiveBuildDefineConstant`, `GetManagedPlatformDefine`, `WriteManagedDefinesProps`, `BuildNativeScriptCMakeLists`, `BuildProjectJson` |
| `Funke-Engine/src/Project/FunkeBuildProfile.{hpp,cpp}` | `.build` platform/backend profiles |
| `Funke-Editor/src/Build/GameBuilder.cpp` | Build pipeline shared by the Build panel, `--build` and `funke build` (`Prepare`, `ResolveProfileName`, `BuildManagedDefinesForSnapshot`, runtime/asset staging) |
| `Funke-Editor/src/Systems/ImGuiEditorLayerPanels.cpp` | Build panel (Configuration combo + overlay reset, Defines row), `RequestCommandLineBuild`, `RenderSettings_Build` |
| `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptSystem.cpp` | Editor hot-reload `dotnet build` / `cmake -DFUNKE_BUILD_PROFILE=DEVELOPMENT` |
| `Funke-Engine/src/Core/Application.hpp`, `Funke-Editor/src/EditorApplication.cpp` | `IsEditor()` / `SetEditorHost(true)` |
| `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Core/Application.cs`, `Core/Engine.cs` | `Application.IsEditor`, `Engine.BuildConfiguration` |

## Related skills
`funke-project-structure` (project.json + `.csproj` configs + scene registration), `funke-assets-and-content` (loose-file assets), `funke-make-a-game` (the end-to-end flow), `funke-engine-scripting` (how the script compiles/hot-reload run, native scripts, adding a runtime binding like `Application.IsEditor`).
