# Build, test, run the engine

For Windows engine builds, tests and launches, prefer `scripts/dev/*.ps1`; they handle toolchain selection, diagnostics and output deployment. Start with the smallest verification that proves the change: documentation/skill edits need no compilation, managed-only changes need only the affected managed project, and native changes need a targeted incremental build. Preserve existing outputs and configuration; use `-Rebuild` only for demonstrated stale/corrupt build outputs or an explicit request.

## Build — `scripts\dev\Build.ps1`

```powershell
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 Engine                       # default project; Release is the default config
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 Editor,ScriptCore -Config Debug
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 Tests                        # EngineTests + EditorTests
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 All                          # Engine, ScriptCore, ScriptCompiler, Editor, Runtime, PackageTool, Launcher, CLI, tests
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 Launcher                     # builds Funke-PackageTool first; its postbuild stages EngineSDK\ (incl. Licenses\ that game builds need)
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 ScriptCompiler               # editor's in-process Roslyn hot-reload compiler -> Funke-Editor\ScriptCompiler\
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 CLI                          # funke.exe (Funke-CLI): compiles the editor's UI-free build sources too
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 -File Funke-Engine\src\Scene\Scene.cpp,Funke-Editor\src\Gui\AssetBrowser.cpp   # compile TUs only
scripts\dev\Build.ps1 Engine -Warnings all
```

Projects: `Engine`, `EditorRuntime`, `Editor`, `Runtime`, `Launcher`, `CLI`, `EngineTests`, `EditorTests`, `Tests`, `ScriptCore`, `ScriptCompiler`, `PackageTool`, `All`.

What it does for you:
- Pins VS2022 MSBuild. VS "18" (the user's IDE) builds into its own `bin-int\<cfg>\<project>-vs18.0\` (`FunkeIntDirSuffix`, premake/compat.lua): sharing one PCH between the two installs fails with `C2375 __builtin_assume_aligned` and leaves a stale `.lib` (LNK2019 in consumers).
- Builds the `.vcxproj` directly (`-t:<proj>` on `Funke.sln` → MSB4057; the sln can't build SDK-style C# → MSB4236). `ScriptCore` and `ScriptCompiler` go through `dotnet build`.
- Regenerates premake (`vendor\bin\premake5.exe vs2022`) when a `.cpp` under a native project's `src\` (Engine, EditorRuntime, Editor, Runtime, Launcher, CLI, test projects) exists that its `.vcxproj` doesn't list, or a root `*.lua`, `premake/*.lua`, `premake/dependencies/*.lua` or one of those projects' `premake5.lua` changed since the last regen. Files premake deliberately drops via `removefiles` (e.g. `Funke-Engine/src/Diagnostics/*.cpp`) are remembered in `bin-int\_agent\premake-unlisted.txt`. Package sources (`packages/NAME/**`, `funke-package.lua`) are **not** watched: pass `-Regen` after adding a package `.cpp` or editing a manifest.
- Prints only `error` lines and warnings in git-changed files, as `path(line,col): CODE message`, deduplicated. Full log: `bin-int\_agent\<target>.log`.
- After each build copies `bin\<cfg>\Funke-Engine\Funke-Engine.dll` (+pdb) into Funke-Editor, Funke-Launcher, Funke-Runtime, Funke-CLI and the test folders. Without this the editor keeps running the old engine and fixes "don't work". `-NoDeploy` disables it.
- Warns when a Funke app from the same config is running (DLLs locked → copy/postbuild fail). A deploy that stays stale fails the build: `DEPLOY FAILED` lists the copies, exit code 1 (a stale `Funke-Engine.dll` next to a fresh exe dies before `main` with `0xC0000138` and no output).

`Build.ps1` regenerates with plain `premake5 vs2022`; it does not preserve custom generation options. For a workspace generated with module/profiler/profile options, regenerate explicitly with those same options when needed, then use `-NoRegenCheck` to avoid replacing them. Package and module-variant workspaces need their own targeted build path.

## Test — `scripts\dev\Test.ps1`

```powershell
scripts\dev\Test.ps1                              # build + run Engine and Editor doctest suites
scripts\dev\Test.ps1 -Filter "*Prefab*"           # doctest --test-case filter (wildcards, comma = OR)
scripts\dev\Test.ps1 -Suite Engine -Filter "*Prefab*"  # only the affected native suite
scripts\dev\Test.ps1 -Suite CSharp -Filter Vector3   # xUnit, plain word = FullyQualifiedName~word
scripts\dev\Test.ps1 -Suite All -NoBuild
scripts\dev\Test.ps1 -List                        # list test cases
```

Engine log spam (it logs to stdout) is filtered; only doctest lines and failures remain. Full output: `bin-int\_agent\test-<Suite>.log`. Tests live in `Tests/Funke-Engine-Tests/src/*Tests.cpp` (doctest, `TEST_CASE`/`CHECK`), `Tests/Funke-Editor-Tests/src`, `Tests/Funke-ScriptCore-Tests/*.cs`. A new test `.cpp` is picked up by Build.ps1's automatic regen.

CI equivalent (what a PR must pass): `scripts\RunTests.bat --release` and `dotnet test Tests\Funke-ScriptCore-Tests\Funke-ScriptCore-Tests.csproj -c Release`, then smoke tests in `scripts/ci/` (`application_smoke_test.py`, `runtime_smoke_test.py`, `project_package_smoke_test.ps1`). Locally use `Test.ps1`, not `RunTests.bat`: it resolves MSBuild via `vswhere -latest` (VS "18" here → PCH clash) and builds serially.

## Run & verify — `scripts\dev\Run.ps1`

```powershell
scripts\dev\Run.ps1                                     # Editor, sandbox project, 1 screenshot after 8 s, then close
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -App Runtime -Project C:\path\to\GameProject -Seconds 5 -Shots 3 -Interval 1
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Recent                             # the project the Launcher opened last (user's real project — only when asked)
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -KeepOpen -Foreground               # leave it running in front, e.g. to continue with computer-use
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -ExtraArgs "--ci-smoke-test"
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <3D project> -EditorView     # screenshot the Editor View tab (default is whatever tab the layout selected); -GameView: the Game View tab, e.g. with -Play -OpenWindow gamestats
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -App Runtime -Variant 2d -Project <dir> # engine-module runtime variant (bin\<cfg>-windows-x86_64-2d)
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <dir> -Play                    # editor enters play mode after load (FUNKE_EDITOR_AUTOPLAY) — repro play-mode crashes
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <dir> -StopAfter 3             # enter Play and stop after 3 s; verify teardown
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <dir> -ReloadAfter 3           # reload the editor in-process after 3 s
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -App Runtime -Project <dir> -ScreenshotAt 2s,5s -FixedStep 60          # engine screenshots at GAME time, then quits
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -App Runtime -Project <dir> -InputScript run.json -Exec "physics.debug on"  # scripted keys/mouse/touch/commands
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <dir> -OpenWindow build,buildprofiles   # editor with those windows open (FUNKE_EDITOR_OPEN); also projectsettings (projectsettings:graphics picks the category), preferences, packages, profiler, gamestats (Game View Stats overlay)
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <3D project> -EditorView -Select Player   # select + frame that entity (FUNKE_EDITOR_SELECT) — check selection box / gizmo / F
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Project <3D project> -EditorView -DrawMode triangle   # Editor View draw mode triangle|mixed (FUNKE_EDITOR_DRAW_MODE)
scripts\dev\Run.ps1 -Theme glass -OpenWindow preferences   # editor theme auto|dark|light|glass|custom for this run only (FUNKE_EDITOR_THEME); the user's EditorPreferences.json keeps its theme
```

Runtime runs use the isolated player-data profile `agent` (`--prefs-profile=agent`: PlayerPrefs/SaveData under `Profiles\agent`), so a test never changes a game's real saves; `-RealPrefs` opts out. Prefer `-ScreenshotAt` over `-Seconds/-Shots` for games: wall-clock shots drift with load times, game-time shots don't (a fresh `bin-int\_agent\run\shots-<time>-<pid>\` per run, listed at the end, so parallel sessions can't delete each other's). Instead of temporary probes in game code, drive the game with an input script (keys, mouse, touch, `[DevCommand]`s, screenshots, quit). Format: `Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Testing.md`.

Engine-module variants (`Funke.2D`/`Funke.3D` left out) build in their own workspace: `vendor\bin\premake5.exe --without-3d vs2022` (or `--without-2d`, or both → `nomodules`), then MSBuild `premake\generated\variant-<2d|3d|nomodules>\Funke-Runtime\Funke-Runtime.vcxproj`. The first build compiles the whole engine; build after touching code under an `FUNKE_WITH_2D`/`FUNKE_WITH_3D` gate.

Outputs: `bin-int\_agent\run\<App>-<n>.png` (Read them — this is how you see UI/rendering changes), `bin-int\_agent\run\<App>.log` (only this run's log lines, also across spdlog rotations `<exe>.1.log`…`<exe>.3.log`, so a log flood can't push the first error out). The summary lists `[warning]`/`[error]`/`[critical]` lines and any new crash dump in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\CrashDumps`. Exit code 1 on crash or non-zero exit.

The sandbox project is `bin-int\_agent\SandboxProject` (project.json + empty `SampleScene`). Put fixture scenes/assets there for an experiment; delete the folder to reset. Screenshots use `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` so they work while the window is covered; only the main window is captured. Every run passes `--background` (`RunAutomation::IsBackground()`): the window never takes focus, opens behind the user's windows (`HWND_BOTTOM`), doesn't background-pause, and fullscreen/maximized become a plain window filling the work area. Keep it that way so tests never steal the user's focus; `-Foreground` only when something must be in front (computer-use).

### Drive an open editor — `funke editor` (Editor Bridge)

For several checks in a row, keep one editor open (`Run.ps1 -Project <dir> -KeepOpen`) and drive it instead of relaunching; scripts hot-reload in between. `scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 <command>` runs the repo's own `funke.exe editor`:

```powershell
scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 status -Project <dir>                  # scene, edit/play, script build + errors, game surface
scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 play --size 1080x2400 -Project <dir>   # Play mode, game laid out for that screen
scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 screenshot bin-int\_agent\run\p.png    # offscreen render of the game camera (works minimized)
scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 tap 0.5 0.4 ; ... key Space ; ... drag 0.5 0.7 0.5 0.4 ; ... input run.json
scripts\dev\Editor.ps1 exec "physics.debug on" ; ... recompile ; ... logs --level warning ; ... stop
```

Nothing on the desktop changes (no focus/move, no OS input). Exit codes: 1 failed, 3 busy/timeout, 4 no editor. With several editors open, `--project`/`-Project` picks one; never drive the user's own editor unless asked (`funke editor list`). Source: `Funke-Engine/src/DevTools/EditorBridge*` (protocol, pipe), `Funke-Editor/src/Bridge/EditorBridgeLayer.*` (commands), `Funke-CLI/src/Commands/EditorCommand.cpp`. Doc: `Github-Docs/Documentation/Editor/Editor-Bridge.md`.

## Definition of done

Build the smallest affected consumer when compilation adds evidence; select the relevant `Test.ps1 -Suite` and filter for behavior changes. For UI/rendering/runtime changes, reproduce with `Run.ps1` or the Editor Bridge and inspect the resulting screenshots and log warnings. Documentation-only edits need document/reference checks. Report what was checked and anything that could not be verified.

## Pitfalls

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Fix has no effect in the editor | Stale `Funke-Engine.dll` in `bin\<cfg>\Funke-Editor\`, or user runs Release while you built Debug. Build.ps1 deploys; check the config. |
| `LNK1104 cannot open ...\X.obj` | Another session/VS is building the same tree concurrently. Rerun. |
| `LNK2019` from Editor/Runtime for an engine symbol | Missing `FUNKE_API` (`Funke-Engine/src/Core/Export.hpp`). |
| Every edit rebuilds the whole engine | Something in `pch.hpp` changes per build. Never include `Core/BuildIdentity.hpp` from headers/PCH; use `Engine::GetVersionLong()`. |
| `C1060` out of heap / `C2471` PDB | Historical; fixed by `/Z7` + `CL_MPCount`/`UseMultiToolTask` in `Directory.Build.props`. Don't add `/Zm`, `/Zi`, `/ZI`. |
| New `.cpp` not compiled | Premake regen (Build.ps1 does it for native project sources). Package `.cpp` / `funke-package.lua`: `Build.ps1 -Regen`. |
| Measuring build times | Never point `-p:IntDir` at `%TEMP%` (FileTracker ignores it → always full rebuild). |
| C4251 / C4275 warnings | Permanent DLL-interface noise; filtered. |

## Linux and macOS

No PowerShell scripts there; use premake's gmake workspace directly (premake 5.0.0-beta5+; `gmake2` is the old name). Folders are `bin/<Config>-linux-x86_64`, `bin/<Config>-macosx-arm64` (Apple Silicon) or `-macosx-x86_64` (premake/architecture.lua).

```bash
./scripts/Setup.sh                      # tools (apt/dnf/pacman/zypper or Homebrew), SDL3, libnethost, premake gmake
./scripts/dawn/SetupDawn.sh             # once: libwebgpu_dawn.so/.dylib (Clang)
make config=release -j8 Funke-Launcher  # Engine, Funke-Managed (dotnet: ScriptCore, ScriptCompiler, PackageTool), Editor, Runtime, CLI, EngineSDK
make config=dist Funke-Runtime          # Runtime-Dist for Release exports (before the Launcher)
make config=release Funke-Engine-Tests Funke-Editor-Tests && ./bin/Release-linux-x86_64/Funke-Engine-Tests/Funke-Engine-Tests
python3 scripts/PackagePosix.py         # Funke-Editor-<version>-<Linux|macOS>-<arch>.tar.gz
```

- gmake can't build SDK-style C#: the `Funke-Managed` Makefile project runs `scripts/BuildManaged.py`; consumers depend on it via `FunkeManagedDependencies()`.
- The Launcher postbuild is `scripts/CopyEngineSdk.py` (the `.bat`'s POSIX twin). Keep both copy lists in sync.
- On this Windows machine, WSL Ubuntu can build Linux (`wsl -d Ubuntu`); build in the WSL filesystem, not under `/mnt/c` (9P is slow). Keep `-j` at ~6: more parallel g++ jobs have crashed the WSL VM (out of memory) and left truncated `.o` files that fail to link with "unknown file type".
- Premake scripts must parse on beta5 and newer premake: use `FunkeMultiProcessorCompile()` / `FunkeNoPCH()` (premake/compat.lua), not `flags { ... }`, and `FunkePython()` for Python commands.
- macOS can't be built here; CI's `macos-build` job (macos-14, arm64) covers it.

## Fresh clone / setup

`scripts\Setup.bat` (wraps `python scripts/Setup.py`; `-y` to auto-approve installs): checks Python ≥3.10, MSVC v143, .NET 10 SDK (`global.json` pins 10.0.100, rollForward latestFeature), premake, git submodules under `External/`, LFS, then generates `Funke.sln` and the `.vcxproj` files (git-ignored). Dawn/WebGPU setup lives in `scripts/dawn/`. SDL3 (window/input/platform layer, `External/SDL` submodule) is built by `python scripts/sdl/SetupSDL.py` into `External/SDL-build/<target>-<arch>/install`; Setup runs it with `--if-missing`, and a link error on `SDL3.lib` means it hasn't run. Release packaging: `scripts/BuildWindows.ps1`, `scripts/VerifyRelease.ps1`.

# Funke C++ Code Style

Conventions as they exist in the code today. When this skill and the surrounding file disagree, match the file. Comments: follow `funke-comment-style` (terse why-not-what, one line) — not repeated here.

## Naming

| Element | Convention | Real examples |
|---|---|---|
| Class / struct / enum | PascalCase | `Renderer2D`, `TextureManager`, `SpriteRendererComponent`, `enum class BlendMode` |
| Method / free function | PascalCase | `Initialize()`, `RenderSceneWithVP()`, `GetDefaultTexture()` |
| Non-static member | `m_` + PascalCase | `m_IsInitialized`, `m_PostProcessor`, `m_SceneFbo` |
| Static member | `s_` + PascalCase | `s_Textures`, `s_IsInitialized`, `s_CoreLogger` |
| Constant (`constexpr`/`static const`) | `k_` + PascalCase | `k_InvalidIndex`, `k_MaxQueryCells`, `k_RadixSortMinElements` |
| TU-local global (anonymous namespace) | `g_` + PascalCase | `g_InstancesScratch`, `g_BindGroupCache`, `g_SamplingHz` |
| `thread_local` | `t_` + PascalCase | `t_DispatchingOnLog`, `t_WorkerIndex` |
| Public data field | PascalCase, no prefix | `Position`, `SortingOrder`, `TextureHandle`, `RenderScale` |
| Local / parameter | camelCase | `viewportAABB`, `fboWidth`, `runHandle` |
| Template parameter | `T` or `T`-prefixed | `T`, `TComponent`, `TEntity` |
| Enum values | PascalCase | `PolygonMode::Wireframe`, `Filter::Point` |
| Namespace | `Funke` root; PascalCase sub-namespaces for internal surfaces | `Funke::WebGPUBackend`, `Funke::WebGPUSpriteResources`, `Funke::Diagnostics`, `Funke::ScriptBindingGuard` |

Getters `Get*()` / `Is*()` / `Has*()`, setters `Set*()`. No `get_`/`set_`. Dawn's own `kDepthSliceUndefined`-style names are third-party, not house style.

### Macro families (two prefixes — pick by family, don't invent a third)

- `FNK_` — core engine macros: logging (`FNK_CORE_WARN_TAG`), asserts (`FNK_ASSERT`, `FNK_VERIFY`), `FNK_THROW`, platform/config (`FNK_PLATFORM_WINDOWS`, `FNK_DEBUG`/`FNK_RELEASE`/`FNK_DIST`), build (`FNK_BUILD_DLL`, `FNK_IMPORT_DLL`, `FNK_BUILD_ID`), helpers (`FNK_FORCE_INLINE`, `FNK_BIND_EVENT_FN`, `FNK_GUARDED_BINDING`).
- `FUNKE_` — export/API and feature/module gates: `FUNKE_API` (+ aliases `FUNKE_RENDER_API`, `FUNKE_AUDIO_API`, … all identical to `FUNKE_API`), `FUNKE_WITH_RENDER`/`_AUDIO`/`_PHYSICS`/`_SCRIPTING`/`_APPLICATION`/`_EDITOR`, `FUNKE_PROFILER_ENABLED`, `FUNKE_PROFILE_*`, `FUNKE_TRY_CATCH_LOG`, `FUNKE_ENTITY_BITS`.
- Old `IDX_`/`INDEX_` (pre-2026-10-16 "Index" name) and `AIM_`/`AXIOM_` names are gone; never write them.

## Files, headers, PCH

```cpp
#pragma once                       // always; no include guards
#include "Core/Export.hpp"         // whenever the header uses FUNKE_API
#include "Graphics/TextureHandle.hpp"
#include <glm/glm.hpp>
#include <vector>

namespace Funke {
	class FUNKE_API Thing { ... };
} // namespace Funke
```

- Engine include paths are relative to `Funke-Engine/src`, quoted: `"Graphics/Renderer2D.hpp"`.
- `.cpp` include order: PCH line (if the project needs one) → own header → engine headers → third-party (`<webgpu/webgpu_cpp.h>`, `<glm/...>`, `<imgui.h>`) → std.
- Indentation: tabs in most engine files; a few older headers use 4 spaces — match the file you're in.

**PCH per project — this differs by project:**

| Project | PCH | What a new `.cpp` must do |
|---|---|---|
| `Funke-Engine` | `pch.hpp` / `src/pch.cpp` (not force-included) | First line `#include "pch.hpp"` or it won't compile |
| `Funke-Editor` | `EditorPch.hpp` via `forceincludes` | Nothing — it's force-included (existing files still start with `#include <pch.hpp>`, harmless) |
| `Funke-Runtime`, `Funke-Launcher`, `Funke-EditorRuntime`, `Funke-CLI` | none | Include what you use |

`Funke-Engine/src/pch.hpp` deliberately stops at STL + `Core/` (`Assert`, `Base`, `Log`, `Exceptions`, `Version`; `<Windows.h>` with `NOMINMAX` on Windows). Don't add `<imgui.h>`, `Core/Application.hpp`, `magic_enum`, or anything that changes per build (build identity / dirty fingerprint) — the file's own comment records why. New source files: `scripts\dev\Build.ps1` regenerates premake automatically (`scripts\Setup.bat` is the full, interactive first-time setup, not a regen step); see `funke-build-engine`.

## DLL boundary (`FUNKE_API`)

- `Funke-Engine` is a SharedLib built with `FNK_BUILD_DLL` (→ `__declspec(dllexport)`). Editor, Runtime, Launcher, EditorRuntime, CLI and `native` package layers define `FNK_IMPORT_DLL`.
- Anything called from another binary needs `FUNKE_API` on the class/struct or free function. Missing it shows up as LNK2019 in the *consumer*, not the engine.
- Do **not** mark types whose `.cpp` is compiled directly into each consumer (e.g. `Diagnostics/StatsOverlay`, `Funke-Editor/src/Gui/ProfilerPanel.cpp` shared into Runtime) — that also gives LNK2019.
- Static state shared across the boundary must be defined out-of-line in a `.cpp`. `inline static` in a header gives the EXE and the DLL separate copies (see the note in `Core/Log.hpp`).
- `FUNKE_API` types with `std::` members trigger C4251; that's accepted. Engine-internal structs that never cross the boundary omit `FUNKE_API` (see `GizmoText` in `Graphics/Gizmo.hpp`).

## Compile-time gates

```cpp
#if FUNKE_WITH_RENDER          // module gates are 0/1 — use #if, never #ifdef
#ifdef FUNKE_PROFILER_ENABLED  // profiler is defined/undefined — use #ifdef (see funke-add-profiler)
#ifdef FNK_PLATFORM_WINDOWS    // exactly one of _WINDOWS/_LINUX/_MACOS/_ANDROID/_IOS/_WEB is defined (Core/PlatformDetection.hpp) — give every platform a branch or fallback
#if FNK_PLATFORM_MOBILE        // 0/1 helpers, use #if: _MOBILE, _DESKTOP, _POSIX, _HAS_PROCESSES, _HAS_DYNAMIC_LIBRARIES, _HAS_THREADS
#if defined(FNK_DEBUG) || defined(FNK_RELEASE)   // dev builds; FNK_DIST = shipped
```

Module gates come from `Core/Export.hpp` (`FUNKE_ALL_MODULES` forces all except `FUNKE_WITH_EDITOR`, which premake sets per config so Dist strips editor-only systems). Files of a disabled module are removed in `Funke-Engine/premake5.lua` (`RemoveFilesIfModuleDisabled`).

Engine feature modules `Funke.2D` / `Funke.3D` are a second, finer layer: `FUNKE_WITH_2D` / `FUNKE_WITH_3D` (default 1; runtime variants built with `premake5 --without-2d|--without-3d` or CMake `MODULES` set 0) and their file lists in `Funke-Engine/EngineModules.json`. Core code that touches a module type includes its headers and uses it only inside `#if FUNKE_WITH_2D` (2D-module headers may pull in Box2D, which isn't on the include path then), and additionally checks `EngineModules::IsActive(EngineModule::TwoD)` (`Core/EngineModules.hpp`) where the project setting must switch behaviour at runtime (systems, renderers, default transform). Verify a gate by compiling the TU in a variant: `premake5 --without-2d vs2022`, then MSBuild `premake/generated/variant-3d/Funke-Engine/Funke-Engine.vcxproj -t:ClCompile -p:SelectedFiles=..\..\..\..\Funke-Engine\src\<path>.cpp`.

## Class layout

```cpp
class FUNKE_API MyThing {
public:
	MyThing();
	~MyThing();
	MyThing(const MyThing&) = delete;              // GPU/backend owners are move-only
	MyThing& operator=(const MyThing&) = delete;

	void Initialize();
	bool IsInitialized() const { return m_IsInitialized; }
	static void Helper();

private:
	void Internal();

	bool m_IsInitialized = false;                  // members last, with default initializers
	friend class Renderer2D;
};
```

Static-only managers (`TextureManager`, `ShaderManager`, `RenderApi`, `Profiler`) use `static` methods + `s_` state, and either `= delete` the constructor or keep it private.

## Components

Mostly plain `struct FUNKE_API XComponent` with public PascalCase fields and default member initializers (`SpriteRendererComponent`). Components with derived state are classes with `m_` members and accessors (`Camera2DComponent`, `ParticleSystem2DComponent`). No virtual dispatch (`Physics/Collider2D` is the one exception). Registration, serialization and inspector wiring: `funke-add-component`, `funke-serialize-field`, `funke-inspector-ruleset`.

## Error handling

- **Asserts are live in every configuration.** `FNK_ASSERT` / `FNK_CORE_ASSERT` / `FNK_VERIFY` / `FNK_CORE_VERIFY` (`Core/Assert.hpp`) all call `ReportAssertionFailure`: Debug and Release log, trigger `FNK_DEBUG_BREAK` (`__debugbreak()` on Windows, `raise(SIGTRAP)` elsewhere), then call `std::terminate()` if execution resumes; Dist logs and **continues**. So code after an assert must not crash if the condition is false in a shipped build.
- Signature: `FNK_ASSERT(cond, "message")` or `FNK_ASSERT(cond, FunkeErrorCode::X, "message")`. The message is a plain string, **not** a format string — use `fmt::format(...)` for values. Codes: `Core/FunkeErrorCode.hpp` (`InvalidArgument`, `NotInitialized`, `AlreadyInitialized`, `FileNotFound`, `InvalidHandle`, `OutOfRange`, `OutOfBounds`, `Overflow`, `NullReference`, `LoadFailed`, `InvalidValue`, `Undefined`).
- **Exceptions:** `FNK_THROW(code, msg)` throws `FunkeException` (`Core/Exceptions.hpp`). Used for API misuse, e.g. `Scene::GetComponent<T>` throws on an invalid entity or a missing component (use `HasComponent` / `TryGetComponent` when absence is normal). Application loops wrap layer and renderer calls in `FUNKE_TRY_CATCH_LOG(stmt)`.
- **Never let a C++ exception reach CoreCLR.** Native script bindings are registered through `FNK_GUARDED_BINDING(fn)` (`Scripting/ScriptBindingGuard.hpp`), a noexcept thunk that logs and returns `R{}`.
- **Recoverable problems:** log (`FNK_CORE_WARN_TAG`) and early-return. Early return beats nesting.

## Logging

fmt-style, compile-time checked (`fmt::format_string`): `FNK_CORE_WARN_TAG("Renderer2D", "No pipeline for format {}", fmt)`. A runtime `std::string` can only be passed as the sole message argument (non-template overload); never build messages with `+` and then add format args. `FNK_CORE_*` → stdout + log file only; `FNK_*` (client) → also the editor Console. Levels: `TRACE/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL`. Full table and where output lands: `funke-debug`.

## Resource management

- Ownership: `std::unique_ptr` (`Base.hpp` has a `Scope<T>`/`CreateScope` alias — effectively unused; don't spread it). Scenes are `shared_ptr` owned by `SceneManager` and handed out as `std::weak_ptr<Scene>`.
- Pooled handles with generation counters instead of pointers: `TextureHandle`, `ShaderHandle`, `FontHandle`, `AudioHandle`; entities are `EntityHandle` (EnTT). Validate (`TextureManager::IsValid(h)`) before use.
- GPU objects are move-only RAII wrappers over Dawn handles (`Framebuffer`, `Texture2D`, `Shader`). Anything holding a Dawn handle in a global/static must be released in an explicit `Shutdown()` before `RenderApi::Shutdown` — letting it die in DLL-unload statics aborts in the D3D12 driver. See `funke-rendering`.

## C# (Funke-ScriptCore) in brief

File-scoped `namespace Funke;`, nullable enabled, PascalCase public API, `internal` for interop plumbing (`Funke.Interop.InternalCalls`). Engine-side binding work: `funke-engine-scripting`; game-facing API: `funke-game-scripting`.

Triggers on "comment", "// why", "doc comment", "XML doc", "verbose comments", "comment cleanup", "explain this code", "trim comments", or any time you are about to write a `//` / `/* */` block in `Funke-Engine/`, `Funke-Editor/`, `Funke-Runtime/`, `Funke-Launcher/`, `Funke-ScriptCore/`, or a package layer. # Skill: Funke Comment Style

How comments are written in the Funke engine. The bar is high: **most code gets no comment**, and the ones that exist are one terse line that says something the code cannot.

## The core rule

A comment explains **WHY**, never **WHAT**. The code already says what it does. A comment earns its place only by adding information the reader cannot get from the code itself:

- a non-obvious **rationale** ("why this and not the obvious alternative"),
- an **ordering / sequencing constraint** ("must run before X because X mutates shared state"),
- a **footgun / gotcha** that will bite the next editor,
- an **invariant** the code relies on but doesn't enforce,
- a **workaround** for an external bug (OS / driver / library / ABI),
- a **unit / domain** that isn't obvious from the type (pixels vs world units, etc.).

If a comment isn't doing one of those, delete it.

## Length

- **One line.** Two only if genuinely irreducible (e.g. two independent constraints).
- If you're writing a **3rd consecutive comment line, stop** — you're narrating the code. A run of 4+ comment lines is almost always an essay to cut down to one line or zero.
- No paragraphs. No multi-sentence build-up. State the fact and move on.

## Delete on sight

- Comments that **narrate the next line(s)**: `// loop over entities and draw each` above an obvious loop.
- Comments that **restate an identifier**: `// the renderer` above `auto* renderer = ...`.
- **Decorative banners / ASCII dividers**: `// ─────────`, `// ===== Section =====`. (A single short `// Section` label is fine if it genuinely aids navigation in a long function; the divider art is not.)
- **Doc comments that echo the signature**: `/// Returns the width.` over `int GetWidth()`.
- **History / changelog narration**: `// Changed this to fix the thing in the other PR`.
- Standard language/library behavior explanations ("std::vector grows by doubling…").

## Style

- **English**, always — match the codebase. Never translate comments to another language.
- Terse and declarative. Drop filler ("basically", "note that", "here we", "this function").
- Place the comment directly above the construct it explains.
- A trailing inline `code; // x` is fine for a quick per-line note; don't grow it into a block.

## C# XML doc (`///` summary comments)

- Keep only if it states a **real contract** the caller can't infer (thread-safety, ownership, "call X before Y", null/empty semantics).
- Compress to a **one-line summary**. Delete the boilerplate param/returns lines that just restate the names.
- If it only echoes the method name/signature, delete it entirely.

## ⚠️ Escape-sequence trap (hard-won)

When a comment needs to mention an escape sequence, **write it as a word** — `newline`, `tab`, `backslash` — **never put a literal `\n`, `\t`, or `\\` in the comment text.**

Reason: when this comment is later edited or compressed (by a person or a tool whose replacement string is JSON/escaped), the `\n` can decode into a **real newline** and tear the comment across two physical lines. The second line is then no longer a comment → it breaks compilation, often cascading (a torn comment above an `enum`/`struct` takes down every file that includes the header). This actually happened during a bulk comment pass and broke the engine build.

```cpp
// BAD  — a later edit can turn the \n into a real line break:
// Wire format: items joined by '\n', backslashes escaped as '\\'.

// GOOD — wording carries the meaning, nothing to mis-decode:
// Wire format: items joined by newlines; embedded newline/backslash chars are backslash-escaped.
```

## Hard rules (never break)

- **Never delete or alter a line of real code** while editing a comment. Comment-only edits must keep the file compiling.
- Never leave a dangling `/*` or `*/`. Don't touch `//` or `/* */` that live **inside string literals** (e.g. WGSL shader source in `R"WGSL(...)"`, glob patterns like `"Source/*.cpp"`) — those aren't comments.
- Commented-out code: delete it if it's clearly dead; leave it only if it's an intentional reference/toggle.
- After any bulk comment change, **build** (`funke-build-engine` skill) — a torn comment or an accidentally-eaten code line only shows up at compile time. A `/* */` balance check catches unterminated blocks but not single-line `//` tears.

## Before / after (real engine examples)

**DELETE — pure narration:**
```cpp
// Push the scene's stored editor-time field values onto the freshly-created
// managed instance. Mirrors how ScriptComponent flushes PendingFieldValues …
void ApplyFieldOverrides(Scene& scene)        // ← signature already says this; delete the block
```

**COMPRESS — keep the one real constraint (33 lines → 1):**
```cpp
// MUST precede the render call: SetSize above mutates the shared MainViewport
// that UI systems fall back to, so publishing the region first pins layout to renderSize.
```

**COMPRESS — keep the gotcha (8 lines → 1):**
```cpp
// Sprites-only: only the sprite pipeline honours wireframe; overlays would paint filled quads over it.
```

## Quick test before keeping a comment

Ask: *"Would a competent engineer reading this code already know this?"* If yes → delete. If the answer is a non-obvious why/constraint/footgun → keep it, in one line.

# Debugging Funke

Read the log first; most failures are already explained there.

## Where output goes

| Sink | What lands there |
|---|---|
| **Log file** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\Logs\<exe-stem>.log` on Windows (`Funke-Editor.log`, `Funke-Runtime.log`, `Funke-Launcher.log`, …) | Every logger, every level. Active file plus up to three rotated backups, 10 MiB each, flushed on Warn+. Best-effort (skipped if the path can't be opened); disabled on Web. Set up in `Funke-Engine/src/Core/Log.cpp`. |
| stdout (console) | Same as the file, colored. |
| Android / Web | Android also writes to logcat with tag `Funke` (`adb logcat -s Funke`). Web writes to the browser console and has no file sink. Non-Windows file logs use `Path::GetSpecialFolderPath(SpecialFolder::LocalAppData)/Funke/Logs` (platform user-data root). |
| Editor **Console** panel | Client (`APP`) and `EDITOR` loggers only. **`FNK_CORE_*` never appears there** (filtered by the `Log::OnLog` subscriber in `ImGuiEditorLayer::OnAttach`). |
| Shipped runtime | F7 log overlay (`Funke-Runtime/src/RuntimeLogLayer.cpp`, when `showRuntimeLogs`), F6 stats overlay, Ctrl+F6 profiler (when `profiler.enableInRuntime`). |
| `funke editor logs` (Editor Bridge) | The last 4000 lines of **one open editor** (core + game), per process: `--level warning`, `--contains <text>`, `--since <n>` (number from the previous answer), `--follow`. The shared `Funke-Editor.log` mixes every editor instance; this doesn't. Reproduce in that editor with `funke editor play` / `input` / `exec` (`funke-build-engine`). |

File line format: `[HH:MM:SS] [FUNKE] [level] [Tag] message` — logger names `FUNKE` (core), `APP` (client), `EDITOR`; level is `trace|debug|info|warning|error|critical` (console omits the level and colors it instead). Problems only: pattern `\] \[(warning|error|critical)\] `. To reproduce and capture a clean slice of the log plus a screenshot, use `scripts\dev\Run.ps1` (see `funke-build-engine`). As an agent, `Grep` the log file instead of asking the user to paste console output, e.g. pattern `\[WebGPUApi\]|\[CrashReporter\]|ASSERT failed|Exception:` on `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Funke\Logs\Funke-Editor.log`.

## Logging macros (`Core/Log.hpp`)

```cpp
FNK_CORE_INFO_TAG("TextureManager", "Loaded {} textures", count);   // engine internals: stdout + file
FNK_CORE_WARN_TAG("Renderer2D", "No pipeline for format {}", fmt);
FNK_CORE_ERROR_TAG("WebGPUApi", "RequestAdapter failed: {}", err);
FNK_WARN_TAG("Game", "Player spawned at ({}, {})", p.x, p.y);       // client: also editor Console
FNK_CONSOLE_LOG_INFO("...");                                        // EDITOR logger (currently unused in-tree)
```

- Levels: `TRACE`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`, `FATAL` (→ spdlog critical). There is no `CRITICAL` macro.
- Families: `FNK_CORE_<LVL>[_TAG]`, `FNK_<LVL>[_TAG]`, `FNK_CONSOLE_LOG_<LVL>` (no `_TAG` variant).
- Format strings are compile-time checked fmt. A prebuilt `std::string` may only be passed alone (`FNK_INFO_TAG("Window", msg)`); never concatenate and then add `{}` args.
- C# `Log.Info/Warn/Error` → client logger with tag `Script` (`ScriptBindingsScene.cpp`), so it shows in the Console and the log file.
- Use a `_TAG` with the subsystem/class name so the file is greppable.

## Assertions — live in every config

`Core/Assert.hpp` / `Core/Assert.cpp`:

```cpp
FNK_CORE_ASSERT(Application::IsMainThread(), FunkeErrorCode::Undefined, "AudioManager::Update must be called on the main thread");
FNK_VERIFY(Window::IsInitialized(), "preserved window requires initialized SDL video");
FNK_ASSERT(ptr, FunkeErrorCode::NullReference, fmt::format("Widget {} was null", id)); // message is NOT a format string
```

- `FNK_ASSERT`, `FNK_CORE_ASSERT`, `FNK_VERIFY`, `FNK_CORE_VERIFY` are all compiled in all configurations and behave the same: log `<KIND> failed: (expr) | [Code] msg @ file:line (function)` as a core error, then
  - **Debug and Release:** `FNK_DEBUG_BREAK` (`__debugbreak()` on Windows, `raise(SIGTRAP)` elsewhere), followed by `std::terminate()` if execution resumes. Windows failures are captured by the crash reporter; POSIX `SIGTRAP` is not among its installed fatal-signal handlers.
  - **Dist:** log and **continue**. Code after the assert still runs in shipped builds.
- Grep the log for `ASSERT failed` / `VERIFY failed` to find the site.

## Exceptions

- `FNK_THROW(code, msg)` → `FunkeException` (`Core/Exceptions.hpp`). Notable thrower: `Scene::GetComponent<T>` on an invalid entity (`Cannot get component from invalid entity.`) or a missing component (`Component of type '...' not found on entity.`).
- `Application` wraps layer callbacks and renderer/gizmo/gui begin/end in `FUNKE_TRY_CATCH_LOG`, so these usually surface as a core `Exception: <what>` line, not a crash. The frame keeps going with partial work.
- Exceptions thrown from script callbacks log `Exception in OnUpdate(): ...` in full three times per callback + type + throw site, then a `... repeated N more time(s) in the last 5s` summary (`ScriptExceptionLog.cs`); the first report is the one to read.
- Native script bindings go through `FNK_GUARDED_BINDING` (`Scripting/ScriptBindingGuard.hpp`): a throw logs `[ScriptBinding] exception in <signature>: ...` and returns a default value to C#.

## Crash dumps (`Core/CrashReporter.{hpp,cpp}`)

- Installed by `InitializeCore()` (`Core/Base.cpp`) right after `Log::Initialize()`.
- Windows: unhandled SEH exceptions, `std::terminate`, pure-virtual calls, CRT invalid-parameter and `SIGABRT` all write a minidump (data segs + indirectly referenced memory + thread info) to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\CrashDumps\<exe-stem>_<FNK_BUILD_ID>_<timestamp>.dmp`
  and log `[CrashReporter] Wrote minidump to <path>` (FATAL) before flushing. Only the first crashing thread writes a dump. `FNK_BUILD_ID` (e.g. `2026.1.0-beta.1+29bd8b4d6bdb.dirty.<hash>`) names the commit the binary came from.
- Linux/macOS: fatal signals (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGABRT`, `SIGFPE`, `SIGILL`, `SIGBUS`, on an alternate stack) and `std::terminate` print `[Funke] fatal signal: ...` / `[Funke] std::terminate called` to stderr and write a text report `<exe-stem>-<timestamp>.crash.txt` (version, commit, reason, symbolized backtrace) into the same `Funke/CrashDumps` folder under the platform's local-app-data dir. No minidump. Other platforms only get the stderr line.
- Open a `.dmp` in Visual Studio (File > Open), "Debug with Native Only", symbol path = the matching `bin\<Config>-windows-x86_64\<Project>\` folder. Debug/Release always have PDBs; in Dist only `Funke-Engine` and `Funke-Runtime` (the shipped game) keep symbols, Editor/Launcher Dist don't.
- The editor also autosaves unsaved scenes every 30 s to `<project>/.funke/Recovery` and offers Restore on next open.

## Common failure modes

1. **Nothing renders / black view** — no main camera: `Camera2DComponent::GetMain()` resolves through the active scene (`Scene::GetMainCamera()`, first `Camera2DComponent` without `DisabledTag`); if it's null or `!IsValid()`, `Renderer2D::BeginFrame` returns early. A sprite with an invalid texture handle still draws (falls back to the default Square texture), so "invisible" usually means camera, culling, sorting layer, or alpha.
2. **WebGPU errors** — there is no OpenGL/`glGetError` anymore. Dawn errors arrive through the device callbacks in `Graphics/Backend/WebGPUApi.cpp`: `[WebGPUApi] WebGPU [Validation]: ...`, `[OutOfMemory]`, `[Internal]`, or `Device lost (...)`. Startup lines report `D3D compiler preload`, `Vulkan loader preload`, `RequestAdapter failed`, and the chosen adapter/backend. Pass-level causes and fixes: `funke-rendering`.
3. **Stale entity handle** — check `scene.IsValid(handle)`; use `HasComponent<T>` / `TryGetComponent<T>(e, ptr)` when absence is expected.
4. **Main-thread asserts** — `AudioManager`, `RenderSettings` and others assert or return `WrongThread` off the main thread; job-system workers (`Jobs/`) must not call them.
5. **Missing engine assets** — `FunkeAssets` resolves next to the exe, then one level up (`bin\<cfg>\FunkeAssets`) via `Path::ResolveFunkeAssets`. Log line: `FunkeAssets root not resolved — default textures unavailable`. Project assets resolve by GUID: `funke-assets-and-content`.
6. **"My fix has no effect"** — the editor loads `bin\<cfg>\Funke-Editor\Funke-Engine.dll`; building `Funke-Engine.vcxproj` alone leaves the old DLL there. Copy/rebuild per `funke-build-engine`.
7. **Cryptic compile errors in a new engine `.cpp`** — missing `#include "pch.hpp"` as the first line (`funke-code-style`).
8. **Startup assert about an EnTT group** — something else created an owning group over `Transform2DComponent` / `SpriteRendererComponent`; `Renderer2D` owns that pair (`funke-rendering`).

## Memory

- Global `new`/`delete` tracking only in **Debug on Windows** (`FNK_TRACK_MEMORY` + `FNK_DEBUG`, `Core/Memory.cpp`). `Allocator::GetAllocationStats()` returns `std::map<std::string, AllocationStats>` (per category; fields `TotalAllocated`, `TotalFreed`).
- Cheaper signals in any dev build: profiler modules `Total Memory` (working set MB), `Texture Memory` (`TextureManager::GetTotalTextureMemoryBytes()`), `Entity Count`; the stats overlay shows process working set and private commit.
- Frame arenas (`Memory/FrameArenas`) reset every frame — spans built from them (e.g. gizmo geometry) must not be cached across frames.

## One-shot timing

```cpp
#include "Utils/Timer.hpp"
Timer t;  /* work */  FNK_CORE_INFO_TAG("Perf", "Took {} ms", t.ElapsedMilliseconds());
// also ElapsedSeconds(), ElapsedMicroseconds(), Reset(), Pause()/Continue()

#include "Utils/ScopedTimer.hpp"
{ ScopedTimer st("Perf", "Rebuild atlas"); /* work */ }  // logs "<desc> - <n>ms" via FNK_INFO_TAG (client → Console)
```

For anything that should stay in the code or show in the Profiler panel / Tracy, use `FUNKE_PROFILE_SCOPE` (`funke-add-profiler`).

## Overlays

`Funke-Engine/src/Diagnostics/StatsOverlay` (FPS, CPU main ms, render-thread ms, tris/verts, screen size, working set, private commit, playing audio, entities) and `LogOverlay`. Compiled into Editor and Runtime directly (excluded from the engine DLL). Runtime: F6 stats, F7 logs, Ctrl+F6 profiler. Editor: Ctrl+F6 opens the Profiler panel; the Game View hosts the stats/log overlays.

## Debugger

1. Open `Funke.sln` in VS2022. Startup project `Funke-Editor`; Debugging > Command Arguments: `--project="C:\path\to\MyGame"` (without it the editor logs `No project specified` and runs on fallback paths). `Funke-Runtime` takes the same `--project=`; `Funke-Launcher` needs none.
2. Debug = unoptimized; Release = optimized **with** symbols (best for perf issues); Dist = fully optimized, symbols only for Engine/Runtime.
3. C# scripts run on CoreCLR inside the editor process: attach to `Funke-Editor.exe` with the **Managed (.NET Core)** code type (or Native + Managed for mixed stacks).
4. Repro in tests where possible: `scripts\dev\Test.ps1 [-Filter "*Name*"] [-Suite CSharp|All]` (`funke-build-engine`). Not `scripts\RunTests.bat` locally: it picks MSBuild via `vswhere -latest`, which is VS "18" on this machine (PCH clash with v143), and builds serially; it's the CI entry point.

# Funke Engine Scripting (host, bridge, bindings, hot reload)

How the engine hosts .NET, how C++ and C# call each other, and how to add a binding end to end. The **game-author API** (`EntityScript`, `SceneSystem`, `GlobalSystem`, `Input`, `Physics2D`, …) is documented in `funke-game-scripting` — don't duplicate it here.

## File map

| Side | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptRuntimeHost.{hpp,cpp}` | Runtime backend interface (`Initialize`, `GetUnmanagedEntryPoint`); `ScriptRuntimeHosts::CreatePreferred()` picks the highest-priority registered backend (`FUNKE_SCRIPT_RUNTIME` overrides), else desktop `HostFxrScriptRuntime`; Android/iOS/Web link one from a package (Funke.ScriptRuntime.Mono) |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/DotNetHost.{hpp,cpp}` | Used by the hostfxr backend: loads hostfxr, inits CoreCLR from `<stem>.runtimeconfig.json` next to the core DLL, `LoadAssemblyAndGetFunction` |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptEngine.{hpp,cpp}` | Static facade: `LoadCoreAssembly`, `LoadUserAssembly`, instance create/invoke wrappers over `ManagedCallbacks`, global systems, data assets |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptGlue.hpp` | `NativeBindings` (C++ fns C# calls) + `ManagedCallbacks` (C# fns C++ calls) + `k_ScriptInteropLayoutVersion` |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindings.hpp` | `ScriptBindings::PopulateNativeBindings(NativeBindings&)` (`FUNKE_SCRIPTING_API`) |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindings.cpp` | Core component bindings (UI widgets, audio, …), entity, scene and gizmo bindings, `GET_COMPONENT` macro, `PopulateNativeBindings` (calls every `Populate*` below) |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindingsScene.cpp` | Application, Window, Engine, Time, Log, Input, … → `PopulateNonComponentBindings` |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindings2D.cpp` / `ScriptBindings3D.cpp` / `ScriptBindingsPhysics3D.cpp` | Funke.2D (Transform2D, sprites, Camera2D, Rigidbody2D, Physics2D, …) / Funke.3D bindings → `Populate2DBindings` / `Populate3DBindings` / `PopulatePhysics3DBindings`, called from `ScriptBindings::PopulateModuleBindings` |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindingModuleSlots.hpp` + `ScriptBindingsModuleStubs.cpp` | `FNK_FOR_EACH_2D_BINDING` / `FNK_FOR_EACH_3D_BINDING` slot lists; inactive modules get signature-matched stubs (`FindUnstubbedModuleSlots` backs the EngineModules test) |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindingsEcb.cpp`, `…Jobs`, `…Material`, `…Animation`, `…Localization`, `…PostProcessing.cpp`, `ScriptEditorGui.cpp` | ECB playback, JobSystem, materials, animation, localization, post-processing, editor GUI → `PopulateEcbBindings`, `PopulateJobsBindings`, … `ScriptEditorGui::PopulateBindings` |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptBindingGuard.hpp` | `FNK_GUARDED_BINDING(fn)` noexcept thunk |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/ScriptSystem.{hpp,cpp}` | `SceneSystem` that boots scripting, watches + rebuilds C#/C++, dispatches lifecycle |
| C++ | `Funke-Engine/src/Scripting/NativeScript*.hpp`, `NativeScriptHost.cpp`, `NativeEngineAPI.hpp` | Native C++ scripts |
| C# | `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Interop/ScriptHostBridge.cs` | `[UnmanagedCallersOnly] Initialize` entry point, `ManagedCallbacksStruct`, `InteropHandshake` |
| C# | `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Interop/NativeCallbacks.cs` | `NativeBindingsStruct` mirror + `NativeCallbacks.Bindings` |
| C# | `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Core/InternalCalls.cs` | `internal static` thunks (namespace `Funke.Interop`, despite living in `Core/`) |
| C# | `Funke-ScriptCore/Source/Funke/Interop/ScriptInstanceManager.cs` | `ScriptAssemblyLoadContext`, type cache, every `ManagedCallbacks` target |

`Funke-ScriptCore` targets **net10.0** with `AllowUnsafeBlocks` (`Funke-ScriptCore/Funke-ScriptCore.csproj`).

## Boot sequence

1. `SceneManager.cpp` adds `ScriptSystem` to every scene definition (`definition.AddSystem<ScriptSystem>()`); `ScriptSystem::Awake` boots scripting once per process.
2. `ScriptEngine::Init()`, then the core DLL is found via `ScriptCoreArtifact::FindFirstCompleteDll({ exeDir, exeDir/../Funke-ScriptCore })`.
3. `ScriptEngine::LoadCoreAssembly`: `s_Host = ScriptRuntimeHosts::CreatePreferred()` → `s_Host->Initialize(coreDll)` (hostfxr backend: `DotNetHost::Initialize(<stem>.runtimeconfig.json)`) → `s_Host->GetUnmanagedEntryPoint(coreDll, "Funke-ScriptCore", "Funke.Interop.ScriptHostBridge", "Initialize")` (hostfxr: `FUNKE_DOTNET_UNMANAGEDCALLERSONLY_METHOD`) → `PopulateNativeBindings` → `initFn(&native, &managed, sizeof(NativeBindings), sizeof(ManagedCallbacks), k_ScriptInteropLayoutVersion)`.
4. Managed side runs `InteropHandshake.Validate` first: `-2` layout version, `-3` NativeBindings size, `-4` ManagedCallbacks size mismatch → native logs "Funke-ScriptCore interop mismatch … Rebuild Funke-Engine and Funke-ScriptCore together. Scripting is disabled." On success it copies the native table, fills every `ManagedCallbacks` slot, runs `ComponentTypes.RunAllStaticInitializers()`, installs `FunkeSynchronizationContext`.
5. User assembly: `project->GetUserAssemblyOutputPath()` = `<project>/bin/<Config>/<Name>.dll` (falls back to a `bin/` scan); no project → `Funke-Sandbox.dll`. `ScriptEngine::LoadUserAssembly` → managed `LoadUserAssembly` loads it **from bytes** (+ `.pdb`) into a collectible `ScriptAssemblyLoadContext` ("FunkeUserScripts") — no file lock, so it can be rebuilt while loaded. Then `DataAssetManager::ReloadAll()` and dynamic-component restore.

**CoreCLR initializes once per process.** `ScriptEngine::Shutdown` never closes the host (only unloads the user assembly), and `LoadCoreAssembly` after init is ignored with a warning. Any change to `Funke-ScriptCore` or the binding tables needs an editor **restart** — only the user assembly hot-reloads.

Type lookup (`ScriptInstanceManager.FindType`) tries `Funke.<name>`, `Funke.Components.<name>`, then `<name>`, user assembly before core. Recognized kinds: `EntityScript`, managed `Component`, `IComponent` structs, `SceneSystem`, `GlobalSystem`, `DataAsset`. Lifecycle goes through virtuals (`OnAwake/OnStart/OnUpdate/OnFixedUpdate/OnDestroy/OnEnable/OnDisable`, collision/trigger); a public parameterless `Start()`/`Update()` is still reflected and invoked as a legacy path.

## The two tables

- **`NativeBindings`** (`ScriptGlue.hpp`) ⇄ **`NativeBindingsStruct`** (`NativeCallbacks.cs`): C++ function pointers C# calls. `[StructLayout(Sequential)]`, `delegate* unmanaged<…>` fields.
- **`ManagedCallbacks`** (`ScriptGlue.hpp`) ⇄ **`ManagedCallbacksStruct`** (`ScriptHostBridge.cs`): C# `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` methods (in `ScriptInstanceManager`) C++ calls via `ScriptEngine::GetCallbacks()` / `s_Callbacks`.

Both are **positional**. The guard is the size check plus `k_ScriptInteropLayoutVersion` (`ScriptGlue.hpp`) / `InteropHandshake.LayoutVersion` (`ScriptHostBridge.cs`), bumped together on any add/remove/reorder. Every slot is a pointer, so *reordering or swapping* two slots keeps the size identical and is caught only if the version was bumped — otherwise C# silently calls the wrong function. **Append new slots at the end of both structs**, preserving identical order; use a short group comment only where useful (`funke-comment-style`). Appending still requires rebuilding both sides because the size/version handshake changes.

## Add a C# → C++ binding (end to end)

Worked example already in the tree: `Application.IsEditor`.

1. **Implement** a `static` free function named `Funke_<Group>_<Action>` in the right file:
   - engine-module component/API (Transform2D, sprites, Camera2D, Physics2D… / Transform3D, meshes, lights, Physics3D…) → `ScriptBindings2D.cpp` / `ScriptBindings3D.cpp` (`ScriptBindingsPhysics3D.cpp`), assigned in `Populate2DBindings` / `Populate3DBindings` / `PopulatePhysics3DBindings`, AND add `X(Slot)` to `FNK_FOR_EACH_2D_BINDING` / `FNK_FOR_EACH_3D_BINDING` in `Scripting/ScriptBindingModuleSlots.hpp` — builds/projects without the module fill those slots with signature-matched stubs (the EngineModules doctest fails on a missing entry)
   - core (module-free) component accessor, e.g. UI widgets or audio → `ScriptBindings.cpp`, using `GET_COMPONENT(Type, entityID, failReturn);` (resolves via `ResolveEntityReference`, re-checks `IsValid` + `HasComponent`, binds `comp`; `ScriptBindings2D.cpp` has its own copy)
   - Application/Window/Engine/Time/Log/Input → `ScriptBindingsScene.cpp`; Scene/Entity/Gizmo → `ScriptBindings.cpp`
   - ECB, jobs, materials, animation, localization, post-processing → the matching `ScriptBindings<Area>.cpp`
   ```cpp
   static int Funke_Application_IsEditor() {            // ScriptBindingsScene.cpp
       return Application::IsEditor() ? 1 : 0;
   }
   static int Funke_SpriteRenderer_GetSortingOrder(uint64_t entityID) {   // ScriptBindings2D.cpp + X(SpriteRenderer_GetSortingOrder) in ScriptBindingModuleSlots.hpp
       GET_COMPONENT(SpriteRendererComponent, entityID, 0);
       return comp.SortingOrder;
   }
   ```
   Blittable signatures only: `int` (bools as `0/1`), `float`, `uint32_t`, `uint64_t` entity IDs, `uint8_t`, `const char*` UTF-8 in, out-pointers (`float* x, float* y`). Strings out use the buffer contract `int X_GetFooBuffer(char* outBuffer, int capacity)` returning the **required byte count** (C# calls with `null, 0` first, then allocates) — helpers `CopyStringToBuffer` (ScriptBindings.cpp) / `CopyToManagedBuffer` (ScriptBindingsScene.cpp).
2. **Slot** — append to the end of `NativeBindings` in `ScriptGlue.hpp`: `int (*Application_IsEditor)();`
3. **Mirror** — append to the end of `NativeBindingsStruct` in `NativeCallbacks.cs`: `public delegate* unmanaged<int> Application_IsEditor;`
   Mapping: `int→int`, `float→float`, `uint32_t→uint`, `uint64_t→ulong`, `uint8_t→byte`, `char*`/`const char*→byte*`, `float*→float*`, `int*→int*`, `void*→void*`; return type is the **last** generic argument (`delegate* unmanaged<ulong, int, void>` = `void f(uint64_t, int)`).
4. **Bump** `k_ScriptInteropLayoutVersion` (`ScriptGlue.hpp`) and `InteropHandshake.LayoutVersion` (`ScriptHostBridge.cs`) together — both comments require it on any add/remove/reorder.
5. **Register** in the matching `Populate*` function: `b.Application_IsEditor = FNK_GUARDED_BINDING(Funke_Application_IsEditor);` — never assign a raw function. The guard (`ScriptBindingGuard::Guard<&fn>::Call`) is `noexcept`, catches any C++ exception (UB if it unwinds into CoreCLR), logs `FNK_CORE_ERROR_TAG("ScriptBinding", …)` and returns `R{}`. An **unassigned slot is a null pointer**: C# calls it without a check → access violation.
6. **Thunk** in `InternalCalls.cs`:
   ```csharp
   internal static bool Application_IsEditor() => NativeCallbacks.Bindings.Application_IsEditor() != 0;
   ```
   Strings: `ReadNativeString(NativeCallbacks.Bindings.X_GetFooBuffer)`; string args: `byte[] buf = EncodeUtf8Z(value); fixed (byte* p = buf) …`.
7. **Public API** — static class (`Core/Application.cs`: `public static bool IsEditor => InternalCalls.Application_IsEditor();`, `Engine.cs`, `Window.cs`, `Input.cs`, `Time.cs`, …) or component wrapper in `Scene/Components.cs` (`InternalCalls.X(RequireComponent<T>())` yields the entity id). A **new** wrapper type also needs its display name in `Entity.s_NativeComponentNames` (`Scene/Entity.cs`) — full component pipeline in `funke-add-component`. XML-doc it (`GenerateDocumentationFile` is on) and update `funke-game-scripting` if it's game-facing.
8. **Rebuild Funke-Engine and Funke-ScriptCore together** and restart the editor (`funke-build-engine`; deploy the fresh `Funke-Engine.dll` to the editor). Tests that touch the bridge: `Tests/Funke-ScriptCore-Tests/InteropHandshakeTests.cs`, `Tests/Funke-Engine-Tests/src/MouseCoordinateTests.cpp` (calls `PopulateNativeBindings` and invokes a slot — a cheap pattern for a binding test).

## Add a C++ → C# callback

1. Append the slot to `ManagedCallbacks` (`ScriptGlue.hpp`) and `ManagedCallbacksStruct` (`ScriptHostBridge.cs`); bump both layout versions.
2. Implement `[UnmanagedCallersOnly] public static` in `ScriptInstanceManager.cs`. Wrap the body in `try/catch` + `Log.Error` — a managed exception escaping an `UnmanagedCallersOnly` method kills the process.
3. Assign it in `ScriptHostBridge.Initialize` (`managedCallbacks->X = &ScriptInstanceManager.X;`).
4. Add a static wrapper on `ScriptEngine` that null-checks: `if (!s_Callbacks.X) return; s_Callbacks.X(...);` (pattern of `ScriptEngine::InvokeUpdate`). Callers use the wrapper, never `s_Callbacks` directly.

## Hot reload (`ScriptSystem`)

**C#** (editor host only — gated on `Application::IsEditor()`):
- `m_ScriptWatcher` watches `Assets/` + `.csproj` + `.sln` for `.cs .csproj .props .targets .sln`; polled from `ScriptSystem::OnPreRender` via `Poll(1.0f)`. Suppress with `SetRecompileSuppressed(true)` (script create/rename) or `ScriptSystem::SetAutoRecompileEnabled(false)`.
- `RebuildAndReloadScripts` runs async on a worker thread. First choice is **in-process Roslyn** (`ManagedScriptCompiler` → `Funke-ScriptCompiler/`, see below); on `Fallback` it runs `dotnet build <csproj> -c <FunkeProject::GetActiveBuildConfiguration()> --nologo -v q -nodeReuse:false -p:UseSharedCompilation=false -p:FunkeCodegenEnabled=false -p:DefineConstants=<BuildManagedDefineConstants("FUNKE_EDITOR")>` (5-minute timeout). A second change while building sets `m_RebuildQueued`.
- On success (`OnPreRender`): `TeardownManagedScripts` for every loaded scene → `ScriptEngine::LoadUserAssembly` → `InitializeRegisteredGlobalSystems` → `PrefabTemplateCache::Get().InvalidateAll()`. Failures log the compiler output (`Compiler output:`) under `ScriptSystem` and set `DidLastRebuildSucceed() == false`.
- Teardown destroys managed instances; Edit-mode reload first captures exposed field values into `PendingFieldValues`. `SnapshotManagedFieldsToPending` deliberately skips Play mode, so do not promise preservation of live runtime state or object identity. Callback loops snapshot handles and revalidate scene/entity/component state because user callbacks can mutate the registry.

**In-process compiler** (`Funke-ScriptCompiler/Source/*.cs`, native side `Scripting/ManagedScriptCompiler.{hpp,cpp}`):
- Editor-only assembly loaded from `<exe>/ScriptCompiler/Funke-ScriptCompiler.dll` (a private copy; `Build.ps1 ScriptCompiler` builds and deploys it, the Editor postbuild and `CopyEngineSdk.bat` copy it when present) via `ScriptEngine::GetUnmanagedEntryPoint` into the editor's CoreCLR. Entry points `CompilerHost.Compile(byte* requestJson) → byte* responseJson` and `FreeResult`. Missing DLL or `FUNKE_SCRIPT_COMPILER=dotnet` → plain `dotnet build`.
- Roslyn is **not shipped**: the csproj references the build SDK's `Roslyn\bincore` with `Private=false`; at run time `CompilerHost.EnsureRoslyn` adds a `Resolving` handler for the SDK MSBuild reports (`RoslynTargetsPath\bincore`). Keep every Roslyn type out of `CompilerHost`/`ProjectEvaluation` — only `RoslynSession` (behind `RoslynBridge`'s NoInlining calls) may touch them.
- `ProjectEvaluation` runs `dotnet msbuild -restore -t:Compile -p:ProvideCommandLineArgs=true -p:SkipCompilerExecution=true -p:NonExistentFile=…` with the same `-p:` switches and reads `CscCommandLineArgs`, `ReferenceCopyLocalPaths`, `TargetPath`, `RoslynTargetsPath` (~1 s). `RoslynSession` parses them with `CSharpCommandLineParser`, caches metadata references and unchanged syntax trees, runs source generators (incremental driver; analyzers are skipped) and writes dll/pdb atomically to `TargetPath`.
- Re-evaluates on: different config/defines, `.cs` files added/removed anywhere in the project (bin/obj skipped). Returns `fallback` (→ dotnet build once) on: `.csproj`/`.props`/`.targets`/`global.json` change in the project root or `Packages/`, a copy-local dependency missing or older in `bin/`, `TargetPath` ≠ the editor's expected output, analyzer load failure, a second project on another SDK. Tests: `Tests/Funke-ScriptCore-Tests/ScriptCompilerTests.cs` (real MSBuild + Roslyn on temp projects).
- `Awake` also rebuilds immediately if `BuildArtifactIsStale` (sources newer than the DLL).
- After a package install etc., call **`ScriptSystem::ReloadManagedAssemblies()`** (tears down live instances, restarts global systems). `ScriptEngine::ReloadAssemblies()` is the low-level swap only — wrong when scenes have live scripts.
- On play-mode exit the editor (`ImGuiEditorLayer.cpp`) calls `ScriptEngine::OnPlayModeExited()`, which strips static-event subscribers from the user assembly.
- Editor overlay hooks: `IsScriptRebuildRunning()`, `IsNativeRebuildRunning()`, `GetActiveRebuildElapsedSeconds()`.

Define sets per compile context are owned by `funke-build-and-ship`.

## Native C++ scripts (still supported)

- Author: `class Foo : public Funke::NativeScript` with `Start()`, `Update()`, `FixedUpdate()`, `OnDestroy()`, then `REGISTER_SCRIPT(Foo)` (`Scripting/NativeScript.hpp`). The protected `m_Scene` pointer provides direct access to the owning scene from lifecycle callbacks; it is null before host binding and must not be reassigned by scripts. Base gives `GetEntityHandle()`, `GetEntityID()`, `GetScene()`, `GetRegistry()`, and `AddComponent/HasComponent/GetComponent/TryGetComponent/RemoveComponent<T>` (via `ComponentUtils`; invalid entity → `FNK_THROW(FunkeErrorCode::InvalidHandle, …)`). Logging: inherited `Print(const std::string&)` forwards to `g_EngineAPI->LogInfo`; `FNK_NATIVE_LOG_INFO/WARN/ERROR(msg)` also log through `g_EngineAPI` (`NativeEngineAPI`: `LogInfo/LogWarn/LogError`, `GetDeltaTime`, `Get/SetPosition`, `Get/SetRotation`). The editor creation template has empty lifecycle callbacks and no example fields. For timing, include `<Core/Time.hpp>` and call `Funke::Time::GetDeltaTime()` or `Funke::Time::GetFixedDeltaTime()`; existing float-parameter overrides must be updated and recompiled.
- Layout: `<project>/NativeScripts/{CMakeLists.txt, Source/, build/}` (`FunkeProject::NativeScriptsDir` / `NativeSourceDir`). C++ files created from the Asset Browser are mirrored into `NativeScripts/Source/`. `EnsureNativeScriptProjectFiles()` writes `Source/NativeScriptExports.cpp` (exports `FunkeInitialize`, `FunkeCreateScript`, `FunkeHasScript`, `FunkeDestroyScript`) and `CMakeLists.txt` — **each only if missing**.
- The generated CMake project (`<Name>-NativeScripts`, C++20, `FUNKE_ALL_MODULES=1`) includes `${FUNKE_DIR}/Funke-Engine/src` and **links `Funke-Engine`** from `${FUNKE_DIR}/bin/<Config>-<platform>/Funke-Engine`. Output: `<project>/bin/<Config>-<platform>/<Name>-NativeScripts/`.
- Load: `NativeScriptHost::LoadDLL` shadow-copies the DLL into `%TEMP%/FunkeNativeScriptHost` before loading (so rebuilds aren't blocked), resolves the four exports, calls `FunkeInitialize(&s_EngineAPI)`.
- Hot reload (editor only): `m_NativeWatcher` → `RebuildAndReloadNativeScripts` → cmake configure (only if `CMakeLists.txt` is newer than the cache) with `-DFUNKE_BUILD_PROFILE=DEVELOPMENT`, then `cmake --build build --config <Config> --target <Name>-NativeScripts`; instances are torn down and recreated (state lost). cmake is resolved from env `FUNKE_CMAKE_PATH` / `CMAKE_COMMAND` / `CMAKE_EXE`, then `PATH`, Program Files, or VS's bundled CMake.
- The Build panel does **not** compile or stage the native-script DLL.

## Pitfalls

- **Inserting a slot mid-struct** or editing only one side → handshake refuses (size) or, for same-size reorders, silently calls the wrong function. Append, mirror, bump version.
- **Raw function in a slot** (no `FNK_GUARDED_BINDING`) → a thrown `FNK_THROW`/`std::exception` unwinds into CoreCLR (UB / crash).
- **Forgot to assign** in `Populate*` → null `delegate*` → AV on first C# call.
- **`Entity_GetComponentPtr` / `Scene_OpenQueryView` pointers** are valid only until the next structural change — never cache them across frames or mutate structure while iterating.
- **Returning `const char*`** — the memory must outlive the call; use the buffer contract (or the thread-local `s_StringReturnBuffer`), never a temporary `std::string`.
- **Expecting ScriptCore to hot-reload** — it can't; restart the editor.
- **Rebuilding only the engine** after a binding change → "interop mismatch … Scripting is disabled." Rebuild both.

## Related skills
`funke-game-scripting` (public C# API), `funke-build-and-ship` (FUNKE_EDITOR / FUNKE_BUILD_* defines), `funke-add-component` (component + C# wrapper), `funke-inspector-ruleset` (`[ShowInEditor]` field reflection), `funke-build-engine`, `funke-debug`, `funke-code-style`, `funke-comment-style`.

# Game art for Funke games

Art is where agent-made games most often fall flat. Each asset can be fine on its own and the game still looks cheap, because the assets don't agree with each other: three pixel densities, a blurry upscale next to crisp pixels, a palette chosen file by file, the default font on a pixel-art menu, flat grey rectangles as buttons. This skill gets every asset to follow **one** design language, makes the agent show a sample before it produces a whole asset family, and provides tools that keep the rules mechanical.

## 0. Start from the design language

Read `Design/DesignLanguage.md` and `Design/palette.json` in the project. They fix the art style, pixel density, palette tokens, typography, UI shapes and light direction. If they don't exist, run the pre-production step first (`funke-make-a-game` → `references/pre-production.md`): it asks the user, or decides alone when the user said so, and writes both files. Don't invent colours, sizes or fonts per asset. When the design language doesn't cover something, add the decision to the document first and then use it.

## 1. Pick the production approach per asset family

| Approach | Good for | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Text-grid sprites** (`pixelkit.from_grid`) | characters, enemies, items, icons, small props up to ~32 px | Draw each sprite as a text grid with palette letters, in a generator. Every pixel is placed deliberately, it diffs well, and it is easy to recolour and animate frame by frame. |
| **Procedural with rules** (`pixelkit` helpers + PIL) | UI frames and buttons, tiles with structure (bricks, planks, grass edges), gradients, glows, particle sprites, palette swatches | Shapes plus ramps plus bevels, never raw noise. Write the generator once and regenerate whenever the palette changes. |
| **AI image generation** (use the available `imagegen` skill/tool) | painted backgrounds, illustrations, many varied sprites | Write a precise brief (`references/pixel-art.md` → AI briefs). Inspect the output, recover the native grid per element and align it to the project's grid and palette before use. |
| **CC0 asset packs** (Kenney, etc.) | fast prototypes, fonts, sound | Only with the user's OK. Keep `LICENSE.txt` next to the files, then re-palette the pack so it matches the rest. |
| **Built-in shapes** (`Square`, `Circle`, … tinted) | the very first playable greybox | Placeholders only. Replace them before calling the game done. |

When an asset family would take more than an hour, or the user cares about the look, show the plan and **one sample** (one character with a frame or two, one tile, one panel with a button) before generating the rest. It costs one regenerate; rejecting a whole family later costs days.

## 2. Rules that make pixel art look intentional

1. **One density.** Every sprite, tile and UI art pixel uses the same pixel size on screen. A 16 px tile game has 16 px tiles, characters drawn on that grid, icons on that grid, and UI art scaled by a whole number. Never mix a 32 px item into a 16 px world, and never resize pixel art with a smooth filter.
2. **Palette ramps with hue shift.** Each material has a 4–5 step ramp from dark to light. Shadows lean toward blue/violet, highlights toward warm yellow. `pixelkit.ramp("#4C8C4A")` or the ramps in `palette.json`. No colours outside the palette (`pixelkit.py check` lists them).
3. **One light direction** (default: top-left) for every sprite, tile and UI bevel. Raised things are light on the top/left and dark on the bottom/right; recessed things are the reverse.
4. **Hard edges.** Alpha is 0 or 255, without anti-aliased fringes (they turn into blurry halos in game). Dither or use ramp steps instead of soft gradients inside sprites.
5. **Readable silhouettes and outlines.** Characters and pickups get a dark outline (ink token, or a darker ramp step per side for a softer look) so they read against any background. Tiles usually don't get one. Decide once, and write it in the design language.
6. **No pillow shading, no noise.** Shade from the light direction, not from the edges inward. Texture means placed clusters (cracks, planks, blades of grass), not random noise. Random per-pixel noise is the most common sign of generated art.
7. **Signature colours.** Each thing the player must learn (hazard, pickup, checkpoint, enemy type) keeps one colour everywhere: sprite, particles, UI icon.
8. **Animation:** 2–4 frames for idle/bob, 4–8 for walk/run, held keys on impact. Squash and stretch on landing and jumping, a white hit flash, and frames that stay on the grid.
9. **Resizing existing art:** recover its native grid before changing size. Resample or reconstruct individual elements on aligned cells; use whole-number nearest-neighbour upscaling where possible. Do not downscale a finished sheet by an arbitrary non-integer factor. Nearest-neighbour alone does not prove that outlines, symmetry, thin details or the silhouette survived.

Details, frame counts, tile edge rules, the AI brief template and import settings: `references/pixel-art.md`.

## 3. Rules that make UI look like a game, not a debug panel

1. **Every interactive element is a sprite with depth:** an outline, a highlight on top, a lip or shadow at the bottom, with baked **normal** and **pressed** textures (the pressed one without lip, moved down). Flat rounded rectangles with a colour swap look like a prototype.
2. **9-slice everything that stretches.** Panels, buttons and bars use `Image` sliced mode, so the corners stay crisp at any size. Bake all detail into the borders and keep the centre flat or a simple vertical gradient.
3. **One frame family:** panel, well (recessed list or slot), card, button, pill, tooltip, all built by the same generator from the same tokens.
4. **Text:** at most two fonts (title + body). A pixel font only at whole multiples of its design size. Contrast at least 4.5:1 against its fill. Body text on the 1080p reference no smaller than ~26 units on phones. Text needs a higher `sortOrder` than its panel.
5. **Layout:** a spacing grid (8 or 12 units), consistent outer margins, one primary action per screen, touch targets ≥ 96 reference units on phones.
6. **Motion:** panels pop in (scale 0.9 → 1 with a little overshoot, 0.15–0.25 s), buttons press down, numbers count up. A static UI feels dead.

Engine keys (Image `Type`/borders/`BorderScale`, sprite states on buttons), pixel-perfect UI scaling, fonts and HUD recipes: `references/ui-art.md`.

## 4. Into Funke

- **Files:** `Assets/Textures/<Family>/…` (`Characters`, `Environment`, `Items`, `UI`, `VFX`), fonts in `Assets/Fonts/` with their licence. One generator per family in `Tools/` (`Tools/art_characters.py`, `Tools/art_ui.py`), all reading `Design/palette.json`, and one `Tools/build_art.py` that runs them all.
- **Write the `.meta` before the PNG** (`pixelkit.save_texture` does both, atomically and only on change). An open Editor imports a new PNG immediately and gives it a random GUID. If the scene already references your planned GUID, the sprite renders magenta or empty and logs no error.
- **Choose filtering for the target view:** `Point` with whole-number screen scaling and an aligned camera preserves hard pixels. For fractional UI/camera scales, the helper defaults to native art stored 4× nearest-upscaled with `Bilinear`; this reduces filtering softness and the effect of half-texel slice insets, but is not pixel-perfect at arbitrary scales. Inspect both the native art and the actual final-size result. Smooth UI art: `upscale=1`, Bilinear, colour-bled edges.
- **Let `.meta` own the filter:** SpriteRenderer defaults to `filterMode: 4` (Default); explicitly set `Image.filterMode: 4` too when it should follow the import setting, because Image defaults to Bilinear. Non-default component filters call `SetFilter` on the resolved texture and can affect other users sharing its handle.
- **Sheets:** pack frames with `pixelkit.pack_sheet` and save them with `sprites=` (named slices go into the `.meta`, rects scaled with the upscale), or slice with `funke sprite slice <png> --grid 64x64` after writing your own `.meta`. Reference a slice with `spriteName`, and animate with an `Animator` `.anim` clip using discrete `SpriteRenderer.Texture` keys.
- **Size in the world:** `SpriteRenderer.pixelsPerUnit` = art px per tile × upscale (16 px tiles saved 4× → 64) with `Transform2D` scale 1. Every sprite keeps its native pixel size and pivot, so one density holds by construction.
- **9-slice UI:** `"Image": {"imageType": 1, "border": [l, b, r, t], "borderScale": …}` (Tiled = 2 for structured pixel frames). Fonts ship in `Assets/Fonts/` and cover ASCII + Latin-1 only; outlines and drop shadows are Text Renderer keys (`outlineWidth`, `shadowX/Y` + colors), no duplicate label. Details: `references/ui-art.md`.

## 5. Verify

1. `python <skill>/scripts/pixelkit.py check Assets/Textures/Characters/*.png … --project . --scale 4` (pixel art saved 4×) reports colours outside the palette, soft alpha edges and a wrong pixel grid.
2. Open every generated sheet with `view_image`, at native and actual final size plus an integer enlargement. Check thin details, outlines, symmetry, silhouette and transparency; lint cannot judge these.
3. Take an **in-game** screenshot (`funke-make-a-game` → `references/testing.md`) at the target resolution and judge it there. Lighting, ambient light, UI scale and filtering change how art looks. Compare it with `Design/style-sample.png`.
4. Check every screen for: one density, crisp pixels (no blur, no shimmer when moving), text readable on its background, nothing overlapping, no placeholder shapes left.

## Scripts

`scripts/pixelkit.py` — importable library + CLI (needs Pillow):

| Function / command | Use |
|---|---|
| `Palette.load(path)`, `pal["primary"]`, `pal["grass.3"]`, `pal.ramp_of(token)` | palette tokens and ramps (every token gets a derived 5-step ramp) |
| `ramp(hex, n)` / `pixelkit.py ramp "#4C8C4A"` | hue-shifted ramp dark → light |
| `from_grid(text, legend, pal)`, `mirror_x`, `outline(img, colour)` | text-grid sprites |
| `bevel_rect`, `pixel_panel`, `pixel_button(pressed=…)` | pixel-art frames and buttons (9-slice border 3, +lip at the bottom) |
| `rounded_panel(w, h, fill, radius, outline, outline_w, lip, …, gradient)` | smooth UI shapes, 4× supersampled |
| `scale(img, k)` | nearest-neighbour upscale |
| `pack_sheet(frames)` / `pixelkit.py sheet` | sprite sheet + slices for the `.meta`; every slice keeps its own size and gets its edge pixels extruded by 1 art px (no seams between tiles under Bilinear) |
| `save_texture(path, img, project, filter)` / `write_meta` / `pixelkit.py meta` | meta first, then PNG, atomic, keeps existing GUIDs |
| `pixelkit.py sample <project>` | `Design/style-sample.png` for approval |
| `pixelkit.py check <png…> --project P --scale k` | pixel-art lint |
