# Changelog

Release notes describe user-visible compatibility, reliability, and workflow changes. A public tag is accepted only when its exact version has a section here.

## [2026.1.0-beta.1]

First public beta. The editor runs on Windows x64, Linux x64 and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel); each exports games for its own desktop platform, and to Android, iOS and Web through platform packages. See `Github-Docs/Documentation/Known-Limitations.md`.

- **Repository and SDK cleanup:** removed the retired Glad dependency and unused GLSL assets. Editor icon concepts now live under `design/editor-icons/concepts/` instead of the distributed runtime assets, and Android Java sources use the `dev/funke/player` directory matching their package name.
- **Default font:** the Editor, Launcher and built-in game-text default now use IBM Plex Sans Condensed Regular. The default font's asset GUID stays unchanged, and explicit font selections are preserved.

### New

- **Broader Undo/Redo:** scene edit histories survive Play/Stop; shortcuts work across editor panels and detached windows while text fields keep their own editing shortcuts. Component paste/reset, prefab reverts, script removal and scene-system changes now record undo steps. Private play snapshots preserve the exact edit-state baseline, including clean scenes.
- **Hot-reload fallback:** a replacement C# assembly is loaded and its type signatures checked before discarding the working assembly. A damaged DLL or missing referenced type leaves the previous scripts available, with an error in the Console.
- **Bundled desktop .NET:** build profiles now include a private .NET runtime by default. **Include .NET Runtime** can be disabled for smaller exports; the exporter otherwise validates and copies the matching installed runtime with its license notices. Desktop CI creates, exports, relocates and runs a C# game using that runtime, and checks that a damaged bundle cannot fall back to the machine's installation.
- **Optional 2D lighting package:** `Funke.Lighting2D` provides ambient light, colored point lights and rotated rectangular shadow occluders, with Inspector fields, gizmos, serialization and C# access. Screen-space UI stays unaffected. Lighting lives in the external package; the engine adds general scene-effect and fullscreen-pass APIs. The first version supports 32 point lights and 64 occluders with hard shadows; see *Engine Core > Lighting 2D*.
- **Exported-game platform checks:** an opt-in smoke harness runs actual WebAssembly exports, Android APKs or iOS simulator apps, requires C# success messages and checks rendered pixels. Build, import and package progress shows in an in-editor window; "Show in Explorer" becomes **Reveal in Finder** / **Show in File Manager** (with the file selected on desktops that support it). Crashes write a `<app>-<time>.crash.txt` with a backtrace to the crash dump folder. Missing tools are offered through Homebrew on macOS, and distribution-built .NET SDKs (Ubuntu, Fedora) are recognised.
- **Linux and macOS game exports:** the Linux editor exports a Linux folder (executable plus its libraries), the macOS editor a signed-ad-hoc `<Name>.app` with `Info.plist`, `AppIcon.icns` and the content in `Contents/Resources`. From a source checkout the runtime is compiled fresh with `make`, like MSBuild does on Windows. New projects get a `macOS` build profile next to `Windows` and `Linux`, and new profiles default to the editor's own platform.
- **Triggers:** colliders with **Sensor** enabled now raise `OnTriggerEnter2D`, `OnTriggerStay2D` and `OnTriggerExit2D` (previously sensor overlaps were never reported). `Collision2D.IsTrigger` tells the two apart.
- **Streaming audio from any file:** `AudioStream.Open(path)` plays MP3, WAV or FLAC files outside the project (a music folder, downloads) straight from disk, with `Play/Pause/Stop`, seeking via `Time`, `Length`, `IsAtEnd`, `Volume` and `Loop`. Leaving Play mode closes every open stream.
- **Mouse wheel in scroll views:** the wheel now scrolls a list while the cursor is over one of its rows. It used to react only when the scroll view itself was under the cursor, so lists of buttons only scrolled in the gaps between them. A vertical list wins over a horizontal carousel inside it; multiline input fields keep scrolling their own text.
- **Input fields on phones:** tapping outside a focused field (on a button, a list or empty space) now closes the keyboard; the field used to grab focus back the next frame. Holding a finger on the text selects a word and opens Android's Cut / Copy / Paste / Select all toolbar; dragging selects a range. Password fields no longer allow copying their text, also with Ctrl+C on the desktop.
- **Media controls for music apps:** `MediaSession` shows a Spotify-style "now playing" notification on Android (cover, title, artist, previous / play-pause / next, seek bar), with the same controls on the lock screen and for headset buttons. Scripts publish the track with `SetNowPlaying`, the state with `SetPlaybackState`, and read button presses with `TryGetCommand`. Needs `Audio.PlayInBackground` and the Android build option `backgroundAudio`.
- **Decoding images at runtime:** `Texture.DecodeImage(bytes, maxSize, out w, out h)` turns PNG/JPEG/BMP/TGA bytes (e.g. cover art inside an MP3) into RGBA pixels, shrunk to `maxSize`, and is safe on worker threads; `Texture.Create(w, h, pixels)` makes a texture from them.
- **Android UI uses the full screen width:** the safe area no longer subtracts the back-gesture zones at the left and right edge, which squeezed full-width UI by about 150 px on phones with gesture navigation. Only the status bar, navigation bar and camera cutout count.
- **Android games no longer run out of memory on Mali GPUs:** Arm Mali drivers (seen on the Pixel 9a's Mali-G715) cached a render-pass entry per frame under Vulkan dynamic rendering and never freed it, so UI-heavy scenes grew ~100 MB/s until Android killed the game. Android now uses classic Vulkan render passes.
- **Precompiled C# on Android:** Release APKs compile the game's assemblies, `Funke-ScriptCore` and the framework assemblies they use (including `System.Private.CoreLib`) ahead of time with Mono AOT and LLVM, instead of JIT-compiling them on the phone. Compute-heavy scripts run much faster: a 3D fluid simulation on a Pixel 9a went from about 30 to about 53 FPS (simulation step 1.5×, surface meshing 2.2× faster). Anything not precompiled still falls back to the JIT. The game assembly is loaded into the default load context on Android and iOS (there is no hot reload there). The first Release build spends about a minute compiling the framework once; later builds reuse the cache and add a few seconds. Build profile options `aot` (default: on for Release, off for Development) and `aotLlvm`.
- **Background audio:** `Audio.PlayInBackground = true` keeps sounds playing when the game is minimized, unfocused or sent to the background, and keeps scripts updating there (at a low rate, without rendering) so a music player can start the next track. On Android it runs a foreground media service with a "playing" notification; enable the Android build profile option `backgroundAudio` to declare it. Android games no longer freeze their main loop in the background; paused games poll about ten times a second until the OS suspends them.
- **Android runtime permissions:** `Application.RequestPermission` / `GetPermissionState` ask for permissions such as `READ_MEDIA_AUDIO`; the Android build profile's new `permissions` option declares them in the APK.
- **Scrolling lists of buttons on touch screens:** a drag that starts on a button (or any non-dragging widget) inside a Scroll Rect now scrolls the list once it moves a few units, and the button no longer clicks on release. Scroll Rects also scroll the right distance when the UI is scaled (a window smaller or larger than the reference resolution); before, the scroll range and drag speed were off by the UI scale.
- **Custom shaders:** write your own WGSL shaders as `.wgsl` assets for meshes (`Mesh3D`), sprites (`Sprite2D`) and full-screen post effects (`PostProcess`). You write `fn surface(...)` (and optionally `fn vertex(...)`); the engine inserts it into its template with lighting, shadows, tone mapping and sprite masks. A header declares name, target, blend, cull and depth write, and `// @property float speed = 1 range(0, 5)` (also `vec2`–`vec4`, `color`, `texture`) becomes a field in the material's Inspector. Materials get a **Shader** field (`"shader"` and `"properties"` in the `.material`), Sprite Renderers a **Material** slot (sprites batch only with the same material), and Post Processing up to four **Custom Effects** slots that run after the built-in effects. Shaders get `globals.time`, `deltaTime`, the camera matrices and the screen size. Saving a shader reloads it at once; errors go to the Console as `Shader.wgsl(12): error: ...`, the last working version stays active, and a shader that never compiled draws magenta. C#: `Material.SetFloat/SetVector/SetColor/SetTexture`, the matching getters, `HasProperty`, `ShaderUUID` and `SpriteRenderer.Material`. Builds ship the shaders their materials use, and `funke validate` compiles every shader and reports errors with line numbers. UI Images get a **Material** slot too (shaders with `@target UI`, which use the Sprite2D inputs; C#: `Image.Material`, interop layout version 21). A mesh shader's `fn vertex` now also moves the mesh's shadow, and `// @displacement 0.5` (the farthest it moves a vertex) widens the editor's click area and selection box to match. See *Custom Shaders* in the documentation.
- **Saving data:** `PlayerPrefs` (typed key/value settings) and `SaveData` (any object as JSON, per named slot). Both write atomically and save automatically on quit and when Play stops.
- **Multi-touch:** `Input.TouchCount` and `Input.GetTouch(i)` report every finger on a touchscreen with its `Id`, `Position`, `StartPosition` and `Phase` (Began, Moved, Stationary, Ended). The mouse only follows the first finger, so on-screen controls that need two thumbs at once, e.g. a joystick plus a jump button, read touches. A tap shorter than a frame still reports `Began` before `Ended`. UI reacts to every finger as well: Buttons, Toggles and other Interactables can be pressed and clicked by several fingers at once (two on-screen buttons held together); sliders, scrollbars, scroll views, input fields and dropdowns follow the first finger.
- **Post Processing on 3D cameras:** the Post Processing component (bloom, color grading, vignette, custom effects, ...) now works on a Camera 3D as well, also in projects without the 2D module: the 3D image is processed before UI and 2D overlays are drawn on top, which stay unaffected. The Editor View's Post Processing toggle applies to 3D views too.
- **Setting VSync to its current value no longer rebuilds the swap chain:** games that apply their graphics settings on every scene load no longer lose a frame (and screenshots taken in it) each time.
- **3D picking:** `Camera3D.ScreenPointToRay(screenPoint)` returns a `Ray` through a screen point (viewport pixels, origin top left, like `Input.MousePosition` and touch positions; parallel rays for orthographic cameras), and `Camera3D.WorldToScreenPoint` maps a world point back to the screen with its depth. `Physics3D.Raycast(Ray, out hit)` and `Physics3D.RaycastFromScreen(screenPoint, out hit)` pick the collider under the cursor or a finger. Rebuild `Funke-ScriptCore` together with the engine: the interop layout version is now 24.
- **Distance fog for 3D:** a Camera 3D's new **Fog** (color, **Fog Start**, **Fog End**) blends meshes into the fog color between the two distances, so far-away parts of a level fade out instead of ending at a hard edge. Materials have a **Fog** checkbox (`"fog": false`) for things that should stay clear, such as sky domes. Off by default, so existing scenes look the same. Scene keys `fog`, `fogColor`, `fogStart`, `fogEnd`; C#: `Camera3D.FogEnabled`, `FogColor`, `FogStart`, `FogEnd` (rebuild `Funke-ScriptCore` together with the engine: the interop layout version is now 20).
- **Tilt and rotation on phones:** `Input.Acceleration` (in g, pointing toward gravity) and `Input.Gyroscope` (rad/s) read the accelerometer and gyroscope on Android and iOS, with `IsAccelerometerAvailable` / `IsGyroscopeAvailable`. The axes follow the screen as it is currently rotated, so tilt steering works the same in portrait and landscape. The sensors switch on with the first read; no permission is needed. Desktop and Web without such sensors report zero.
- **Gamepads from C#:** `Input.IsGamepadConnected`, `GetGamepadButton/Down/Up`, `GetGamepadAxis`, `GetLeftStick`, `GetRightStick`, `GetGamepadTrigger`, plus `GamepadButton` / `GamepadAxis`. `Input.GetAxis()` falls back to the first gamepad's stick or D-pad.
- **Collision layers:** every collider has **Layer** and **Collides With** checkbox fields (16 layers in the Inspector, 64 from code). Raycasts and overlap queries accept a `layerMask`; `PhysicsLayers.Mask(...)` builds one.
- **Collider settings from C#:** `IsSensor`, `Layer`, `CollisionMask`, `Friction` and `Bounciness` on `BoxCollider2D`, `CircleCollider2D` and `PolygonCollider2D` (shared `Collider2D` base class).
- **Sprite animation:** the **Animator** component plays sprite-sheet slices through discrete **Texture** keys in a looping animation clip. Animator Controllers switch between clips, and scripts control playback through `Animator`.
- **Post-processing from C#:** the `PostProcessing2D` component wrapper reads and changes every effect at runtime (`ColorGrading`, `Vignette`, `ChromaticAberration`, `Grain`, `Bloom`, `LensDistortion`, `Pixelated`, `GaussianBlur`), with the same value ranges as the Inspector. Works with `GetComponent`, `AddComponent` and component script fields.
- **Undo/redo for structural edits:** create, delete, duplicate, paste, cut, reparent, reorder, add/remove component or script, rename, enable/disable, Static and prefab unpack. The selection survives undo/redo.
- **Editor View toolbars:** the gizmo modes float over the Editor View's top-left corner, the view options (3D toggle, draw mode, Gizmos, Post Processing, Grid Snap) over its top-right corner. **Edit › View** (or a right-click on the view options or the gizmo toolbar) lists every element, and each one can be hidden on its own, as can the whole group. The remaining buttons close up without gaps. The choice is saved per user in the editor preferences and has a **Reset to Default**. Hidden actions stay available in the command palette (Ctrl+K), e.g. *Gizmo Mode: Rotate*, *Draw Mode: Triangle*, *Toggle Grid Snap*. The Game View toolbar works the same way: **Edit › View** (or a right-click on the toolbar) hides Aspect Ratio, VSync, Stats, Logs or the whole toolbar, and *Toggle Game View Stats / Logs / VSync / Toolbar* stay in the command palette.
- **Crash recovery:** unsaved scenes are copied to `.funke/Recovery` every 30 seconds and on an unexpected error; the next start offers Restore or Discard.
- **Setup offers missing build tools:** `Setup.bat` / `Setup.sh` now also detect CMake, the MSVC toolset (Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, default *no*) and the Linux C++ toolchain with X11/GL headers, and ask `[Y/n]` before installing them.
- **Custom project templates:** right-click a project in the Launcher → **Save as Template...** stores its `Assets/` structure, project settings, build profiles, native scripts and local packages as a template in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke\Templates`. **New Project** lists it with a **Custom** chip, and projects created from it start with the same folders, assets and Project Settings. The new **Templates** page in the Launcher sidebar shows custom and built-in templates with their preview image; it starts a new project from a template, saves a project as a template (**From Project**), and edits custom templates: name, description, category and source project (**Edit...**), **Open Source Project**, **Update from Source Project...** (re-copies the project's current state) and delete. Templates can also ship their own `project.json`, `BuildProfiles/`, `NativeScripts/Source/` and `Packages/`.
- **Launcher prerequisite check:** missing .NET 10 SDK or MSVC Build Tools are shown with a download button.
- **New app icons:** the Editor, Launcher and Runtime use the new flame icon (the Launcher on a framed tile), with simplified artwork at small sizes so it stays readable in the taskbar. Games without their own **App Icon** get the flame as their default icon and logo.
- Documentation: *Your First Game* walkthrough and *Known Limitations* page.
- **Android, iOS and Web exports as platform packages:** each target is a separate package (`Funke.Platform.Android`, `Funke.Platform.iOS`, `Funke.Platform.Web`) instead of being built into the engine; a platform without its package is simply unavailable in Build Profiles. Android produces a signed APK, iOS an Xcode project or signed `.app` (macOS only), Web a static WebAssembly + WebGPU site. C# scripts run on these targets through the Mono runtime (`Funke.ScriptRuntime.Mono`); C# on the Web needs the .NET 11 SDK with `wasm-tools`. See *Platform Packages* in the documentation.
- **Screen orientation for phones and tablets:** Project Settings > Display > Mobile > Orientation picks landscape (either side, left or right only), portrait (upright, upside down or both) or any combination; Android and iOS builds start in that orientation. Phone and tablet games always run fullscreen without the system bars.
- **UI respects notches and rounded corners on phones:** top-level UI anchors to the safe area, so corner buttons stay clear of the camera cutout. **Ignore Safe Area** on a RectTransform lets backgrounds and overlays reach the screen edges; scripts read the insets from `Application.SafeArea`.
- **UI Scale Mode:** Project Settings > Display > UI Scaling now offers **Fit** (the whole reference resolution stays visible on any aspect ratio, e.g. wide phones or tall windows) and **Fill** (covers the screen) besides **Match Width or Height**. Stored as `uiScaleMode` in `project.json`.
- **Fill Parent for UI rects:** **Fill Parent Width** / **Fill Parent Height** make a RectTransform span its parent rect (the screen's safe area for a root canvas) along that axis instead of using its Size, so a 1920×1080 canvas grows with wide phones, corner-anchored buttons stay in the screen corners, and a bottom toolbar can run the full width. Stored as `fillParent` (both axes), `fillWidth` or `fillHeight` in scenes and prefabs.
- **On-screen keyboard on Android and iOS:** focusing an Input Field opens the system keyboard (number pad for number fields, hidden text for secret fields) and keeps the field visible above it; closing the keyboard ends editing.
- **Build Profiles show platform requirements and options:** for package platforms the panel lists the package, the builder's requirement check with a fix for each missing tool, and editable platform options (signing keystore, orientation, SDK paths, ...). Options are stored as `platformOptions` in the `.build` file; `env:NAME` reads a value such as a password from an environment variable.
- **Files changed outside the editor apply live:** scenes, audio clips, fonts and Data Assets edited by another program (a text or audio editor, `git pull`, an AI agent) now reload while the project is open, like textures already did. A loaded scene with unsaved edits asks **Reload from Disk** / **Keep Editor Version** instead of being overwritten, and auto-save never overwrites an external change. **Preferences › Behavior › External Changes** decides whether unchanged scenes reload without asking.
- **3D foundation:** new built-in components **Transform 3D** (position, Euler rotation, scale; parented through the hierarchy), **Camera 3D** (perspective or orthographic), **Mesh Renderer** (Cube, Sphere, Plane, Cylinder with a color, lit or unlit) and **Directional Light** (color, intensity, ambient). A depth-tested 3D renderer draws them in the runtime and in the editor's Game View; 2D sprites and UI draw on top. C# gets `Transform3D`, `Camera3D`, `MeshRenderer` and `DirectionalLight`.
- **3D materials:** new `.material` asset (Asset Browser → **Create → Material**, edited in the Inspector) with base color, base color texture, metallic, roughness, emissive color/intensity, tiling/offset and a lit/unlit switch. Mesh Renderers reference it in the new **Material** slot; their Color now tints the material. Shading is physically based (GGX) in linear color space with tone mapping. C# gets a `Material` class (`AssetManager.Load<Material>`, `MeshRenderer.Material`).
- **Custom 3D meshes:** `.obj` files are mesh assets; a Mesh Renderer's new **Custom Mesh** slot draws one instead of the primitive (`customMesh` in scenes). Polygons are triangulated, missing normals are generated, edits on disk reload live, and picking/selection use the mesh bounds. **Mesh Collider 3D** collides with the renderer's custom mesh or its own **Custom Mesh**. C# gets a `Mesh` asset class (`AssetManager.Load<Mesh>`, `MeshRenderer.CustomMesh`, `MeshCollider3D.CustomMesh`).
- **3D collider gizmos:** in the 3D Editor View the selected entity's Box, Sphere, Capsule and Mesh Collider 3D are outlined (green, triggers light blue), visible through meshes.
- **Transparent materials:** a material's new **Surface** setting (`"surface": 1`) makes it alpha blended by Base Color alpha × texture alpha × the renderer's Color alpha. Transparent meshes are drawn after opaque ones, back to front per object, without writing depth. Lit transparent surfaces get more opaque at grazing angles (Fresnel), so glass and water mirror the sky when seen from the side. C#: `Material.Surface` / `MaterialSurface`.
- **Meshes built from C#:** `Mesh.Create()` makes an in-memory mesh that `SetData(positions, indices, normals, uvs)` fills or replaces at any time (normals are computed when left out); assign it to `MeshRenderer.CustomMesh`. Updating every frame is cheap: the GPU buffers are rewritten in place. `Clear()` empties it, `Destroy()` frees it, and meshes left over are freed when Play mode ends. Useful for procedural terrain, water surfaces, trails or marching-cubes output.
- **3D lights and shadows:** new **Point Light** and **Spot Light** components (range-limited inverse-square falloff, soft spot cone), any number of directional/point/spot lights per scene (up to *Max Lights* per frame), editor gizmos and **3D Entity** presets for both. The main Directional Light casts soft shadows from meshes with **Cast Shadows** on. C# gets `PointLight` and `SpotLight`.
- **3D particles:** new **Particle System 3D** component (and **3D Entity → Particle System 3D**) emits camera-facing billboards from a sphere, hemisphere, cone or box shape, with life time/speed/size variation, rotation, gravity, drag, bursts, Scale and Color over Lifetime, world or local simulation space, an optional texture (soft round dots without one) and **Alpha** or **Additive** blending. The 3D Editor View shows the emission shape and previews the effect with Play / Restart / Stop. C# gets `ParticleSystem3D` (`Play`, `Stop`, `Emit`, `Clear` and the main settings). See *3D → Particles* in the documentation.
- **3D sky:** Camera 3D has a **Background** setting; new cameras show a procedural gradient sky (top/horizon/ground colors, sun disc towards the main Directional Light) that also lights meshes as ambient (**Sky Ambient**). Cameras from existing scenes keep their solid clear color. Shown in the Editor View, Game View and runtime.
- **3D graphics settings:** Project Settings → Graphics → **3D Rendering** adds Shadow Quality, Shadow Distance, Max Lights, Exposure and Tone Mapping (saved under `graphics` in `project.json`, changeable at runtime through `RenderSettings` in C++ and C#).
- **Texture quality, anisotropic filtering and anti-aliasing:** Project Settings → Graphics → **Runtime Quality** adds **Texture Quality** (Full, Half, Quarter: scene textures skip their top one or two mip levels), **Anisotropic Filtering** (Off, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x, for textures filtered Trilinear or Anisotropic) and **Anti-Aliasing** (Off or FXAA, with Low/Medium/High quality) for 2D and 3D. Point-filtered textures (pixel art) and UI are never changed by the texture settings, and FXAA runs on the scene image only, so UI, text and gizmos stay sharp. Saved under `graphics` in `project.json` (`textureQuality`, `anisotropicFiltering`, `antiAliasing`, `antiAliasingQuality`) and changeable at runtime through `RenderSettings` (C#: `RenderSettings.TextureQuality`, `AnisotropicFiltering`, `AntiAliasing`, `AntiAliasingQuality`, or `SetTextureQuality(...)` etc. for the `GraphicsApplyStatus`); the samplers are rebuilt at the next frame. See *Graphics Settings* in the documentation.
- **MSAA for 3D:** **Anti-Aliasing** has a third value, **MSAA 4x** (`"antiAliasing": "MSAA4x"`, C# `AntiAliasingMode.MSAA4x`). The 3D scene is drawn with four samples per pixel, which smooths the edges of meshes, 3D particles and lines but leaves every texel as it is: Point-filtered textures (pixel art, voxel worlds) stay pixel-exact, where FXAA softens them. Works on desktop, Android and Web, in the runtime and the Game View (the Editor View follows its **Post Processing** toggle). 2D sprites and cut-out (discarded) texels are not smoothed; 2D games keep using FXAA. The 4x target needs about 65 MB of GPU memory at 1920×1080.
- **3D physics (Jolt Physics):** new **Rigidbody 3D** (dynamic, kinematic or static; mass, drag, gravity scale, continuous collision, per-axis freeze, interpolation for smooth movement at high frame rates), **Box Collider 3D**, **Sphere Collider 3D**, **Capsule Collider 3D** and **Mesh Collider 3D** (the Mesh Renderer's mesh or a primitive, concave or convex). Colliders on child entities join their parent's Rigidbody 3D, colliders without one are static, and **Is Trigger** turns a body into a trigger. Physics runs in play mode and in the runtime. C# gets `Rigidbody3D` (velocities, `AddForce`/`AddTorque` with `ForceMode3D`, sleeping), the collider classes, `Physics3D.Raycast` and `Physics3D.Gravity`, and the `OnCollisionEnter3D/Stay3D/Exit3D` and `OnTriggerEnter3D/Stay3D/Exit3D` callbacks. See *Physics 3D* in the documentation.
- **3D Editor View:** a **3D** toggle in the Editor View toolbar switches to a perspective scene camera (right mouse orbits, with WASD/QE to fly; middle mouse pans; wheel zooms; **F** frames the selection), with a ground grid, click selection and a move/rotate/scale gizmo with undo. The Create menu gains a **3D Entity** submenu (Empty, Cube, Sphere, Plane, Cylinder, Camera 3D, Directional Light); in 3D mode **Create (Entity)** and **Camera** create 3D entities.
- **Project templates:** the Launcher's *Create New Project* dialog lets you pick **Empty 2D** or **Empty 3D**; new projects start empty (a camera, plus a directional light in 3D). Templates are folders under `templates/` (a `template.json` plus an `Assets/` tree), so new ones need no engine change.
- **Package versions and dependencies:** package `version`s are SemVer, `dependencies` can carry npm-style ranges (`"MyGame.Grid@^1.2.0"`), and a new `engine` field states which engine versions a release supports. Project generation, the runtime and the Package Manager all check them: dependencies load first and no longer need their own `project.json` entry, and a package whose dependency is missing, out of range or made for another engine is skipped with a clear error instead of crashing. The Package Manager installs missing dependencies along with a package, offers **Update** when the registry has a newer compatible release (with rollback if it fails), refuses to remove a package others still need, and reads multiple releases per registry entry.
- **packages-lock.json:** records the exact package versions and their sources next to `project.json`. Commit it; a fresh clone gets **Restore locked versions** in the Package Manager, which downloads the same releases and checks their SHA-256.
- **Engine modules:** 2D (sprites, 2D cameras/particles/post-processing, Box2D) and 3D (meshes, materials, lights, 3D particles, Jolt) are optional modules a project lists in `project.json` `modules` (`"Funke.2D"`, `"Funke.3D"`). The Package Manager lists them under **Engine Modules** next to the packages (Install/Remove, then Reload Editor; CLI: `funke package add|remove Funke.3D`), and packages declare the modules they need with `modules = { "Funke.2D" }` in `funke-package.lua` (or `"modules"` in a registry release): installing such a package enables them, a module can't be removed while a package needs it, and a package whose module is off isn't loaded or built. The editor then offers only the enabled modules' components, presets and view mode, and disabled modules' systems, renderers and script APIs stay off. Game builds ship a runtime compiled without the unused modules (desktop through a premake runtime variant, Android/iOS/Web through the CMake `MODULES` option), and a build stops when a shipped scene uses a component of a disabled module. Projects without the field keep both modules; the built-in starter is 2D-only. An entity belongs to one world: 2D and 3D components (and either with a Rect Transform 2D) can't be combined — the Add Component menu, `Entity.AddComponent`, entity command buffers and Paste Component refuse the mix, and scenes that already contain one load with a warning and the foreign component inactive instead of crashing. See `Github-Docs/Documentation/Engine-Core/Engine-Modules.md`.
- **`funke` command-line tool:** creates projects (`funke create MyGame`), builds games without the editor (`funke build --release --platform Windows`), runs them (`funke run`), validates every project file the way the engine loads it (`funke validate`), converts scenes/prefabs/Data Assets between JSON and binary (`funke convert`), creates, applies, reverts and unpacks prefab instances (`funke prefab`), slices sprite sheets (`funke sprite slice`) and adds or removes packages (`funke package`). `funke.exe` ships next to the Launcher; `funke setup-path` puts it on your user PATH. See *Command-Line Tool* in the documentation.
- **More external changes apply live:** `project.json` and build profiles edited outside the editor are reloaded instead of being overwritten on the next save, prefab instances in open scenes update when their `.prefab` changes on disk (overrides are kept), and Prefab Mode no longer auto-saves over a prefab that changed on disk (it reloads or asks). A `.meta` file that no longer parses is kept as `.meta.corrupt` and logged before it is replaced.
- **Prefab previews in the Asset Browser:** `.prefab` tiles show a rendered image of the prefab instead of the file icon. It appears once the prefab has loaded and its fonts are baked. Sprites, world text and UI are framed from the front. Meshes are shown at a three-quarter angle if the project has Funke.3D. Prefabs that draw nothing or fail to load keep the icon. A preview updates when the `.prefab` changes on disk, including saves from Prefab edit mode, and when a texture is reloaded.

### Changed

- **Sprite animation cleanup:** removed the `SpriteAnimator2D` component, its scene system and C# API. Use an `Animator` with a looping `.anim` clip and discrete `SpriteRenderer.Texture` keys. Existing scenes and scripts using the removed component need conversion; rebuild the engine and `Funke-ScriptCore` together.

- **Inspector header stays visible:** the entity's icon, name, enabled switch and options stay pinned at the top (with the prefab bar) while the components scroll below. Components are listed in a fixed order, the transform first and scripts last, instead of an arbitrary one that could put a Box Collider above the Transform.
- **Reorder components in the Inspector:** drag a component's header onto another one, or use **Move Up** / **Move Down** in its menu. C# scripts and components are placed individually among the built-in components; the transform stays on top. The order is saved per entity in scenes and prefabs (key `ComponentOrder`, written only once components were reordered, a prefab override on instances), is one undo step and applies to the whole selection. Components added later go to the bottom. Dragging a header into a reference field still assigns the component.
- **Progress window for package changes:** installing and removing packages shows each step in the progress window (workspace generation, then every package's C++ and C# layer), titled "Installing X..." or "Removing X..."; NuGet installs and removals, installs from a git URL and **Create new package** show it too.
- **Lighter Launcher:** the Launcher no longer starts a scene, the scene systems, 16 sleeping job threads, the frame arenas, the shader manager or the scan of the ~380 built-in assets it never uses. Apps that only draw their own UI can do the same with the new `ApplicationConfig` switches `EnableScenes`, `EnableJobSystem` (off: jobs run inline), `EnableFrameArenas` and `RegisterBuiltInAssets`.
- **Setup on macOS and Linux:** `scripts/Setup.sh` finds versioned Pythons (`python3.13` from Homebrew's `python@3.13`) and hands that interpreter to every premake step and build command, so macOS' own Python 3.9 is never used. Without a .NET SDK, Setup installs one into `~/.dotnet` with `dotnet-install.sh`, which needs no administrator rights (the Homebrew cask does), and offers to add it to the shell profile. A vendored premake that can't run (the Intel-only 5.0.0-beta2 build on Apple Silicon: "Bad CPU type in executable") or is older than 5.0.0-beta5 is moved aside and replaced by Homebrew's or a downloaded beta5. Makefiles are generated with premake's `gmake` action (formerly `gmake2`), by Setup and by the editor. Where the Command Line Tools' `make` is blocked ("Permission denied" on managed Macs), Setup offers GNU make (`brew install make`), SDL3 and Dawn build with it, and the editor's package and engine builds use `gmake` when it is installed.
- **Anisotropic filtering is a graphics setting:** textures filtered **Trilinear** now get anisotropic filtering too (default 16x, *Anisotropic Filtering* in Project Settings → Graphics), so they stay sharp on floors and walls seen at a grazing angle. Textures filtered **Anisotropic** follow the same setting instead of a fixed 16x. Set it to Off to get the previous Trilinear look.
- **Index is now called Funke.** Everything that carried the old name was renamed, with no compatibility layer: the C# namespace `Index` is now `Funke` (`using Funke;`, `Funke.UI`, …), C# defines `INDEX_*` are `FUNKE_*` (`FUNKE_BUILD_RELEASE`, `FUNKE_ANDROID`, …), native macros `IDX_*` / `INDEX_*` are `FNK_*` / `FUNKE_*`, the programs are `Funke-Editor`, `Funke-Launcher`, `Funke-Runtime` and `funke.exe` (CLI), the assemblies `Funke-ScriptCore.dll` and `Funke-Engine.dll`, package manifests `funke-package.lua` with ids `Pkg.Funke.*`, engine modules `Funke.2D` / `Funke.3D`, built-in asset paths `funke:` in the `FunkeAssets/` folder, the project cache folder `.funke/`, and user data in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke`. Binary scenes start with `FNKSCNB`; custom shaders must not use names starting with `fnk_`. Projects made with Index need their scripts, `project.json`, package references and binary scenes migrated before they open in Funke. Built-in asset GUIDs are unchanged. The package registry and the launcher's Asset Library moved to `Ben-Scr/Funke-PackageRegistry` and `Ben-Scr/Funke-AssetLibrary`, and the registry's packages are now `Funke.*` (`Funke.AudioMixer`, `Funke.Cryptography`, `Funke.Serialization`, `Funke.Tilemap2D`); projects that list `Index.*` packages need the new names. The 2D physics library Index-Physics is now Funke-Physics and ships in the `Funke.Physics` package (see below).
- **Fast Body 2D physics is now the `Funke.Physics` package.** Fast Body 2D, Fast Box Collider 2D, Fast Circle Collider 2D and `FastPhysics2D` left the engine core; projects that use them install the package (Package Manager or `funke package add Funke.Physics`, it enables `Funke.2D`). Scenes keep their keys (`FastBody2D`, `FastBoxCollider2D`, `FastCircleCollider2D`) and scripts keep their API (`Funke.FastBody2D`, `Funke.Physics.FastPhysics2D`; new: `FastBody2D.BoundaryCheck`). The library underneath (formerly Index-Physics, now Funke-Physics) was reworked: a sorted uniform-grid broadphase, precomputed solver constraints and grid-accelerated queries make a pile of 4 000 boxes step in 0.58 ms instead of 13.9 ms, 20 000 sparse bodies in 0.74 ms instead of 5.5 ms, a raycast among 20 000 bodies take 0.6 µs instead of 274 µs, and creating and destroying 20 000 bodies 0.55 ms instead of 128 ms, with the same contacts and query results. Games that don't install the package no longer ship the library. Rebuild `Funke-ScriptCore` together with the engine: the interop layout version is now 31.
- **Faster scripts, hierarchies and UI text:**
  - **C# component access is faster and no longer allocates.** Reading or writing a component property such as `transform.Position` makes one validity call to the engine instead of two. Component, class, material-property and animator-parameter names are no longer re-encoded into a new buffer on every call.
  - **Unity-style public `Start()`/`Update()` methods** are called through a delegate bound once per script, not through reflection every frame.
  - **`GetComponent<SomeScript>()` and `TryGetComponent` on an entity without that script** no longer copy the list of every live script instance on each call.
  - **Moving one 2D transform** now recomputes only that entity and its children. Before, in scenes with any parent–child hierarchy, every transform in the scene was recomputed.
  - **3D world matrices** are rebuilt only when Position, Rotation or Scale changed. Before, they were recomputed several times per frame.
  - **UI text** no longer forces a GPU submit between text phases, and it reuses its texture bindings across frames.
  - **Text layout** reads glyphs from a direct table, and kerning for ASCII pairs is baked once with the font atlas instead of being looked up in the font file for every character pair.
  - **UI layout runs once per frame in games** instead of two or three times: a pass is skipped when the screen, safe area, UI scale and UI state haven't changed since the last one. The editor still lays out every pass. Draw order and mask clipping are worked out in one walk of the hierarchy instead of once per element, and picking the UI element under the pointer no longer allocates.
  - **3D meshes outside the camera are no longer drawn,** and meshes outside the shadow volume are no longer drawn into the shadow map. Skinned meshes and shaders whose `fn vertex` moves geometry without a `// @displacement` hint always draw. Material lookups happen once per material per frame.
  - **3D physics** no longer rebuilds its list of bodies and colliders from scratch on every step.
  - **Scripts that don't override `OnUpdate`, `OnFixedUpdate` or the `…Stay` collision and trigger callbacks** are no longer called for them every frame.
  - **Post-processing draws far fewer full-screen passes.** Bloom's composite, Color Grading, Lens Distortion, Chromatic Aberration, Vignette and Grain now run as one pass: a typical Bloom + Color Grading + Vignette stack writes the screen once instead of three times, plus two clears. Only Gaussian Blur, Pixelated and custom effects start a new pass. Gaussian Blur blurs at half resolution with at most 33 taps per direction; the blur radius stays the same, so **High** quality with many taps costs a fraction of before.
- **One "Reload the editor?" prompt for every change that needs it:** adding or removing an engine module or packages, switching the rendering API (also through a build profile or an edited `project.json`) and changing the editor font all open the same dialog in the main window, listing what changed, with **Reload Now** and **Later**. After **Later** the status bar shows "Reload pending" with a **Reload Now** button. Undoing the change (e.g. switching the backend back) removes it from the list. The Package Manager no longer shows its own reload banner, and Project Settings no longer has its own restart dialog.
- **Prefab instances in the Inspector:** a component that differs from its source prefab shows the override `*` right after its name in the header (`Box Collider 3D*`) instead of on a separate line below it. A new **Select Prefab** button next to "Prefab Instance" shows the source prefab in the Asset Browser.
- **Add Component popup shows component icons:** every entry has the same icon left of its name as its Inspector header (scripts and C# components show the script icon). Entries that can't be added show the icon dimmed.
- **Release builds ship without the stats and log overlays:** unless `project.json` sets `showRuntimeStats` / `showRuntimeLogs`, both now follow the build profile, on for Development and off for Release. This also covers `funke build --release`, which used to ship both overlays (on phones they covered the game's own buttons). Switching the profile in the Build panel resets them to that default; a switch in Project Settings › Build › Diagnostics overrides it.
- **Repeated script exceptions no longer flood the log:** the same exception from the same callback (same type and throw site, e.g. once per frame in `OnUpdate`) is logged in full three times, then summarized every 5 seconds as `… repeated N more time(s) in the last 5s`. Pending counts are written when Play stops. The first, real report no longer rotates out of `<exe>.log`.
- **`funke validate` checks entity and component references in script fields:** an entity uuid that matches no entity in the file, a `"<uuid>:<Component>"` whose entity lacks that component (prefab instances are checked against their prefab and overrides), a component that doesn't match the field's type, and malformed values are errors; unknown component names are warnings. Display names (`Rect Transform 2D`), serialized keys (`RectTransform2D`) and C# class names (`RectTransform`) are all accepted.
- **Removed the sample textures `FunkeAssets/Textures/Game/` (`Player.png`, `Laser.png`, `Meteor.png`)** from the engine assets. A project that still references them needs its own copy under `Assets/`.
- The "user assembly load context is still alive after unload" message is now a trace line at shutdown. It is a warning only when the previous scripts are still in memory after a hot reload.

- **Scene and prefab files list components in a fixed order:** Sprite Renderer, Camera 2D, Particle System 2D and the 3D components now follow the physics and audio components (Transform 2D stays first). Re-saving an existing scene reorders these keys once; values and loading are unchanged.

- **Funke is now open source under the MIT License.** It can be used, modified and redistributed freely, including in commercial games; the previous custom license with a mandatory visible credit no longer applies.

- **`Application.PersistentDataPath` and `TemporaryCachePath` are per game:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<Company>\<Name>` instead of a folder shared by every Funke game. Data written to the old `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Funke` folder is not moved.
- **Faster C# hot reload:** saving a script now compiles it in-process with Roslyn from your .NET SDK instead of running `dotnet build` (one edited file in a 20-script project: about 20 ms of compile time instead of about 1.9 s). The compiler uses the exact settings `dotnet build` would use. Adding or deleting a `.cs` file costs one extra MSBuild pass (about 1 s), and project file or package changes still run one full `dotnet build`. Set `FUNKE_SCRIPT_COMPILER=dotnet` to always use `dotnet build`.
- **Debug overlays on phones:** Android and iOS builds show the runtime stats and log overlays from the start whenever they are enabled, since there are no F6/F7 keys to open them.
- **Play no longer saves scenes.** Unsaved edits are snapshotted privately and are still unsaved after Stop.
- The collider **Layer Mask** number field is now a **Layer** checkbox dropdown.
- **New projects store scenes and prefabs as JSON** (readable diffs, editable by tools and agents); builds still ship them as binary. Existing projects keep their setting; `funke convert --format json` switches one.
- **Converting the asset format now includes Data Assets:** changing Project Settings › Editor › Asset format (and `funke convert`) also rewrites `.dataasset` files, which previously kept their old encoding.
- **Builds only ship assets the game uses:** unreferenced files from `Assets/` and `FunkeAssets/` (unused fonts, textures, shaders, `.cs` sources, scenes not in the build list) are left out. References are followed from the build scenes through GUIDs, asset paths and scene names, plus path literals and `AssetManager.FindAll` calls in C# scripts. Files only found through computed paths belong in `Assets/StreamingAssets/`, which always ships. See *Building and Shipping › Which assets ship*.
- The Build panel's output directory follows the active profile's platform (`Builds/Android`, `Builds/Web`, ...) as long as its last folder is a platform name; custom folder names are kept.
- **Faster frames in script- and sprite-heavy scenes:** component access from C# no longer scans every component type on each call; spawning or destroying non-Static sprites no longer rebuilds the Static sprite grid; unsliced sprites skip the sprite-sheet lookup; prefabs are read from disk once instead of on every instance or spawn; bloom renders at half resolution with at most 25 blur taps (same glow radius); and the profiler costs almost nothing while its panel is closed.
- New `Entity.TransformRefReadOnly` and `GetNativeComponentReadOnly<T>()`: read a transform without making the engine re-check every transform that frame, as the writable `TransformRef` does. `Funke-ScriptCore.dll` and the engine must be updated together (script interop layout version 5).
- `Window.IsFullScreen`, `Window.Position`, `Window.Title` and `Window.Minimize/Maximize/Restore()` are ignored inside the editor, where they used to resize or move the editor itself; they still apply in the built game.
- **Window, input and gamepads now run on SDL3 instead of GLFW.** Games ship `SDL3.dll` instead of `GLFW.dll` (the Build panel copies it automatically). `KeyCode`, `MouseButton`, `GamepadButton` and `GamepadAxis` keep their values, so scripts and saved bindings are unaffected. Gamepads are hot-plugged and recognized through SDL's controller database, and high-DPI displays (Retina, Windows scaling) report correct sizes.
- `Packages/FunkePackages.props` is the same file on every OS: it picks the package output and `Bin/<platform>-<arch>` folders through MSBuild conditions, so a project committed on Windows builds unchanged on Linux and macOS. Managed packages prebuilt only for Windows are used on the other platforms too.
- `funke setup-path` works on Linux and macOS: it installs an `funke` launcher script in `~/.local/bin`.
- **Platform services are portable:** file and folder dialogs, message boxes, opening files/URLs, "Show in Explorer", system theme and language detection, user folders and dynamic library loading go through one platform layer built on SDL3. The engine code now compiles for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and Web; see *Known Limitations* for which targets can already be exported.

### Fixed

- **`Application.ScreenWidth` / `ScreenHeight` and `Camera2D.ViewportWidth` / `ViewportHeight` in the Game View:** in the editor they returned the size of the whole editor window, while `Input.MousePosition`, touches and the UI use the Game View. Scripts that turn pointer pixels into their own coordinates with them (list and wheel controls, on-screen pedals) hit the wrong place in Play mode, a row or more away from the pointer, and `Camera2D.WorldToScreen` was off as well. They now return the game's screen everywhere: the Game View (or the `funke editor play --size` surface) in the editor, the letterboxed area with a locked aspect, otherwise the window.
- **Static colliders follow their transform:** a collider without a Rigidbody 2D (a static body) stayed where it was created: a prefab with such a collider spawned at a position (`Entity.Instantiate(prefab, position)`), a moved parent, or a script moving it left the physics shape behind at the old place, so things fell through or hit invisible walls. The static body now moves with its transform.
- **Physics bodies in moved prefab instances:** a Rigidbody 2D on a child of a prefab instance whose root was moved in the scene (or by an override) started at the child's position inside the prefab and only jumped to its real place on the first physics step, and scripts read that wrong world position in `OnStart`. Bodies now start at their real place, and the world transform is right from the first frame.
- **Mouse wheel scrolled too far at high frame rates:** the glide a wheel notch starts in a Scroll Rect with **Inertia** was computed from the length of the frame, so at 144 or 300 fps one notch flung the list several times farther than at 60 fps. The glide is now the same at every frame rate (the 60 fps distance, as before). With the default Deceleration Rate (0.135), one notch moves the content about 18.6 px per unit of **Scroll Sensitivity**, glide included.
- **Renaming in the Inspector:** a name typed into the Inspector was only kept when Enter was pressed; clicking elsewhere dropped it. The name now changes as you type (the Hierarchy follows), the edit is one undo step, and Esc restores the old name. With several entities of different names selected, leaving the empty field empty keeps their names.
- **Script fields edited during Play stayed after Stop:** values changed in the Inspector while playing were written back into the scene when play ended, unlike every other play-time change. Stop now restores the values from before Play.
- **Camera 3D gizmo:** the camera was drawn as a fixed 1-unit pyramid (an orthographic camera at a quarter of its size) at a 16:9 aspect, with a lone line sticking up. A selected Camera 3D now shows its real view volume from Near Clip to Far Clip at the Game View's aspect; other cameras show a short piece of it with a triangle marking their up side.
- **macOS: ImGui's WebGPU backend didn't compile** ("unknown type name 'NSString'"): `imgui_impl_wgpu.cpp` uses Cocoa there and is now compiled as Objective-C++.
- **Newer premake releases rejected the build scripts:** `flags { "MultiProcessorCompile" }` and `flags { "NoPCH" }` were removed after premake 5.0.0-beta5; the scripts use the new `multiprocessorcompile` / `enablepch` fields where premake has them.
- **Native packages on Linux and macOS couldn't find Dawn** ("library 'webgpu_dawn' not found"): their link paths only covered the Debug/Release folders of the Visual Studio build, not the single-config folder Make and Ninja build into.
- **Linux and macOS game builds and `PackagePosix.py` looked for `libIndex-Engine`:** builds staged from the editor ("Required libIndex-Engine.dylib not found"), the package ABI stamp and the release packer still used the engine library's old name; they use `libFunke-Engine` now.
- **`vendor_patches.py` on Python 3.9:** it used `zip(..., strict=True)` from Python 3.10 and failed with "zip() takes no keyword arguments" when premake ran it with macOS' own Python.
- **`Entity.SetParent` on 3D entities:** with `worldPositionStays` (the default) only Transform 2D entities kept their place; a Transform 3D entity kept its local Position, Rotation and Scale instead, so a part detached to the scene root jumped to the world origin and one moved to another parent was shifted, turned and scaled by it. Transform 3D entities now keep their world position, rotation and scale too, also right after a script moved them or a parent in the same frame. Under a rotated child of a non-uniformly scaled parent the pose can't always be matched exactly, since Transform 3D has no shear; under a parent scaled to 0 the local transform is kept.
- **Scripts on freshly spawned prefabs:** after `Entity.Instantiate(prefab)`, `GetComponent<MyScript>()` returned null in that frame and the next; only built-in components were there at once, so spawners had to wait two frames before they could configure what they spawned. The spawned entity and its children now have their script instances when `Instantiate` returns: the prefab's field values are set, `OnAwake` and `OnEnable` have run (after the clone is placed and parented, so `OnAwake` sees the spawn position), and `OnStart` follows before the first `OnUpdate`, as in Unity. Fields that point at another script of the same prefab resolve too. Disabled entities still wake when they are enabled.
- **List fields of entity and component references in prefabs:** a `List<Entity>`, `List<Image>` or array (also inline objects with entity fields) pointing at the prefab's own children kept the template's ids, so every instance read wrong or empty entities; only single `Entity` and component fields were retargeted. List elements now point at each instance's own children, for prefab instances as for duplicated and pasted entities. Hand-written files need `"type": "list"` with the `"itemType"` (`entity` or `component:<Name>`) the editor writes.
- **Tris and Verts in 3D scenes:** the stats overlay (**F6** in the runtime, **Stats** in the Game View) counted only 2D sprites, so 3D scenes showed 0 triangles and 0 vertices, and the Profiler's **Triangles** and **Vertices** rows never got a value. Both now count Mesh Renderers (primitives, models and runtime meshes), Skinned Mesh Renderers, every instance of an instanced draw, 3D particles, 2D sprites and 2D particles. Triangles the shadow map draws again appear separately as **Shadow tris**, so **Tris** matches what the cameras show. The Game View counts only its own render, not the Editor View. Counting costs a few additions per draw call. See *Test Builds and Debug Tools › Stats overlay*.
- **2D layer over 3D in the editor:** in scenes with a Camera 3D and a Camera 2D, the Game View, `funke editor screenshot` and the project preview drew sprites, 2D particles, world text and gizmos through the Camera 3D's perspective on its z = 0 plane, so they came out larger, further out or cut off compared to the built game. They now go through the Camera 2D's own projection, as in builds.
- **UI made garbage every frame:** the C# UI event dispatch built a managed wrapper for every Interactable in the scene each frame, including idle and hidden ones (about 260 bytes each), so a game UI with a few hundred buttons and slots produced 50–150 KB of garbage per frame and frequent garbage collections. Widgets with nothing to report are now skipped, and the dispatch allocates nothing; events fire exactly as before.
- **Builds into folders from before the rename:** `funke build` and **Build** refused an existing output folder with "not owned by Funke" when it still carried the `.index-build-output` marker of an Index-era build. That marker counts as Funke's own again; the next build replaces it with `.funke-build-output`.
- **Sliced images in small windows:** the borders of a **Sliced** or **Tiled** Image were drawn in screen pixels, so at a small UI scale (a 480 px window with a 1080 px reference) rounded panels, pills and badges looked about 2.5 times rounder and thicker than designed. Borders now scale with the UI scale and the rect's scale like positions and sizes.
- **Script fields set right after enabling an entity:** an entity that started disabled got its script instances only on the next script pass, so `GetComponent<MyScript>()` right after `IsEnabled = true` returned nothing, and the scene's field values arrived later and replaced values set meanwhile. Enabling an entity during play now creates its scripts at once (scene values, `OnAwake`, `OnEnable`), and values set after that stay.
- **Enabling children before their parent:** `IsEnabled = true` on a child that was switched off in the editor did nothing while its parent was still off, so a panel shown with "children first, then the panel" stayed partly empty. The child now remembers that it is enabled and turns on with its parent, like Unity's `activeSelf`.
- **Switching an entity off in its own `OnEnable`:** `OnEnable` ran while the entity was still marked disabled, so `IsEnabled` and `IsEnabledInHierarchy` read `false` there and `Entity.IsEnabled = false` was ignored; the entity stayed on. `OnEnable`/`OnDisable` now run after the hierarchy has switched, so both read `true` in `OnEnable` and switching off there takes effect (with `OnDisable`). In native code, `Scene::OnEntityEnabledChanged` reports the same edges.
- **Triangle and Mixed draw modes in the 3D Editor View:** both modes only affected 2D sprites, so 3D meshes stayed shaded. **Triangle** now draws every Mesh Renderer and Skinned Mesh Renderer (built-in primitives, `.obj`/glTF models and runtime meshes) as black triangle edges over the sky, including edges hidden behind other meshes; **Mixed** draws the shaded scene with the visible triangle edges on top. Particles are hidden in Triangle mode, and meshes with a custom shader show their undisplaced triangles.
- **3D selection box missed the model:** in the 3D Editor View the selection box only covered the selected entity's own mesh, so a character root whose model sits on a child showed a small cube at its feet, and **F** zoomed onto that cube. The box now surrounds every mesh the entity and its enabled children draw, and **F** frames all of it. Skinned Mesh Renderers used their rest-pose (often T-pose) bounds for the box and for click picking even when the clip's pose looked different; they now follow the pose the model is drawn in.
- **Project packages linked against the wrong engine build:** a project's native package was linked against the first `Funke-Engine.lib` found under the engine's `bin/` (usually the Debug one), so a Release package could miss newer engine functions or fail with unresolved symbols. Each configuration now links its own engine build first. Project package builds also stalled on the PDB server (`mspdbsrv`) on some machines; they now embed debug info in the object files like the engine (`/Z7`).
- **`funke help`** showed `usage: index` instead of `usage: funke`.
- **Web builds with C# scripts didn't start:** the browser refused the game with "module uses a mix of legacy and new exception handling instructions", because the .NET 11 runtime uses the new WebAssembly exception encoding and the engine was compiled with the old one. C# Web builds now compile the engine the same way; Web builds without scripts are unchanged.
- **Default editor layout:** **Layout › Default** (also **Reset Layout** in the command palette and **Reset to Default** under Editor Preferences › Layouts) left every panel floating and shrunk, because it looked for a bundled `imgui.ini` that no longer ships and could pick up an unrelated one from the working directory. The editor now builds the default layout itself: Entities on the left, Inspector on the right, Editor View and Game View in the middle, Project and Log below. It is also applied on startup when the saved layout docks none of these panels, which repairs layouts saved before the rename to Funke and presets from that time.
- **Audio mixer fades too fast (`Funke.AudioMixer` 1.1.1):** `FadeVolume` and `TransitionTo` finished in half the requested time, and in a quarter with an additive scene loaded, because the fade advanced on every coroutine pump instead of once per frame. Fades now take exactly the given seconds.
- **Slow sprite texture swaps from scripts:** assigning `SpriteRenderer.Texture` (or anything else that resolves a texture by GUID) re-read and re-parsed the texture's `.meta` every time, even when the texture was already loaded; for sprite sheets with thousands of slices that cost milliseconds per call, so games setting many tiles froze. Resolved textures are now cached per GUID and sampler. The setter also no longer rebuilds the texture's GPU sampler on every call when the renderer's **Filter Mode** is Default.
- **Mirrored sprites disappearing:** a sprite with a negative scale and no (or an axis-aligned) rotation got an inverted culling box and was never drawn. Its bounds are now computed from the absolute scale.
- **`funke validate` and sound clips:** an AudioSource's `clipAsset` pointing at a `.wav`, `.mp3` or `.flac` was reported as "is not a .anim file", so every scene with music failed validation and the engine load test was skipped. `clipAsset` now accepts an animation clip (Animator) or an audio file (AudioSource).
- **Project packages when `funke` runs inside the project:** with the project folder as working directory, `funke build` and `funke package list` treated `Packages/` as engine packages, so `funke build` skipped compiling them and the game's scripts failed with missing types. They are project packages again.
- **Sprite-sheet slices in the Animator and the Inspector:** the **Texture** of a Sprite Renderer or Image now keeps its slice wherever the value is read back. Recording in the Animation window turns a pick of another slice of the same sheet into a key (it used to see no change), keys from Record and **Add Property** store the slice as `"<guid>|slice|<name>"` (they used to store only the GUID, so playback showed the whole sheet), and previewing a clip no longer resets the sprite to the whole sheet. Picking another slice in the Inspector can be undone (it used to leave no undo step), the Texture field shows `Sheet > Slice`, and a multi-selection with different slices shows as mixed. The documented `"property": "SpriteName"` track never existed: use `Texture` (see *Animation*). Playing a discrete track no longer reapplies an unchanged key every frame, which reloaded the texture's `.meta` each frame.
- **Game builds with both Visual Studio 2022 and 2026 installed:** exporting a 2D-only or 3D-only project (`funke build` or **Build**) failed with `C2375 '__builtin_assume_aligned'` because the runtime was compiled with Visual Studio 2026's MSBuild against precompiled headers made with Visual Studio 2022's copy of the MSVC headers. The runtime is now compiled with Visual Studio 2022 when it is installed, otherwise with Visual Studio 2026 (MSVC v143). `FUNKE_MSBUILD` selects a specific `MSBuild.exe`.
- **Hidden cursor stays in the middle:** with `CursorMode.Locked` the invisible cursor still moved with the mouse, so a click could press a UI button somewhere off to the side and the cursor reappeared at a random spot when unlocked. `Cursor.Visible = false` hid it but let it roam freely. A locked or hidden cursor now stays at the center of the game view: mouse motion only feeds `Input.GetMouseDelta()`, UI under the crosshair gets hover and clicks, and unlocking shows the cursor in the middle. In the Editor the pointer is held on the Game View's center, so clicks while playing can't reach other panels (it still drifted over the editor whenever a key or button changed in the same frame).
- **Cursor lock in the Editor works like Unity's:** the game holds the mouse only while it plays in the focused Game View, which Play now focuses. **Escape** or switching to another app hands the editor its normal, visible OS cursor (no custom game cursor, no mouse-look while you move to other panels). `Cursor.Mode` and `Cursor.Visible` keep reading what the game set, so scripts that re-apply their cursor state every frame no longer take the mouse straight back. Clicking into the Game View, focusing it, or a new lock from the game (e.g. closing its pause menu) applies the game's cursor settings again. Stopping play mode always releases the mouse.
- **Camera fog on custom mesh shaders:** meshes drawn with a `Mesh3D` custom shader ignored the Camera 3D's fog and stood out sharply against a foggy horizon. They now fade into the fog color like standard materials; a material's **Fog** switch (`"fog": false`) still opts out, e.g. for a sky dome or clouds that fade themselves.
- **Mismatched engine DLL is reported instead of crashing:** the Editor, Launcher, Runtime and `funke` tool check at startup that `Funke-Engine.dll` was built from the same engine headers as themselves and log a readable error naming both builds when it was not. When a started program dies before it runs (a missing DLL, or a stale `Funke-Engine.dll` lacking a function it needs), the Launcher, **Build & Run** and `funke run` / `funke open` / `funke build --run` now say so instead of failing silently.
- **Prefabs written as a flat `"Entities"` list open in the editor:** a `.prefab` holding only `{"type":"Prefab","Entities":[…]}` (the layout AI agents and hand-written JSON use) instantiated fine in scenes, but selecting it showed an empty Inspector, double-clicking did not open Prefab edit mode, and the log got a "No Entity/prefab block" warning every frame. The Inspector and Prefab edit mode now read every layout the engine accepts, and a prefab that really can't be loaded is reported once until the file changes.
- **Slider thumbs can be grabbed:** pressing the part of a slider's handle that sticks out of the track (e.g. a round thumb taller than the bar, or past its end) did nothing, and a handle without its own Interactable only reacted where it covered the track, so the pointer had to stay on the fill. The handle now always grabs the slider and drags it from where it was picked up instead of jumping the value.
- **`ParticleSystem3D.Emit` right after moving the emitter:** the burst used the position from the last frame's particle update, so a script that moved the emitter and called `Emit` in the same frame spawned the particles at the old spot. It now uses the emitter's current position, including its parents.
- **Inspector values of C# struct components are kept:** fields of an `IComponent` struct edited in the Inspector only went into an unused list and never reached the component, so the game started with the struct's defaults. The Inspector now reads and writes the component's own bytes (in edit and Play mode), and the scene saves them.
- **Removing an engine module no longer crashes the editor on reload:** after **Reload Editor** with a module removed (e.g. Funke.3D from a 3D project, or both modules for a UI-only project) the editor died without a crash dump. Scripting kept component lookups from the destroyed component registry, because the rebuilt registry could repeat its change counter; every registry now counts in a range of its own.
- **Leaving Play mode is faster:** Stop no longer round-trips each Play scene through a validation load and a baseline reload before discarding it, and the restored edit scene skips a redundant validation load. On a 3D level (≈200 entities) Stop went from about 300 ms to about 135 ms. The log reports each stop as `[PlayMode] Stopped in … ms`.
- **Stopping Play no longer runs scripts in the edit scene:** the frame that stopped Play still updated the restored edit scene, so its scripts' `OnStart` ran in edit mode. Anything spawned there (e.g. a fluid simulation's 4000 particles) landed in the scene and was saved, piling up with every Play/Stop and making Stop take seconds. Stop also no longer serializes the Play scene as a fallback before discarding it, which cost about 1 s with thousands of runtime-spawned entities; a 6000-particle 3D scene now stops in about 60 ms.
- **Focus (F) in the 3D Editor View** now also works when the Entities or Inspector panel has focus; it used to react only while the cursor was over the Editor View.
- **JetBrains IDEs as script editor:** IntelliJ IDEA can now be picked as the external script editor (it opens the project folder and jumps to the line; it has no C# code completion, Rider does). Rider and IntelliJ are found in every install location: versioned `Program Files\JetBrains\…` folders, JetBrains Toolbox 2.x (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`), Toolbox 1.x (`apps\…\ch-0\<build>`) and the installer's registry entries; each version is listed with its number. Rider was previously only found in an old Toolbox layout and an unversioned folder that real installs don't use.
- **Sprites and UI can be selected in the 3D Editor View:** entities with Transform2D or a RectTransform were not clickable in 3D mode. They are now picked on the z = 0 plane they are drawn on (ahead of the meshes behind them), get a selection outline, and **F** frames them.
- **Clicking through stacked objects in the 3D Editor View:** clicking the same spot again selects the next entity behind the current one, as in 2D, instead of always the nearest.
- Component icons in the Inspector show their own colours instead of a blue tint.
- **New component icons:** Audio Source (music note), Particle System 2D/3D, C# scripts and components, Point Light, Spot Light, every 2D and 3D collider shape, and Rigidbody 2D/3D have their own icons in the Inspector; the Hierarchy uses them for lights, particles and audio. Generated by `scripts/assets/generate_component_icons.py`. Fast Body 2D now uses the Rigidbody 2D icon. Package components can pick an icon with the new `icon` argument of `Package::RegisterSerializableComponent` / `RegisterComponent` or `Package::SetComponentIcon<T>()`.
- **Game View aspect "Project (…)":** the aspect dropdown has an entry that follows the project's build Aspect Ratio, so the Game View shows the shipped framing.
- The editor crashed when leaving Play mode in 3D projects (e.g. clicking **Stop**): the rest of that frame still drew the Game View from the play scene that had just been destroyed. Stopping now takes effect at the start of the next frame; double-clicking a scene during Play and Exit-Play-on-Recompile go the same way.
- Blurry taskbar icon on Windows with display scaling above 100 %: the Editor, Launcher and games without their own **App Icon** showed the 32 px icon scaled up. The window now gets the embedded icon at the exact size for the monitor's DPI.
- Native project packages stopped loading after the engine was rebuilt ("package was built against a different Funke-Engine binary"), and tilemaps and other package components vanished until someone rebuilt the package by hand. Opening a project in the editor now rebuilds every source package under `Packages/` that has no build for the running engine (never built, or built against another `Funke-Engine.dll`) before packages load. The editor window appears once the build is done; a failed build is logged and the package stays unloaded.
- Smoother motion with VSync: the frame delta time is now snapped to the display's refresh interval instead of the jittery measured gap between frames (±25 % at 144 Hz), which made everything that moves judder. Game time still follows real time.
- 3D physics: balls and other dynamic bodies no longer hop when they roll across the edge between two triangles of a mesh collider (Jolt's enhanced internal edge removal is on for dynamic bodies).
- Game builds ship the engine's current built-in assets (`FunkeAssets`): the copy a project receives when it is created now only overrides files that were changed in the project. Before, a build shipped that snapshot unchanged, so older projects kept outdated built-ins such as the previous engine icon on the splash screen.
- Restarting the current scene from a script (`SceneManager.LoadScene` on the active scene, e.g. a "Restart" button) no longer floods the log with "… is no longer attached to a live entity": unloading the old copy invalidated the C# component references the freshly loaded copy had just picked up.
- C#: `RectTransform.Entity` returned nothing for UI entities, because it required a `Transform2D` that UI entities never have.

- **The `funke` CLI no longer deletes components when it rewrites a scene or prefab** (`prefab create/apply/revert/unpack`): 3D components (Transform 3D, Camera 3D, Mesh Renderer, lights, 3D physics), UI widgets and layout groups, Sprite Animator 2D, Post Processing 2D and other registry-serialized components were silently dropped because they were only saved while the editor or a game was running.
- The Launcher's **Open** and **Run** buttons work on the first click: on a project that wasn't selected yet, the buttons disappeared while the mouse button was held, so the click only selected the project.
- The Launcher's project preview now shows 3D scenes: it renders through the scene's Camera 3D like the Game View (before, 3D projects got only the 2D layer or no preview at all).
- The Launcher's project preview keeps the game's aspect ratio (the build's locked aspect, otherwise the Game View's). Portrait games used to be captured at 16:9 and looked stretched; their preview now shows the whole frame with black side bars. Existing previews update the next time the project is opened in the editor.
- The Editor View's **3D** toggle is remembered per project (`editorView3D` in `project.json`) instead of resetting to the project's default on every start.
- **Stopping Play froze the editor for seconds** in scenes with many prefab instances or scripted entities (about 2 s at 3,000 entities): reloading the edit scene wrote a log line for every prefab override and every script field. Loading scenes, in the editor and in built games, is faster for the same reason.
- Android: games no longer stay black on GPUs that reject the opaque surface mode (e.g. Mali), recover their picture after returning from the background or after the screen was locked (unlocking left the screen black), and stop their music as soon as they go to the background (it kept playing on the home screen until the app was reopened). Saves go to the app's own storage, and `OnApplicationPaused` also saves `PlayerPrefs`, since the system may end a backgrounded app without a quit.
- `Input.GetKeyDown`/`GetKeyUp` and `GetMouseDown`/`GetMouseUp` no longer miss a press and release that arrive within one frame. Backspace on Android's on-screen keyboard now deletes text, and very short taps now press buttons.
- `UIPointer.HoveredEntity` reports what is under the pointer now instead of what was under it last frame. On touch screens the finger jumps to where it lands, so a tap on a button looked like a tap on the game world (e.g. it deselected objects in a level editor).
- Input Field caret and selection are drawn at the field's sorting order (they were hidden behind panels with a higher order, e.g. a field in a popup), and the caret is at least one logical pixel wide so it is visible on high-density phone screens.
- **App icon:** icons larger than 256×256 (the usual 512/1024 px PNGs) were not embedded in Windows builds, so the game kept the Funke icon. The `.exe` now carries every size from 16 to 256 px, built from any PNG, JPG, BMP or ICO. Icons outside `Assets/` or in `.ico` format now also reach the running game. Platform packages always get a PNG (previously only files ending exactly in `.png`) and the app id `com.<company>.<name>`. On Linux every Funke game used to share the app id `dev.funke.engine`.
- **Custom cursors:** cursors stay the right size at 125–400 % display scaling (they used to shrink on Windows), keep their aspect ratio instead of being stretched to a square, and have a configurable **Hotspot** (Project Settings › Branding › Cursors, or `Cursor.SetTexture(texture, hotspot)` in C#); previously the click point was always the top-left pixel. On Android and iOS cursor settings are ignored without a warning.
- The editor crashed while closing when the project used the Vulkan render backend.
- **Sliders** take presses on both the handle and the track: grabbing the handle drags it from where it was grabbed, and clicking the bare track jumps the value to the pointer. Previously a handle with its own Interactable disabled the track, and without one only the track rect reacted, so most of a large handle was dead.
- `Cursor.Visible = false` now hides the cursor over the Game View during Play in the editor; the editor UI used to show it again every frame unless the project had a custom cursor image.
- An exception during a frame used to close the editor without warning; it now keeps unsaved scenes for recovery and explains what happened.
- A last-opened scene that cannot be read no longer leaves the editor with no scene; an empty unsaved scene opens and the file is left untouched.
- Exceptions in UI event handlers, coroutines and several other script entry points no longer terminate the process; they are logged to the Console.
- Errors from `OnApplicationQuit`, `OnApplicationPaused` and `OnFocusChanged` handlers now appear in the Console instead of being lost.
- Crash dumps are also written for `std::terminate`, `abort()`, pure virtual calls and invalid CRT parameters.
- A game started without the .NET 10 Runtime shows a message with a download link.
- `Gizmo.DrawLine(start, direction, distance)` no longer throws `NotImplementedException`.
- Prefab instances spawned after a scene change no longer render solid white: the fast-spawn prefab cache kept texture handles that the scene unload had already freed.
- Textures that were being written while the editor read them (or whose `.meta` was mid-write) no longer stay white: the editor retries them on the next file change and also watches `.meta` files.
- **VSync off is no longer capped at the monitor refresh rate on Direct3D 12.** Presents now allow tearing, so `Application.VsyncEnabled = false` runs up to `Application.TargetFrameRate` in windowed and fullscreen mode. The frame cap is also more accurate (240 instead of ~233). The chosen present mode is logged.
- Release reliability, packaging, and data-safety fixes.
